We can catch them with their pants down."
"Daoist Qianji..." Wang Ya mused, stroking his beard.
"I have heard of him.
He committed heinous crimes in the Central Continent.
He is a master of concealment and puppetry—extremely troublesome.
When Hu Yanqing of the Guiyuan Sect claimed he was here to capture a fugitive, I thought it was a mere pretext.
It seems he wasn't lying."
Xia Xuanyin nodded decisively.
"I have already sent a distress signal to the Central Continent.
Reinforcements from the Heavenly Abyss Alliance are en route.
They should arrive within days.
The moment they touch down, we will mobilize our forces and strike the Demon Nest directly."
His gaze swept over the room, sharp as a blade.
"Until then, this information must be kept absolutely confidential.
We cannot afford to beat the grass and startle the snake."
Everyone nodded solemnly.
"Head Seat Wang Ya," Zhang Xian said, shifting the topic.
"One more favor.
Yun Wanqing and the others will arrive shortly.
I fear they will panic if they cannot reach me upon landing.
Could you intercept them and let them know I’ve arrived safely in the Southern Capital?"
"Rest assured, consider it done." Wang Ya agreed solemnly.
He stood up, his robes snapping.
"There is no time to lose.
I will depart immediately.
By the time I reach the coordinates, their transfer should be complete."
Wang Ya hurried out.
Xia Xuanyin also stood, walking over to loom over Zhang Xian.
His gaze was profound, filled with complex emotions.
"Zhang Xian.
The intelligence you brought back is worth a kingdom.
On behalf of the hundreds of millions of lives in the Southern Region...
I thank you."
The Emperor paused, his tone shifting to carry a subtle, heavy warning.
"To fight monsters, one must sometimes use monstrous methods.
I understand this.
However, demonic techniques are insidious, and their consequences are endless.
You must guard your original heart.
Do not let the abyss stare back."
Zhang Xian’s heart tightened.
The Emperor knew.
He met Xia Xuanyin’s gaze without flinching.
"Your Majesty need not worry.
I know my limits."
Xia Xuanyin looked at him deeply for a moment longer, said nothing, and turned to leave.
The heavy door clicked shut, leaving only Zhang Xian and Lin Yinyin in the room.
The tension instantly evaporated.
Lin Yinyin scooted closer, her small face a mixture of lingering fear and heartache.
"You lecherous Big Brother," she sniffed, wiping her eyes.
"You really are considerate toward Sect Master Yun.
Willing to risk your life just to keep her safe?"
Zhang Xian smirked.
"What?
Jealous?"
"No!" Lin Yinyin denied it, though her face was full of grievance.
She held out the fragments of the white jade in her palm.
"I just feel bad for the [United Heart Winged Pendant].
My only chance to save you... gone just like that."
Seeing her pitiful expression, Zhang Xian couldn't help but laugh.
With a sleight of hand, he pulled another pair of identical pendants from his storage ring and dangled them before her.
"Here.
Stop crying.
I have fresh ones."
Lin Yinyin stared at the brand-new jade pendants, her eyes popping wide.
"Ah?
How do you have more?" She looked up, glaring at him with sudden realization.
"Brother!
Are these... mass-produced?"
"Well..."
"Ah!
So Yun Wanqing and Master probably have them too, right?" She jumped up, hands on her hips, her sadness replaced by indignation.
"Wow!
And here I was, weeping like a fool!
You big liar!
You scumbag!"
Exposed, Zhang Xian raised his hands in surrender.
"Hey, hey!
Yinyin, listen!
Didn't I think of you first?
As soon as danger struck, I teleported to your room, didn't I?"
"Pah!" Lin Yinyin’s face flushed red.
"I know you!
You just didn't want Master and the others to know you have a stockpile of these things!
You're afraid they'll know your true colors—a two-timing rogue!
You just think I'm easy to bully!"
She pounced, her small hands going for a pinch.
"Ah!
Yinyin, have mercy!"
Meanwhile, halfway across the region.
Yun Wanqing stood trembling, her hand hovering over her own [United Heart Winged Pendant], ready to crush it and warp into the unknown.
"Wait!"
A voice broke the sound barrier as Wang Ya descended from the sky.
"Zhang Xian is alive, Sect Master Yun.
There is no need to worry."
Yun Wanqing spun around violently.
"Really?"
Wang Ya looked at her—tears brimming in her eyes, her face a mask of panic and terror.
He let out a silent sigh.
"He arrived in the Southern Capital a step ahead of us," Wang Ya said, keeping his voice steady.
"He sustained some minor injuries and is recuperating, but he is safe.
We can discuss the details later.
For now, board the flying vessel."
Only then did the invisible wire pulling at Yun Wanqing’s heart finally snap, leaving her weak with relief.

chapters.title: Chapter 159 I Must Meet This Godfather
paragraphs: Ten days later, above the Southern Capital.

An ancient flying vessel pierced the cloud layer, drifting slowly toward the city. At the bow stood a young man in dark martial robes. He possessed sharp features, eyes bright as starlight, and stood with his hands clasped behind his back—Xia Chengyan, the Crown Prince.
He spread his arms wide, embracing the magnificent sprawl of the capital below.
"Southern Region!" he bellowed, his voice clear and resonant. "I, Xia Chengyan, have returned!"

Beside him stood a young woman in simple, elegant cyan robes, her hair tied in a high, practical ponytail. This was Grandmaster Lin Xiaozhu of the Divination Sect. Watching Xia Chengyan’s exaggerated display of "returning home in glory," she couldn't help but roll her eyes.
Xia Chengyan grinned shamelessly and extended a hand toward her. "Come on, come on, Miss Xiaozhu. Let’s fly down hand-in-hand. We need to make a dashing entrance!"
Lin Xiaozhu swatted his hand away with a look of disdain. "Absolutely not. It’s humiliating."
"Tsk. You have no romantic bone in your body," Xia Chengyan clicked his tongue but didn't press the issue.
He straightened his attire, deliberately draping a gaudy, dark red robe trimmed with gold over his shoulders—the height of flamboyance. He took a deep breath, stepped onto the railing, and leaped.
"OLD—MAN—! I'M—HERE—!"
A shout that pierced the heavens accompanied his descent. He fell like a meteor, smashing violently into the vast plaza before the Imperial Palace.
Boom!
Dust billowed into the sky as a massive crater formed in the stone. The Royal Guards, startled by the sudden bombardment, drew their blades in panic.
As the dust settled, Xia Chengyan revealed himself, standing tall and brushing non-existent dirt from his shoulders. He wore an expression that screamed, I am the most dashing man alive.
Lin Xiaozhu materialized silently beside him, looking bored.
The guards lowered their weapons, relief washing over them. "We pay our respects to the Crown Prince!"
Xia Chengyan waved them off, his burning gaze fixed on the depths of the palace. "Old man! Your son is back!"
The moment the words left his mouth, a wave of golden imperial qi swept out from the hall.
"Aaaah—!"
Xia Chengyan was caught in the blast, spinning through the air like a top, screaming miserably as he was flung into the inner sanctum.
Inside the inner hall.

Xia Xuanyin looked at his tumbling son with eyes full of gratification. At a glance, he could tell Xia Chengyan’s aura was rounded and condensed. He had reached the first level of the Nascent Soul stage.
Even more surprising was the cyan-clad girl beside him, who radiated the same cultivation level.

"Imperial Father!" Xia Chengyan steadied himself and offered a casual salute. He waved his hand proudly. "The Heavenly Abyss Alliance has sent two heavy hitters. These minor troubles in the Southern Region? Leave them to your son."
The corner of Xia Xuanyin's mouth twitched. He suppressed the urge to smack the boy again and turned to Lin Xiaozhu, bowing solemnly.
"Grandmaster Lin, you have traveled far. On behalf of the Southern Region, I offer my deepest gratitude."

Lin Xiaozhu bowed slightly in return. "Your Majesty is too polite. I am Lin Xiaozhu, here on orders from the Alliance Leader to assist. I heard Your Majesty needs to pinpoint the location of the [Demon Nest]. Do we have any leads?"

"We do," Xia Xuanyin said directly. "We have already confirmed the exact coordinates of the secret realm housing the Demon Nest. We were simply waiting for you and Chengyan to arrive. Tomorrow, we gather our forces and strike directly at the heart."
"What?!"
The smug look on Xia Chengyan's face instantly froze. His eyes widened as he exclaimed, "You found the Demon Nest? Then why did we come all this way? To watch a show?"
Xia Xuanyin glared at him. "The situation changed. I’ll explain the details later."

Lin Xiaozhu remained calm. "That is for the best. Coincidentally, the Heavenly Abyss Alliance has been investigating the source of the 'Seven Emotions' corruption. Recently, cultivators have been losing their minds and going berserk. We lacked leads, but perhaps we can find the connection here."
Xia Xuanyin nodded and arranged for servants to escort Lin Xiaozhu to her guest quarters.
Once she was gone, Xia Xuanyin produced a brocade box containing the [Zhang's Grand Gift Package] and handed it to his son. "Chengyan. This is for you."
Xia Chengyan opened the box curiously. He instantly gasped.
"Holy shit! Yellow Court Spirit Cleansing Pills? An Immortal Ascension Pill? And a complete set of Spirit Treasures? Old man, where did you loot all this good stuff?"

A complex emotion flickered in Xia Xuanyin's eyes. "They were gifted by a Southern Region prodigy named Zhang Xian. His origins are mysterious, his wealth is bottomless, and his methods are endless. He is the one who located the Demon Nest."
Xia Xuanyin briefly summarized Zhang Xian's background.
Xia Chengyan’s eyes exploded with light. "Too damn awesome. I must meet this Godfather!"
He stared at the box for a moment, then shoved it back into Xia Xuanyin's hands.
"Old man, this is your opportunity. Keep it. Greed chews more than it can swallow, and my life-bound artifact is enough for me. Besides, with my genius aptitude, I’m already awesome enough.

He grinned. "I’m counting on you to live a few more years so I can keep playing around in the Central Continent. Later, just give me two stalks of the Immortal Ascension Herb. One for me, one for Xiaozhu."
Xia Xuanyin looked at his son. Despite the hippie smile, the boy's eyes were sincere. A warm current surged through the Emperor's heart.
"What is the background of this Miss Lin?" Xia Xuanyin asked. "You and her..."

Xia Chengyan immediately puffed out his chest. "Niece of the Heavenly Abyss Alliance President, Sword God Lin! One of the Central Continent's Ten Outstanding Youths, ranked right alongside me. Heh, she likes me. She’s my little tag-along."
Xia Xuanyin raised an eyebrow. " The truth."

Xia Chengyan’s shoulders slumped. "Fine. I begged her. I know you’re too proud to ask the Central Continent for help unless you're desperate. Since you actually asked, I had to make sure it was handled beautifully. I... I almost got on my knees to get her to agree."
"What did you promise her?"
"Uh... does learning to bark like a puppy count?"
Xia Xuanyin was speechless. He patted his son's shoulder heavily. "She traveled thousands of miles to help you. Her feelings are not shallow. Do not let her down."

Xia Chengyan nodded, his expression turning serious. "I know. I’m sincere about her, too. I told her I’d make her my one and only Empress. Do you think I’m like you, with three thousand beauties in the harem?"
Xia Xuanyin felt a familiar, phantom ache in his head.
Early the next morning, above the Southern Capital.
Dozens of massive flying warships, each of a different design, hovered silently in the sky, forming a steel canopy.
Xia Chengyan and Lin Xiaozhu boarded the flagship alongside the Emperor. Xia Chengyan stood at the railing, striking a pose against the wind, scanning the deck.
His attention was instantly captured.
Near the bow, three women of peerless beauty and vastly different temperaments were clustered around a handsome young man.

There was Yun Wanqing, dressed in elegant robes, her demeanor gentle as water, whispering to the man with eyes full of concern. There was Li Fuxi, clad in stark white Daoist robes, cold and distant as the moon, standing silently at his side. And there was Lin Yinyin, lively and cute, chattering excitedly with flushed cheeks.
The man in the center was, of course, Zhang Xian.
Xia Chengyan’s eyes lit up with profound respect. He nudged his father and lowered his voice.
"Imperial Father... that must be the mysterious prodigy, Zhang Xian, right?"

chapters.title: Chapter 160 Eyes That Could Melt Steel
paragraphs: Xia Xuanyin shot his son a sidelong glance. "Oh? And how would you know?"

Xia Chengyan flashed a smug grin. "Isn't it obvious? Look at him. You can't call someone a Heaven's Chosen if he doesn't have the women to prove it. It’s practically the standard loadout for a protagonist."
As the words left his mouth, Lin Xiaozhu’s cool voice drifted from behind him. "What is the matter? Are you envious?"
Xia Chengyan shuddered visibly. He instantly composed himself, his expression shifting to one of solemn righteousness.
"Envious? Absurd," he declared. "Romance is a shackle. Women only slow down the speed at which I draw my sword."
He paused, stealing a quick, cautious glance at Lin Xiaozhu. His voice softened instantly. "Present company excluded, of course."
The corner of Lin Xiaozhu’s lips twitched upward. "Heh."
Xia Xuanyin watched his son’s antics and sighed internally. This brat is determined to lose all the Royal Family's face.

The Emperor led Xia Chengyan and Lin Xiaozhu forward, formally introducing them to the assembly. The crowd erupted in polite applause and flowery compliments. They praised the two returning Nascent Soul prodigies with idioms like "the dragon's bearing and phoenix's grace" and "the student surpassing the master."
Xia Chengyan and Lin Xiaozhu returned the greetings with practiced ease, their demeanor impeccable.
When they reached Zhang Xian, Xia Chengyan stepped forward first. His tone held genuine admiration.

"This must be Brother Zhang Xian, the man who humbled the Baoqing Workshop and gave the Guiyuan Sect a migraine. I have heard much of your renown. Seeing you today, your bearing is truly extraordinary. I am Xia Chengyan."
"Brother Xia flatters me," Zhang Xian replied, cupping his hands.

Inwardly, Zhang Xian was startled. This Crown Prince looked no older than two hundred years, yet his aura was condensed and flawless—a true Nascent Soul expert. The resources of the Central Continent truly produced monsters.
At that moment, a System prompt chimed in Zhang Xian's mind.
[Ding! Discovered a 73-point Daughter of Destiny: Lin Xiaozhu.]
[Ding! Lin Xiaozhu's Favorability towards you is 1. Binding successful.]
Xia Chengyan’s smile widened as his gaze swept over the three beauties standing near Zhang Xian.
"Brother Zhang, you are truly blessed! These three must be your wives, correct? Tsk, tsk. The bliss of having multiple partners... it is enough to make any man jealous."
Zhang Xian remained silent.
This Crown Prince really has no filter.
Li Fuxi’s brows furrowed slightly. Her voice cut through the air, cold and clear. "This humble Daoist is Li Fuxi. I am Zhang Xian’s Master.
The tone was flat, yet it carried an undeniable weight of authority.
Xia Chengyan’s smile froze on his face. He hurriedly bowed. "Ah, so it is Master Li. My apologies, I spoke out of turn."

Internally, however, the Prince clicked his tongue. Master? Please. The way she was looking at him just now... her eyes were practically melting steel. Brother Zhang plays a dangerous game. He’s conquered his Master and the legendary mistress of the Cloud Raiment Pavilion? He is truly a role model for our generation.
Shortly after, the fleet mobilized. Dozens of flying vessels roared to life, piercing the clouds as they headed north.
Inside the flagship’s tactical cabin, Xia Xuanyin gathered the core leadership, including Zhang Xian, Xia Chengyan, and Lin Xiaozhu.
The Emperor’s gaze swept over the room. "Esteemed allies, I will no longer conceal our true objective. This is not a patrol. This is a decapitation strike. We are going to eradicate the Demon Nest."
A ripple of shock went through those not privy to the inner circle, quickly replaced by a surge of battle lust.
"The location has been confirmed." Xia Xuanyin pointed to a desolate sector on the Southern Region star map. "It is hidden within a small, abandoned secret realm to the north."

He tapped the map. "Intelligence confirms the core defense consists of three Nascent Soul entities: the Central Continent puppet master, Daoist Qianji, and the two we encountered at the tournament—the Black Venerable and the White Venerable."

"Daoist Qianji is particularly dangerous," Xia Xuanyin continued. "He specializes in refining corpse puppets. Furthermore, the Nest is likely swarming with minions corrupted by the Entity of Evil Thoughts."

"We kept this quiet to prevent tipping them off," he concluded, his voice resonating like struck iron. "This battle determines the survival of the Southern Region. I expect everyone to give their all."
The atmosphere in the cabin reached a boiling point.
After the strategy meeting, Zhang Xian was the first to knock on Yun Wanqing’s cabin door.
When she opened it, a flicker of joy lit up her eyes. "How is your recovery progressing?"
"I am unharmed," Zhang Xian said, stepping inside. He looked at the gentle woman before him and sighed softly.

"You didn't have to come, you know. Elder Yun sensed his Heavenly Tribulation approaching and has gone into seclusion to break through. The Demon Nest is dangerous; we don't know what traps lie in wait."
Wanqing shook her head. She walked to the window, watching the sea of clouds rush past. "Two masters from the Mountain Zen Monastery are guarding my father. I would be of no use there."
She turned, her gaze firm. A gentle, teasing smile touched her lips. "Besides, are you looking down on me now?"

She stepped closer. "I am an eighth-stage Golden Core cultivator with a Spirit Treasure for protection. Thanks to you, I now possess a top-grade Fire Spiritual Root. If your Master can go, why can’t I?"
Zhang Xian looked into her clear eyes and saw an unshakable resolve. They both tacitly avoided speaking the name Xuan Zhou.
He stepped forward. "When we arrive, if you encounter any danger, crush the Mandarin Duck Pendant immediately."

"Mm," Yun Wanqing murmured, interlacing her fingers with his. Her palm was warm. "You must promise me not to be reckless. The injuries from the last battle haven't fully healed, and the Demon Nest views you as a thorn in their side. Please, be careful.
Her eyes were filled with a deep, dissolving tenderness.
Zhang Xian looked at her beautiful face, inches from his own. He lowered his head and pressed a kiss to her smooth forehead.
Yun Wanqing’s cheeks flushed a soft pink, but she didn’t pull away. Instead, she leaned gently into his embrace.
After a moment of warmth, Zhang Xian reluctantly pulled away.
Outside Yun Wanqing’s cabin, he stopped. He meticulously checked his robes, ensuring no lingering fragrance or stray hairs remained, before walking toward Li Fuxi’s quarters.
He pushed the door open.

Li Fuxi sat cross-legged on a meditation cushion, her spirit sword resting across her knees. She held a snow-white silk handkerchief soaked in spirit spring water, wiping the blade with absolute focus.
Her movements were gentle, but her eyes were sharp as glacial ice.

Zhang Xian could feel the rolling waves of sword intent radiating from her. She was sharpening her mind, adjusting her state for the coming slaughter—preparing to avenge her master and senior brother.
"Master," Zhang Xian called out softly.

Li Fuxi’s hand paused on the blade. "You said that among the demons, there is a Nascent Soul puppet master from the Central Continent? One who can refine the bodies of those whose souls haven't dispersed into puppets?"

"It is true," Zhang Xian replied gravely. "When Zhiyin and the others were trapped in the secret realm, her puppet substitute was refined by them. And Star Concealment... they controlled his divination techniques by refining his body, allowing them to blind the heavenly secrets."
Li Fuxi fell silent.
Slowly, she raised her head, her gaze locking onto Zhang Xian.
"Some time ago, at the Demon Sweeping Assembly, you fought a tall, sturdy puppet. It was skilled in deploying yellowish-brown defensive formations."
Her voice trembled slightly. "Did you... see its true face?"
Zhang Xian’s heart tightened.
He nodded slowly. "I did. I detonated a Spirit Treasure to break its defense."
He paused, his voice low. "The explosion blew off half its face."

I am Xia Chengyan."
"Brother Xia flatters me," Zhang Xian replied, cupping his hands.
Inwardly, Zhang Xian was startled.
This Crown Prince looked no older than two hundred years, yet his aura was condensed and flawless—a true Nascent Soul expert.
The resources of the Central Continent truly produced monsters.
At that moment, a System prompt chimed in Zhang Xian's mind.
[Ding!
Discovered a 73-point Daughter of Destiny: Lin Xiaozhu.]
[Ding!
Lin Xiaozhu's Favorability towards you is 1.
Binding successful.]
Xia Chengyan’s smile widened as his gaze swept over the three beauties standing near Zhang Xian.
"Brother Zhang, you are truly blessed!
These three must be your wives, correct?
Tsk, tsk.
The bliss of having multiple partners... it is enough to make any man jealous."
Zhang Xian remained silent.
This Crown Prince really has no filter.
Li Fuxi’s brows furrowed slightly.
Her voice cut through the air, cold and clear.
"This humble Daoist is Li Fuxi.
I am Zhang Xian’s Master.
The tone was flat, yet it carried an undeniable weight of authority.
Xia Chengyan’s smile froze on his face.
He hurriedly bowed.
"Ah, so it is Master Li.
My apologies, I spoke out of turn."
Internally, however, the Prince clicked his tongue.
Master?
Please.
The way she was looking at him just now... her eyes were practically melting steel.
Brother Zhang plays a dangerous game.
He’s conquered his Master and the legendary mistress of the Cloud Raiment Pavilion?
He is truly a role model for our generation.
Shortly after, the fleet mobilized.
Dozens of flying vessels roared to life, piercing the clouds as they headed north.
Inside the flagship’s tactical cabin, Xia Xuanyin gathered the core leadership, including Zhang Xian, Xia Chengyan, and Lin Xiaozhu.
The Emperor’s gaze swept over the room.
"Esteemed allies, I will no longer conceal our true objective.
This is not a patrol.
This is a decapitation strike.
We are going to eradicate the Demon Nest."
A ripple of shock went through those not privy to the inner circle, quickly replaced by a surge of battle lust.
"The location has been confirmed." Xia Xuanyin pointed to a desolate sector on the Southern Region star map.
"It is hidden within a small, abandoned secret realm to the north."
He tapped the map.

"Intelligence confirms the core defense consists of three Nascent Soul entities: the Central Continent puppet master, Daoist Qianji, and the two we encountered at the tournament—the Black Venerable and the White Venerable."
"Daoist Qianji is particularly dangerous," Xia Xuanyin continued.
"He specializes in refining corpse puppets.
Furthermore, the Nest is likely swarming with minions corrupted by the Entity of Evil Thoughts."
"We kept this quiet to prevent tipping them off," he concluded, his voice resonating like struck iron.
"This battle determines the survival of the Southern Region.
I expect everyone to give their all."
The atmosphere in the cabin reached a boiling point.
After the strategy meeting, Zhang Xian was the first to knock on Yun Wanqing’s cabin door.
When she opened it, a flicker of joy lit up her eyes.
"How is your recovery progressing?"
"I am unharmed," Zhang Xian said, stepping inside.
He looked at the gentle woman before him and sighed softly.
"You didn't have to come, you know.
Elder Yun sensed his Heavenly Tribulation approaching and has gone into seclusion to break through.
The Demon Nest is dangerous; we don't know what traps lie in wait."
Wanqing shook her head.
She walked to the window, watching the sea of clouds rush past.
"Two masters from the Mountain Zen Monastery are guarding my father.
I would be of no use there."
She turned, her gaze firm.
A gentle, teasing smile touched her lips.
"Besides, are you looking down on me now?"
She stepped closer.
"I am an eighth-stage Golden Core cultivator with a Spirit Treasure for protection.
Thanks to you, I now possess a top-grade Fire Spiritual Root.
If your Master can go, why can’t I?"
Zhang Xian looked into her clear eyes and saw an unshakable resolve.
They both tacitly avoided speaking the name Xuan Zhou.
He stepped forward.
"When we arrive, if you encounter any danger, crush the Mandarin Duck Pendant immediately."
"Mm," Yun Wanqing murmured, interlacing her fingers with his.
Her palm was warm.
"You must promise me not to be reckless.
The injuries from the last battle haven't fully healed, and the Demon Nest views you as a thorn in their side.
Please, be careful.
Her eyes were filled with a deep, dissolving tenderness.
Zhang Xian looked at her beautiful face, inches from his own.
He lowered his head and pressed a kiss to her smooth forehead.
Yun Wanqing’s cheeks flushed a soft pink, but she didn’t pull away.
Instead, she leaned gently into his embrace.
After a moment of warmth, Zhang Xian reluctantly pulled away.
Outside Yun Wanqing’s cabin, he stopped.
He meticulously checked his robes, ensuring no lingering fragrance or stray hairs remained, before walking toward Li Fuxi’s quarters.
He pushed the door open.
Li Fuxi sat cross-legged on a meditation cushion, her spirit sword resting across her knees.
She held a snow-white silk handkerchief soaked in spirit spring water, wiping the blade with absolute focus.
Her movements were gentle, but her eyes were sharp as glacial ice.
Zhang Xian could feel the rolling waves of sword intent radiating from her.
She was sharpening her mind, adjusting her state for the coming slaughter—preparing to avenge her master and senior brother.
"Master," Zhang Xian called out softly.
Li Fuxi’s hand paused on the blade.
"You said that among the demons, there is a Nascent Soul puppet master from the Central Continent?
One who can refine the bodies of those whose souls haven't dispersed into puppets?"
"It is true," Zhang Xian replied gravely.
"When Zhiyin and the others were trapped in the secret realm, her puppet substitute was refined by them.
And Star Concealment... they controlled his divination techniques by refining his body, allowing them to blind the heavenly secrets."
Li Fuxi fell silent.
Slowly, she raised her head, her gaze locking onto Zhang Xian.
"Some time ago, at the Demon Sweeping Assembly, you fought a tall, sturdy puppet.
It was skilled in deploying yellowish-brown defensive formations."
Her voice trembled slightly.
"Did you... see its true face?"
Zhang Xian’s heart tightened.
He nodded slowly.
"I did.
I detonated a Spirit Treasure to break its defense."
He paused, his voice low.
"The explosion blew off half its face."

chapters.title: Chapter 161 Leisure on the Eve of Battle
paragraphs: Li Fuxi fell silent. She raised her left hand, spiritual light dancing at her fingertips as she sketched rapidly in the empty air. Water vapor condensed, coalescing into a pristine mirror hovering before them.
Ripples cleared to reveal a face—a man with honest, rugged features and a steadfast set to his jaw. Even in the reflection, an air of unshakeable integrity seemed to radiate from him.
"Is it him?" Li Fuxi’s voice carried a tremor she couldn't quite suppress.
Zhang Xian scrutinized the image in the water mirror, overlaying it mentally with the ruined, half-shattered visage of the earth-attribute puppet he had fought.
He nodded slowly. "The puppet's face was stiff and waxen, but the bone structure and brow ridge are a match. It’s him."
Li Fuxi squeezed her eyes shut and let out a long, shuddering breath.
She raised her hand again. The water mirror rippled and shifted, reforming into the image of a middle-aged scholar with an elegant, refined demeanor.
"And him? Have you seen this man?"
Zhang Xian studied the image for a moment before shaking his head. "No. I haven't encountered him."
"They are my Senior Brother, Wang Pan," Li Fuxi said, her voice low and thick with suppressed emotion. "And my mentor... the former Head of Spirit Sword Peak, Master Wangchuan."

She paused, her gaze fixing on Zhang Xian. "Actually, back at the Demon-Suppression Conference, I had my suspicions the moment I saw that puppet unleash the [Profound Yellow Mountain-Steadying Rock]. Senior Brother Wang Pan’s cultivation technique is too unique. Almost no one else in the Southern Region mastered it to that degree. When you mentioned Daoist Qianji later... I knew."
Her eyes grew distant, lost in the memories of laughter that once echoed through Spirit Sword Peak.

Back then, Senior Brother and Second Senior Sister had been quietly in love. Li Fuxi was just a child, a little tag-along trailing behind them. She remembered how Second Senior Sister used to tease Senior Brother about his clumsy technique, mocking him for only knowing how to hide inside a "turtle shell" instead of wielding a sword with the dashing flair of other cultivators.
Senior Brother would just scratch his head and smile that honest smile.
“My job isn’t to look cool,” he would say. “It’s to protect you all. To protect Spirit Sword Peak.”
His swordsmanship was mediocre at best, but his [Profound Yellow Mountain-Steadying Rock] was flawless, an impenetrable wall known throughout the Southern Region.

Zhang Xian felt a weight settle in his chest. Beneath Li Fuxi’s calm narration, he sensed a turbulent ocean of grief. Her Master and Senior Brother were her world. To know their souls were denied rest, their bodies desecrated and refined into demonic puppets—it was a torture worse than death.
"Master," Zhang Xian said softly. "If we encounter them in the Demon Nest..."
CLANG—!
Li Fuxi’s spirit sword vibrated, emitting a sharp, piercing hum that cut through the air.

"Zhang Xian, you underestimate me." Her eyes snapped open, cold and clear. "I pray we encounter them. I will personally shatter the puppet shells imprisoning their souls. I will be the one to set Senior Brother and Master free."
She turned away, the vulnerability vanishing behind a mask of steel. "Go and rest. We must be in peak condition for the battle to come."
"Yes, Master." Sensing the absolute finality in her killing intent, Zhang Xian bowed and retreated without another word.
Leaving his master to her preparations, Zhang Xian made his way to Lin Yinyin’s cabin.
The moment he pushed the door open, a voice dripping with vinegar greeted him.
"Oh look! Master Zhang is finally off the clock? After comforting the first wife and the second wife, you finally remembered you have a little concubine tucked away here?

Zhang Xian didn’t say a word. He stepped inside, backhanded the door shut, and flicked his wrist. Spiritual light flared, instantly erecting a high-grade barrier that blocked all sound and severed any prying Divine Sense.
Lin Yinyin watched the swift, sneaky movements, her eyes widening.
No way. Is Brother really going to... in broad daylight?
She had embarrassed herself by misreading the mood several times before, so she tried to play it cool. "So... what does Brother have in mind this time?"
Zhang Xian chuckled, a wicked glint in his eyes as he sat down next to her, closing the distance. "What do you think?"
"Ah!" Lin Yinyin shrank back, her composure cracking. "Brother, chill out! Your injuries aren't even fully healed, and the war is about to start! Can't you... can't you get your priorities straight?"
Her voice dropped to a whisper, her face burning a brilliant crimson. "Wait... wait until the battle is over. Then Yinyin promises to play whatever game you want..."
Seeing her flustered, shy appearance, Zhang Xian felt a surge of heat. He reached into his robe, pulled out an exquisite jade slip, and shoved it into her hands.
"It is precisely because the battle is imminent that we need to do this. Right now."
"Cultivation?" Lin Yinyin blinked, confused. She accepted the jade slip and probed it with her Divine Sense.
Instantly, her jaw dropped.

The slip was filled with vivid, high-definition illustrations of men and women in various... entangled postures. Alongside the scandalous art were detailed diagrams of energy meridians and circulation routes.
Even for someone who claimed to be worldly, this was too much. She yelped and threw the jade slip across the room as if it were a burning coal.
"Ah! Pah, pah, pah! Brother, you pervert! Where did you get such filth? That’s too obscene!"

Zhang Xian kept a straight face, looking the picture of righteous indignation. "Obscene? How dare you! This is the orthodox Buddhist supreme art, [Joyous Zen]! I deciphered and annotated it myself. It represents the Grand Dao of Yin and Yang mutual generation. It’s a top-tier method for rapidly boosting cultivation!"
Lin Yinyin grimaced. "Do we really have to? I’ve heard those dual cultivation arts are just 'Furnace' techniques. One person steals the other’s cultivation."

Tears welled up in her eyes. She thought Zhang Xian wanted to use her as a disposable battery. She felt incredibly wronged, but she bit her lip, forcing back a sob. Her hand trembled as she reached out to pick up the discarded jade slip.
If Brother really needs my cultivation... I’ll give it to him.
Seeing her tragic expression, Zhang Xian realized she had misunderstood completely.
"Silly girl! What is going through that head of yours?" He grabbed her hand gently. "This isn't a plundering technique. This is a true Dual Cultivation secret art. It’s about mutual benefit!"

"Think about it. If the Mountain Zen Monastery practiced predatory arts, the righteous sects would have sieged them into oblivion centuries ago. Clear your mind. Look at the circulation routes. Does it look like theft, or does it look like fusion and regeneration?"
"Really?" Lin Yinyin looked at him suspiciously, sniffing back a tear.

Suppressing her intense embarrassment, she forced herself to examine the diagrams and text again. With her Heavenly Spiritual Root and genius-level comprehension, the initial shock faded, replaced by understanding.
She quickly saw the profundity of [Joyous Zen]. As Zhang Xian said, the core wasn't theft—it was balance. A perfect cycle of Yin and Yang elevating both partners.
"Okay... I guess you still have a conscience." She clutched the jade slip to her chest, her face still flushed, but her eyes bright with focus.
They began to study the manual together.

As they read, the spiritual energy within their bodies began to resonate, circulating involuntarily in sync with the method. A strange, intoxicating warmth flowed between them. The temperature in the small cabin rose, and the air grew thick with a heavy, enchanting ambiguity.
Meanwhile, in Xia Chengyan’s cabin.
The Crown Prince had barely spent an hour in his room before he started feeling restless. He got up and wandered down the hall to Lin Xiaozhu’s door.
A wooden sign hung on the handle: DO NOT DISTURB.
"Well, damn." Xia Chengyan wilted instantly.

"Sigh." He paced the corridor, bored out of his mind. Suddenly, he snapped his fingers. "I know! I’ll go hit up Brother Zhang. I need to ask him for some pointers. How the hell does he manage so many beauties without going insane?"
Excited, he jogged over to Zhang Xian’s cabin and knocked.
Knock knock.
No answer.
"Huh? Not here?" Xia Chengyan frowned. "Must be visiting one of his ladies."
He waited two hours and knocked again. Still nothing.
"Man, he’s got stamina."

Envious, Xia Chengyan leaned against the wall. His gaze swept idly down the hallway and stopped at Lin Yinyin’s door. His cultivation was high enough to detect the extremely subtle, high-level barrier fluctuations sealing the room.
"Oho? So that's where he is."
Xia Chengyan recalled Lin Yinyin—the lively, cute girl in Zhang Xian’s harem. A bit too energetic for my taste, I prefer the refined coolness of my Xiaozhu, but to each their own.
He decided to wait.
One day passed.
Two days passed.
For three straight days, Xia Chengyan would periodically stroll past Lin Yinyin’s cabin. Every single time, he sensed the barrier was still active. The fluctuations hadn't ceased for a second.
"Tsk, tsk, tsk..."
Xia Chengyan shook his head, his face a mixture of shock and pure bro-spect.
"War is knocking at the door, and he's still going at it? Brother Zhang... you are an absolute legend."

chapters.title: Chapter 162 Breaking More Than Just the Ice
paragraphs: By the afternoon of the third day, Xia Chengyan found himself wandering past the hallway again. He stared at the barrier ripples still sealing the door, his expression blank.
He was beginning to question reality.
Three days.
Straight.
This... this is just inhuman.
Just as his worldview was about to be shattered and rebuilt from scratch—
Click.
The door to Lin Yinyin’s cabin finally opened.

Zhang Xian stepped out. Far from looking exhausted, his complexion was ruddy and glowing with health. His aura brimmed with vitality, as if he had just bathed in a spiritual spring. Even the lingering weakness from using [Shadowflame] had been completely washed away.
He immediately spotted Xia Chengyan standing in the corridor, looking a bit shell-shocked.
Zhang Xian flashed a warm, enthusiastic smile. "Yo, Brother Xia. Fancy meeting you here."
Xia Chengyan snapped back to reality. The look he gave Zhang Xian wasn't just friendly anymore; it was the kind of awe one felt when gazing up at a towering, insurmountable mountain.

He immediately adopted a humble posture, cupping his hands with profound respect. "Ah, Brother Zhang! What a coincidence! This Little Brother actually had some... cultivation questions I was hoping to ask you. Do you have a moment?"
Zhang Xian paused.
Little Brother?

The man standing before him was a Nascent Soul prodigy fresh from the Central Continent, the Crown Prince of the Great Xia Dynasty. He was nobility among nobility. Yet here he was, bowing and scraping like a junior disciple?
What is this guy plotting? Zhang Xian wondered, eyeing him suspiciously.
Still, he politely invited Xia Chengyan into his cabin.
Once seated, Xia Chengyan started with the usual pleasantries, thanking Zhang Xian profusely for the earlier gifts of Spirit Stones and resources.
After the polite small talk, the Prince coughed dryly, shifting nervously in his seat.
"Actually, Brother Zhang, I didn't just come here to say thanks. This Little Brother... cough... Xia has a personal matter I need your expert advice on."
"Oh?" Zhang Xian raised an eyebrow. "Speak freely, Brother Xia."
Xia Chengyan rubbed his hands together, leaning in with a look of man-to-man conspiracy.

"It’s about... well, Brother Zhang, how did you, uh, handle three different beauties at once? That kind of harem blessing isn't easy to manage. Do you have a secret technique? Could you give me some pointers?"
Zhang Xian nearly choked on his tea.
He stared at the Crown Prince. This guy—powerful, wealthy, talented—had camped outside his door for three days just to ask that?
Zhang Xian’s mouth twitched. He looked into Xia Chengyan’s eyes, seeing nothing but pure, unadulterated thirst for knowledge.
He held the silence for a long moment, then spat out two words.
"Sincerity."
Xia Chengyan blinked. "..."
The anticipation on his face froze. "Uh... Brother Zhang? That’s it? Nothing else?"
Zhang Xian stroked his chin, his expression turning solemn. "Money. Or rather, Spirit Stones. Treasures. Wealth."

"Money? That’s the secret?" Xia Chengyan looked disappointed. "My old man is the Emperor. I’m not lacking in Spirit Stones or treasures. I have VIP black cards for every major auction house in the Central Continent! And as for sincerity, I have that too. I treat her better than anyone."
Zhang Xian looked at him and shook his head slowly, wearing a profound expression.
"No. You don't get it."
"Huh?" Xia Chengyan looked lost.

"Your lady, Lin Xiaozhu. She’s the niece of Sword God Lin, the leader of the Heavenly Abyss Alliance, correct?" Zhang Xian explained leisurely. "In terms of background, she’s not below you. In terms of cultivation, she’s your equal. Anything you have, she probably has too—maybe even more."
"When the two parties are perfectly matched in status and wealth, your money loses its power. It’s not a flex to her."
Xia Chengyan fell into deep thought, nodding slowly.

"When you cannot establish absolute economic dominance," Zhang Xian continued, "you have to invest more heavily in sincerity." He smirked, teasing him. "But from what I can see, Miss Lin is already quite fond of you. What’s the rush?"
Called out, Xia Chengyan flushed slightly. "Brother Zhang has keen eyes! Xiaozhu treats me well, it’s just..."
He sighed. "I feel like there’s still a thin layer of paper between us. We haven't defined the relationship. It makes me feel... unsure."

Zhang Xian nodded with an 'I got you' look. "I understand. But I suspect you want to do more than just break the ice and define the relationship, right? Perhaps His Highness wants to take things... physically further?"
"Pfft—!"
Xia Chengyan sprayed his tea all over the floor.
He coughed violently, face turning beet red. "It’s—it’s not that I’m desperate for that! Just curious! Purely for academic reference!"
Zhang Xian burst out laughing, finally letting the poor guy off the hook.
For the next hour, the two men engaged in a deep, philosophical exchange on "How to woo a woman who likes you but hasn't made it official yet."

Drawing from his vast experience—which mostly consisted of being shameless and throwing money at problems—Zhang Xian offered a treasure trove of advice. Xia Chengyan listened with rapt attention, nodding repeatedly, his eyes shining as if a new world had opened before him.
"So that's how it is!"
"Brilliant!"
"I've learned so much!"
The Crown Prince looked like he had just received an enlightenment transmission from a sage.
Satisfied, Xia Chengyan stood up to leave. "Brother Zhang, you truly are wise. This method is absolutely badass. I think I can finally nail this situation."
Zhang Xian paused.
Badass? Nail it?
Those words—Niubi and Gaoding—popped out of the Prince's mouth naturally.
Suspicion flared in Zhang Xian’s heart again.
Is he a fellow transmigrator?
But something felt off. The slang usage was slightly stiff, like someone using borrowed words rather than native slang.

He hesitated for a second, then asked casually, "Brother Xia, your way of speaking is quite unique. Those terms you used... I rarely hear them in the Southern Region. Where does that dialect come from?"

"Oh, this?" Xia Chengyan waved his hand dismissively. "It was a huge trend in the Central Continent years ago. It’s called 'Vernacular' or 'Strongman Slang' (Qiang Zhe Yu). Legend has it that a maverick Senior pioneered it. It emphasizes being direct, punchy, and grounded!"

"It sort of fell out of fashion later, but I like it. It sounds cool and feels satisfying to say. Holy sh*t, Awesome—it just rolls off the tongue. There are still some people in the Central Continent who use it, but not many."
Zhang Xian nodded, keeping his face impassive.
I knew it.
Another footprint left by a transmigrator predecessor. That Senior must have been quite influential in the Central Continent to start an entire linguistic subculture.
Remembering how his System progress bar surged after he crippled Yang Poxiao, Zhang Xian reminded himself to be cautious. He absolutely could not expose his origins.
"I see. Fascinating," Zhang Xian said with a polite smile, seeing his guest out.
Once Xia Chengyan was gone, Zhang Xian’s expression sobered.
He checked the time. He and Lin Yinyin had spent three days comprehending the [Joyous Zen] manual. That meant they were only one day away from the Demon Nest.
The fun and games were over. The war was about to begin.
He sat down cross-legged and began his final inventory check.

First, his gear: A full set of lower-grade Spirit Treasures, various Earth-grade talismans, and pills. He was balanced for both offense and defense. He also had his favorite tactic—detonating Spirit Treasures like grenades. Against Golden Core cultivators, it was devastating. Against Nascent Soul enemies? Limited utility, unless they stood still and let him blow them up.
Next, his trump cards: The [Void-Piercing Shuttle] for escape, and the [Nine Nether Tribulation Puppet] for combat. These were his lifeline.
Finally, his own strength.
Golden Core Fifth Layer. Top-grade Wood Spiritual Root. His other four roots were slightly weaker, but having integrated them, he could now utilize wind and thunder attribute abilities proficiently.

Currently, his deadliest technique was the [Shadowflame] he had stolen from Yang Poxiao. However, it was a double-edged sword. It was a one-shot nuke for a decisive moment; using it would leave him drained and vulnerable.
He had absorbed some of Yang Poxiao’s memories and knew that the man’s Top-grade Fire Root and [Shadowflame] had been exchanged from a System.
Zhang Xian sighed. He had been "returning" wealth for so long, yet he still hadn't received a reward of that specific high-grade caliber.
Well, he thought, eyes narrowing. Maybe this war will change that.

He stared at the barrier ripples still sealing the door, his expression blank.
He was beginning to question reality.

Straight.
This... this is just inhuman.
Just as his worldview was about to be shattered and rebuilt from scratch—
Click.

Zhang Xian stepped out.
Far from looking exhausted, his complexion was ruddy and glowing with health.
His aura brimmed with vitality, as if he had just bathed in a spiritual spring.
Even the lingering weakness from using [Shadowflame] had been completely washed away.
He immediately spotted Xia Chengyan standing in the corridor, looking a bit shell-shocked.
Zhang Xian flashed a warm, enthusiastic smile.
"Yo, Brother Xia.
Fancy meeting you here."
Xia Chengyan snapped back to reality.
The look he gave Zhang Xian wasn't just friendly anymore; it was the kind of awe one felt when gazing up at a towering, insurmountable mountain.
He immediately adopted a humble posture, cupping his hands with profound respect.
"Ah, Brother Zhang!
What a coincidence!
This Little Brother actually had some... cultivation questions I was hoping to ask you.
Do you have a moment?"
Zhang Xian paused.
Little Brother?
The man standing before him was a Nascent Soul prodigy fresh from the Central Continent, the Crown Prince of the Great Xia Dynasty.
He was nobility among nobility.
Yet here he was, bowing and scraping like a junior disciple?
What is this guy plotting?
Zhang Xian wondered, eyeing him suspiciously.
Still, he politely invited Xia Chengyan into his cabin.
Once seated, Xia Chengyan started with the usual pleasantries, thanking Zhang Xian profusely for the earlier gifts of Spirit Stones and resources.
After the polite small talk, the Prince coughed dryly, shifting nervously in his seat.
"Actually, Brother Zhang, I didn't just come here to say thanks.
This Little Brother... cough...
Xia has a personal matter I need your expert advice on."
"Oh?" Zhang Xian raised an eyebrow.
"Speak freely, Brother Xia."
Xia Chengyan rubbed his hands together, leaning in with a look of man-to-man conspiracy.
"It’s about... well, Brother Zhang, how did you, uh, handle three different beauties at once?
That kind of harem blessing isn't easy to manage.
Do you have a secret technique?
Could you give me some pointers?"
Zhang Xian nearly choked on his tea.
He stared at the Crown Prince.
This guy—powerful, wealthy, talented—had camped outside his door for three days just to ask that?
Zhang Xian’s mouth twitched.
He looked into Xia Chengyan’s eyes, seeing nothing but pure, unadulterated thirst for knowledge.
He held the silence for a long moment, then spat out two words.
"Sincerity."
Xia Chengyan blinked.
The anticipation on his face froze.
Brother Zhang?
That’s it?
Nothing else?"
Zhang Xian stroked his chin, his expression turning solemn.
"Money.
Or rather, Spirit Stones.
Treasures.
Wealth."
"Money?
That’s the secret?" Xia Chengyan looked disappointed.
"My old man is the Emperor.
I’m not lacking in Spirit Stones or treasures.
I have VIP black cards for every major auction house in the Central Continent!
And as for sincerity, I have that too.
I treat her better than anyone."
Zhang Xian looked at him and shook his head slowly, wearing a profound expression.
"No.
You don't get it."
"Huh?" Xia Chengyan looked lost.
"Your lady, Lin Xiaozhu.
She’s the niece of Sword God Lin, the leader of the Heavenly Abyss Alliance, correct?" Zhang Xian explained leisurely.
"In terms of background, she’s not below you.
In terms of cultivation, she’s your equal.
Anything you have, she probably has too—maybe even more."
"When the two parties are perfectly matched in status and wealth, your money loses its power.
It’s not a flex to her."

Purely for academic reference!"

chapters.title: Chapter 163 When Did They Become So Close
paragraphs: One day later. The entrance to the desolate Minor World.

Dozens of colossal spirit vessels hovered in the void, their hulls gleaming under the starlight. A suffocating, murderous aura saturated the space between them, heavy enough to crush the lungs of a mortal.

Xia Xuanyin stood at the prow of the flagship, his imperial robes snapping in the cosmic wind. His eyes were like lightning, sweeping over the legion of cultivators standing in grim silence behind him.
His voice, infused with qi, rolled through the void like thunder:
"Fellow Daoists! Today, we gather not for exploration, nor for treasure! We are here for one purpose—to purge the demonic plague!"

"The corruption has ravaged our Southern Domain. It has slaughtered the innocent and rotted the foundations of our cultivation world. Their crimes are unrecordable, their evil intolerable to the Heavens!"

"Today, the Heavenly Dao watches. The Demon Nest has been found. It lies within the dead world before us. This war is not for private vengeance, but for public justice! For the peace of billions, for the souls of our fallen kin! For the dignity of every cultivator who walks the path!"
The Emperor drew his sword, pointing it at the swirling vortex of the entrance.

"I, Xia Xuanyin, swear this oath! I shall lead the vanguard. I will be the first to bleed and the first to kill. Cultivators of the Southern Domain, lend me your strength! We shall scour this filth from existence!"
His gaze sharpened, turning cold as absolute zero.
"Furthermore: Any among us found tainted by black energy or fallen to the demonic path—capture them for interrogation. But if they resist... kill them without mercy!"
"Follow me! SLAUGHTER THE DEMONS!"
"SLAUGHTER THE DEMONS!!!"
A roar like mountains collapsing and tsunamis crashing erupted from every vessel. The killing intent soared, piercing the very fabric of the void.

Xia Xuanyin wasted no more words. He transformed into a streak of golden light, plunging headlong into the spatial rift. Top-tier powerhouses like Xia Chengyan, Lin Xiaozhu, and Zhiyin followed close behind, trailing comets of spiritual energy.
Zhang Xian took a deep breath. He exchanged a glance with Li Fuxi, Yun Wanqing, and Lin Yinyin. He saw no fear, only steel resolve.
"Let's go."
The four of them rose into the air, merging into the river of light flowing into the Minor World.

Earlier, Lin Yinyin and Yun Wanqing had insisted on joining the front lines. Zhang Xian had worried, but he hadn't stopped them. The path to immortality defied the Heavens; true powerhouses could not be raised in a greenhouse. Still, he hadn't sent them in empty-handed. He had equipped them with [Void-Piercing Shuttles] and [Nine Nether Tribulation Puppets]. Between those trump cards and their own formidable artifacts, their survival was all but guaranteed.
Inside the desolate Minor World.
A leaden gray sky pressed down on a landscape of deathly silence.

This was the domain of the demons. Zhang Xian felt a chill run down his spine. He could taste the faint, foul negative energy in the air. It felt like maggots clinging to bone, constantly trying to burrow into his mind and erode his will.

As the army landed, the silence was shattered. Cultivators deployed their movement techniques—riding flying swords, clouds, or artifacts—and streaked toward the core of the world where the demonic energy was thickest.
Ahead, Xia Chengyan flew side-by-side with Lin Xiaozhu. The girl raised a fair hand, and a massive Eight Trigrams formation disk materialized beneath their feet, humming with soft, profound light.
"Big Bro! Sisters-in-law! Over here!
Xia Chengyan waved enthusiastically at Zhang Xian. "Hop on Xiaozhu’s disk. It’s the Rolls-Royce of flight tools—fast and steady!"

Zhang Xian smiled and didn't stand on ceremony. He signaled Li Fuxi, Yun Wanqing, Lin Yinyin, and the silent Golden Core crone guarding Yun Wanqing to follow him. They landed lightly on the formation disk, which was spacious enough to hold a dinner party.
The women exchanged confused glances.
When did the Crown Prince become so tight with Zhang Xian? And... 'Sisters-in-law'? Plural?
However, sensing the gravity of the situation, they tacitly chose to stay silent.
Once everyone was secure, Lin Xiaozhu performed a hand seal. The disk’s runes flared, and it accelerated instantly, locking into position right behind Emperor Xia’s golden chariot.
As they flew, Lin Xiaozhu spoke, her voice calm but serious. "The dangers ahead are unpredictable. Allow me to cast a hexagram to glimpse our fortune."
She produced a bamboo tube carved with esoteric runes.
Tapping the tube, she murmured an incantation. The cylinder spun rapidly, emitting a high-pitched hum.
Snap.
A jade lot jumped out.

Xia Chengyan leaned in to read the characters carved into the jade. "'Upper Middle'? Hah! That’s an auspicious sign! I told you, with this dream team, sweeping the Demon Nest will be a walk in the park!"
Lin Xiaozhu didn't smile. She frowned, shaking her head.
"The qi mechanism is chaotic. This reading feels... false." She paused, her eyes narrowing. "Let me test the fortune bond of 'Diu Diu'."
She formed a new set of seals. The tube spun again.
Snap.
Another lot jumped out.
Lower Upper.

A faint, mirthless smile touched Lin Xiaozhu’s lips. "I thought so. I used a 'Qi-Locking Technique' to permanently fix Diu Diu's fate as 'Middle'. But this hexagram shows 'Lower Upper'. The heavenly secrets in this realm have been scrambled by a powerful force. The enemy is prepared for us."
Lin Yinyin blinked, curiosity overcoming her nerves. "Miss Lin, what is a 'Diu Diu'?"

"A little spiritual fox I adopted years ago," Lin Xiaozhu explained patiently. "Because its fate is magically locked, any deviation in a reading about it proves that the surrounding divination field is compromised. We are flying blind."
Lin Yinyin nodded, looking impressed.
Suddenly, Xia Chengyan caught his father’s eye across the void. Emperor Xia gave an almost imperceptible nod.
"Everyone, heighten your vigilance!" The Emperor’s command boomed across the formation.
Before the echo faded, four figures moved in perfect synchronization.
Perfected Being Shouheng, Zhiyin, Lin Xiaozhu, and the Supreme Elder of the Spirit Sword Sect took positions at the cardinal directions—Southeast, Northwest, Northeast, Southwest.
BOOM!

Four pillars of blinding golden light erupted from them, piercing the gloom. The beams converged high above the army, weaving together to form a colossal, mirror-like screen. Runes flowed across its surface like liquid fire. It hung in the gray sky like an artificial sun.
"Four Symbols Break Evil, Clear Heart Shines Universally!" Perfected Being Shouheng’s voice resonated like a temple bell.
Warm, purifying light cascaded down from the golden mirror, bathing the entire expeditionary force.

Zhang Xian felt a rush of coolness penetrate his forehead. His Divine Sense instantly sharpened, the fog lifting from his mind. The subtle, irritating bloodlust that had been creeping into his psyche vanished like smoke in a gale.
"ARGHHH—!"
"NO! NOOO!"
But beneath the holy light, hell broke loose.
Screams of agony tore through the ranks. Dozens of cultivators suddenly convulsed. Their eyes turned pitch black, veins bulging with necrotic energy as black smoke poured from their pores.
Some clutched their heads, wailing as the light burned them. Others snapped, roaring like beasts as they drew their weapons and slashed at the allies standing next to them.
Zhang Xian watched in shock as a Golden Core supervisor from the Yunmiao Sect raised his sword and tried to behead his own junior brother.
"It is the corruption of [Desire]. They have been turned," Emperor Xia’s voice cut through the chaos, cold and merciless. "They are no longer your kin. They are claws of the demon. Kill them."
Panic flared, but these were the elites of the Southern Domain. The hesitation lasted only a heartbeat.
Blades flashed. Spells detonated.
The corrupted cultivators, disoriented by the purifying light, were swiftly cut down by their comrades. The internal rebellion was crushed before it could truly begin.
At that moment, Zhiyin stepped forward.

Countless palm-sized, lifelike miniature puppets flew out from her sleeves. They swarmed over the army like hummingbirds, flying to every single cultivator. Each puppet held a jade pendant glowing with warm yellow light.

"These are improved [Clear Heart Pendants]," Zhiyin announced, her voice carrying a soothing mental frequency. "Wear them. They will shield your mind from the corruption of Desire. All pendants are linked to form a grand mental defense array."
Her tone hardened slightly.
"Furthermore, look to your left and right. If you see anyone not wearing a pendant... strike first. They are likely a hidden demon."

chapters.title: Chapter 164 Stop Hiding and 1v1 Me!
paragraphs: Zhang Xian caught the jade pendant from the miniature Zhiyin hovering before him. The jade felt warm and smooth against his palm, sending a stream of refreshing coolness up his arm and into his inner palace, settling his mind instantly.
He inwardly gave a thumbs up. Having a professional support carry the team is just different. Look at these logistics. Look at these AOE buffs. Top tier.
As for how much his own massive injection of funds contributed to the R&D of these pendants? Details. A whale doesn't care about the process; a whale only cares about the results.
He had just fastened the pendant to his waist when his heart gave a violent lurch. A vast, suffocatingly cold aura surged from the gray horizon like a tidal wave.
"Here they come!" Zhang Xian’s eyes narrowed, his Divine Sense exploding outward to scan the field.
Hovering in the void above the desolate plain stood a figure clad in familiar black robes. A white mask covered his face, revealing only a pair of eyes as cold as glacial ice.
The White Venerable, Xuan Zhou.

Waves of terrifying Nascent Soul pressure radiated from him, distorting the air. Behind him stood a dark, dense mass of cultivators—at least a thousand strong. Most had dull, lifeless eyes, their bodies wreathed in faint black mist. They looked less like men and more like marionettes. Far behind them, a distorted, vortex-like spatial gate churned slowly.
"To think you actually found this place directly," Xuan Zhou’s voice filtered through the mask. It was flat, even, and utterly devoid of emotion.
Xia Chengyan stood at the prow of the formation disk and let out a loud, mocking laugh.

"Hahaha! So you're the White Venerable? The guy who hides his head and shows his tail?" He pointed a finger at the masked figure. "Xia Chengyan of the Heavenly Abyss Alliance is here! You demonic trash, surrender now and I might make it quick!"

Xuan Zhou’s gaze seemed to sweep over the alliance forces, but it didn't linger for a fraction of a second, as if he were looking at empty air. He slowly raised a hand toward the dark mass of puppets behind him and clenched his fist in the void.
"ROAR—!"
"KILL—!"

The thousand-plus corrupted cultivators snapped to action like machines with a flipped switch. Black threads surged into their eyes, erasing the last vestiges of reason. Like floodwaters bursting a dam, they launched a fearless, suicidal charge.
Zhang Xian noted grimly that the front lines were filled with Foundation Establishment and even Qi Condensation fodder.
"Delusional," Emperor Xia Xuanyin snorted coldly. "Form ranks! Engage!"
The elite disciples, deacons, and Elders of the great sects had long since formed their battle arrays.
BOOM!

Spiritual light erupted across the front line. Sword Qi crisscrossed the sky like a net; spells roared like thunder. It was less a battle and more like a scythe sweeping through dry wheat. The demonic minions at the front were vaporized instantly. The low-level cultivators were as fragile as paper, turning to ash before they could even scream.
It was a one-sided slaughter.
In mere moments, the thousand-strong army was annihilated. Corpses carpeted the barren earth.

Xia Chengyan flicked his imaginary sleeves, looking incredibly smug. He shouted across the battlefield, "Is that it? That's your army? Hey, old thief White Venerable! Stop hiding behind trash and come 1v1 me!"

Xuan Zhou continued to ignore him completely. His icy eyes scanned the righteous alliance forces as if observing a colony of ants. He spoke again, his voice possessing a terrifying lack of inflection.
"Just a bunch of worthless discarded pieces. I simply borrowed your hands to clean house. They aren't even worthy of the word 'demon'."
He turned slowly, facing the massive vortex gate. His voice pierced the void, clearly ringing in every cultivator's ears.
"This White Venerable awaits your esteemed presence inside the Demon Nest."
With that, he took a single step into the distorted vortex and vanished.
The alliance army halted before the swirling vortex of light.

Perfected Being Wang Ya stared at the pale white portal, noting the faint Five Elements spiritual light flowing at its edges. "This is it. The entrance to the secret realm. The Demon Nest is right in front of us."
A naturally cautious cultivator spoke up, voice tense. "Everyone, be extremely careful. Could this be like last time? What if the gate vanishes the moment we enter, trapping us in a dead zone?"
His worry wasn't unfounded. The lesson from the previous encounter was written in blood; demons were cunning, and spatial traps were their specialty.

Hearing this, several experts in formations and spatial theory immediately stepped forward. Some pulled out compass artifacts, watching the needles spin wildly. Others formed complex hand seals, firing beams of probing light into the vortex. A few cautiously tossed specially crafted spatial beacons into the gate to test its stability.
Lin Xiaozhu didn't move. She stood quietly at the edge of the formation disk, eyes half-closed.
A vast, refined, and incredibly precise wave of Divine Sense spread out from her. It didn't just scan the gate; it penetrated deep into the very core of the dead world beneath their feet.
A moment later, her eyes snapped open. Her gaze was clear and calm.
"You need not worry. This vortex isn't a temporary trap. It is a stable space formed after the origin of this small world was forcibly severed."

"I have analyzed the world's origin," she explained. "This small world's vitality was cut off at least a thousand years ago. This secret realm... it was a final refuge. The survivors of this world used forbidden methods to slice a piece of their reality away from the dying parent world to create a lifeboat. But now, it seems this lifeboat has become a true demon's den."

"Whether it is a dragon's pool or a tiger's den, or a pit of monsters and ghosts, it matters not," Xia Xuanyin declared, his voice iron. "The Demon Nest is before us. The enemy is inside. We are cultivators—what is there to fear?
His eyes blazed like torches. With a snap of his black dragon robes, the Emperor stepped into the spatial turbulence, charging boldly into the vortex.
The army followed, filing through the distorted tunnel.
After a brief wave of dizziness, they emerged on the other side. A suffocating aura of death slammed into their faces.
The moment they landed, Xia Xuanyin’s Divine Sense flooded the area. His expression instantly darkened.
"There isn't a single living soul."

Wang Ya crouched down, crumbling the dry, cracked earth between his fingers. He had never been here personally, but years ago, he had heard Zhiyin Two describe this place as indistinguishable from a mortal kingdom. Why was it now a barren wasteland?
The group advanced in silence. Soon, they reached the core of the secret realm—a massive, once-prosperous capital city.
But the sight that greeted them was a horror that choked the breath from their lungs.
The city walls were crumbled ruins. The streets were empty of life. But they were not empty.
As far as the eye could see, the ground was paved with white bones.

Tens of thousands of skeletons lay everywhere. They were frozen in disturbing, casual postures. Some were curled in corners. Some lay by the roadside. Others were still standing, locked in poses of walking or chatting, as if time had been instantaneously frozen.
Under the dim gray sky, the sea of bones gleamed with a pale, sickly luster.
"Ah!" Lin Yinyin, still possessing the heart of a young girl, couldn't help but gasp, covering her mouth in horror.
Zhang Xian looked out over the city, his expression heavy. Through the positioning of the bones, he could almost see the ghosts of the past.

One second, this city had been bustling with the noise of the market, children playing, merchants shouting. The next second, invisible death had swept through like a plague, stripping every living being of their vitality instantly.
There had been no struggle. No resistance. Only silent, total annihilation.

"It is the effect of the [Withered Glory Samsara Restriction] pushed to its absolute limit," Lin Xiaozhu’s voice trembled slightly. "The moment the formation activated, it extracted the life force origin of every living being in the realm. They didn't even have time to realize they were dying. In a few breaths, an entire civilization turned to dry bones."
She took a deep, shaky breath. "Judging by the weathering... this happened about two years ago."

"Two years..." Xia Xuanyin’s eyes burned with a terrifying cold light. "Right after we discovered the traces of the Demon Nest. To hide their tracks, they didn't hesitate to slaughter the entire population of their own secret realm."

chapters.title: Chapter 165 Let’s Jump Him!
paragraphs: A suffocating mixture of grief, outrage, and murderous intent hung heavy in the air.
Then—
SCREEECH!
A grating, metallic cackle tore through the silence of the dead capital, sounding like iron scraping against bone.
Everyone looked up sharply.
In mid-air, a phantom figure coalesced, shrouded entirely in voluminous black robes. His face was hidden behind an expressionless metal mask, revealing only a pair of muddy, soulless eyes.
"Welcome, everyone, to the Demon Nest."
His voice filtered through the mask, laced with mockery and cruelty. He waved a withered hand casually, as if scattering feed to chickens.
Whoosh! Whoosh! Whoosh!

Like a downpour of black rain, countless figures shot out from the void. Densely packed like a swarm of locusts, they plummeted toward the alliance forces. These figures moved with stiff, jerky limbs. Their eyes were vacant voids.
They were puppets.
Most emitted the aura of the early or mid-Golden Core stage. But what chilled the cultivators to the bone wasn't their strength—it was their faces.
"Senior Brother Zhao? No!"
"That's Uncle-Master Wang!"
"Junior Sister! How could you be..."

Cries of shock and roars of pure agony erupted instantly. Among the descending horde were disciples and Elders who had gone missing years ago or had fallen in previous battles. Now, refined into unfeeling tools of war, their faces twisted with necrotic energy, they pounced on their former brothers, sisters, and lovers.
"Daoist Qianji!" Xia Chengyan roared, his eyes burning with fury. "You sick bastard!"

Without hesitation, the Prince shot into the sky. A longsword flowing with crimson-gold flames materialized in his hand. The blade's light tore through the gloomy sky, slashing straight for the masked puppeteer.
"Hmph." Daoist Qianji snorted coldly, not bothering to dodge.
The space behind him twisted, and a towering, bulky puppet suddenly stepped out. The puppet raised both massive arms, and a thick, solid wall of earthen-yellow light instantly condensed before it.
CLANG!!!
Xia Chengyan’s peerless sword strike slammed into the shield, erupting in a blinding explosion of sparks and shockwaves. The light shield shuddered violently, but it did not shatter.
"[Profound Yellow Mountain-Suppressing Rock]?"
Li Fuxi’s pupils contracted to pinpricks. She recognized that signature defense at a glance. It was the unique, unparalleled skill of her Eldest Senior Brother, Wang Pan.
An icy, absolute killing intent detonated from her body.
Shing!

Her spirit sword left its sheath. Two brilliant lotuses of sword qi bloomed around her, spinning with lethal velocity. Several Golden Core puppets that tried to intercept her were instantly shredded into meat and scrap metal.
She tapped the ground, transforming into a streak of white light, following Xia Chengyan’s wake to pierce straight at Daoist Qianji.
Below, the [Eight Trigrams Formation Plate] beneath Lin Xiaozhu’s feet lit up with piercing intensity. She swept her gaze over the chaotic battlefield, her expression turning grave.
"I sense them! Two other Nascent Soul signatures... deep within the Imperial Mausoleum!"
As soon as her words fell, the entire secret realm began to quake violently. A blinding, pure white light erupted from both the sky and the ground, swallowing everything indiscriminately.
"It's a randomized teleportation array! Be careful!" Lin Xiaozhu’s urgent warning came just a split second before the light engulfed them.
Crap, Zhang Xian thought the moment the light flared.
From the corner of his eye, he saw Li Fuxi charging recklessly toward Qianji. He didn't hesitate. He slapped a high-grade Wind Talisman on his leg.
Whoosh!
Leaving an afterimage behind, he appeared beside Li Fuxi as if teleporting. In the instant before the white light swallowed them, he wrapped his arm tightly around her slender waist.
"What are you doing?!" Li Fuxi shouted, shocked and angry.
The next second, the world spun.
Vertigo slammed into them.

When the light faded, Zhang Xian and Li Fuxi found themselves standing in a vast, open square. Majestic, dilapidated palace ruins surrounded them. Directly ahead, perched on the soaring eaves of a palace roof, stood the black-robed Daoist Qianji.
His hands were clasped behind his back, his icy gaze locked onto them like a viper.
"How deeply affectionate," Qianji cackled, the sound grating on the ears.
His gaze swept over Zhang Xian before settling greedily on Li Fuxi.

"You must be the brat the White Venerable wants dead. And as for the little girl beside you..." He licked his lips beneath the mask, his eyes flickering with a sinister, ghostly light. "Tsk, tsk, tsk. A pure Dual Spiritual Root. If I refined you into a puppet to serve by my side day and night... wouldn't that be delightful?"
BOOM! BOOM!
Before he could finish his monologue, two powerful auras shot toward the square like meteors.
It was Xia Chengyan and Zhiyin.
"Old geezer! Prepare to die!"
Xia Chengyan arrived screaming, his crimson-gold sword erupting with scorching radiance as he slashed at the roof.
Seeing Zhiyin following closely behind, a trace of surprise flashed in Qianji’s dark green eyes.
"Oh? Your puppet actually broke through to the Nascent Soul stage? How bizarre. A tool surpassing its master's realm... if I hadn't seen it with my own eyes, I would call it impossible."
Zhiyin’s face remained impassive, her clear, cold gaze fixed on the villain. "Was it you who dismantled Zhiyin Two?

Daoist Qianji let out a strange laugh. "Correct. That puppet was interesting; its core structure had some unique ideas. I never thought a backwater like the Southern Region could produce such puppetry. If I have the chance, I’d love to... dissect your techniques."
"Refining the living into dolls. Treating cultivators as raw materials." Zhiyin’s voice dropped an octave. "With you, there is nothing to discuss."
"Why are we talking to him?!" Xia Chengyan interrupted, vibrating with impatience. "Let's jump him! It’s a 4v1 gank! I’ve got a date with my Xiaozhu later, so let's wrap this up!"
BOOM!
The Prince transformed into a beam of golden light. His sword carried the momentum to boil seas and scorch the heavens as he led the charge.

A cold light flashed in Li Fuxi’s eyes. Man and sword became one, a beam of refined killing intent piercing straight at the enemy. Zhang Xian didn't hold back either, tossing a handful of expensive talismans to harass the villain from the flanks.
Facing a siege from three sides, Daoist Qianji didn't panic. He sneered.
"Hmph. Trying to bully the old with numbers? Little brats, I think you’ve forgotten who I am!"
He threw his arms wide.
WARP!
Space twisted violently! several figures exuding terrifying auras instantly teleported in front of him.
First, a middle-aged man with a rugged, resolute face stepped forward. He held a wrought-iron long spear.
CLANG!
The spear moved like a dragon, parrying Xia Chengyan’s crimson flame sword with impossible precision. The strike was heavy, filled with the bloody aura of a veteran general.
It was the Great Xia Dynasty's missing Grand General—Han Lie.
Second, an old man with crane-white hair and a youthful face drifted backward. He wore ancient robes and formed hand seals with blinding speed.

A complex star chart lit up beneath his feet. Countless starlight runes ascended, weaving into a massive net of light that sealed the sky above the square. A heavy, crushing pressure descended on the battlefield.
Li Fuxi’s heart sank. This was the former Head of Tianque Peak, the master of divination and formations—Perfected Being Star Concealment.
Suddenly, both Li Fuxi and Zhang Xian felt a lethal lock-on.
A third figure blurred toward them. The man raised both hands, firing two condensed, pure-gold finger beams straight at their foreheads.
The pressure contained within those fingers was undeniably Nascent Soul level, even if the movements were slightly stiff.
When Li Fuxi saw the face of her attacker, her entire body trembled. Her grip on her sword tightened until her knuckles turned white.
That face belonged to the man she revered as a father. Her mentor.
Perfected Being Wangchuan.
At the same time, the hulking puppet beside Daoist Qianji moved. It spread its massive palms.
HUMMMMM—
Waves of thick, earthen-yellow halos pulsed outward. Instantly, an impenetrable layer of [Profound Yellow] armor encased Qianji and his elite puppets.
