Little brats, I think you’ve forgotten who I am!"
He threw his arms wide.
WARP!
Space twisted violently! several figures exuding terrifying auras instantly teleported in front of him.
First, a middle-aged man with a rugged, resolute face stepped forward.
He held a wrought-iron long spear.
CLANG!
The spear moved like a dragon, parrying Xia Chengyan’s crimson flame sword with impossible precision.
The strike was heavy, filled with the bloody aura of a veteran general.
It was the Great Xia Dynasty's missing Grand General—Han Lie.
Second, an old man with crane-white hair and a youthful face drifted backward.
He wore ancient robes and formed hand seals with blinding speed.
A complex star chart lit up beneath his feet.
Countless starlight runes ascended, weaving into a massive net of light that sealed the sky above the square.
A heavy, crushing pressure descended on the battlefield.
Li Fuxi’s heart sank.
This was the former Head of Tianque Peak, the master of divination and formations—Perfected Being Star Concealment.
Suddenly, both Li Fuxi and Zhang Xian felt a lethal lock-on.
A third figure blurred toward them.
The man raised both hands, firing two condensed, pure-gold finger beams straight at their foreheads.
The pressure contained within those fingers was undeniably Nascent Soul level, even if the movements were slightly stiff.
When Li Fuxi saw the face of her attacker, her entire body trembled.
Her grip on her sword tightened until her knuckles turned white.
That face belonged to the man she revered as a father.
Her mentor.
Perfected Being Wangchuan.
At the same time, the hulking puppet beside Daoist Qianji moved.
It spread its massive palms.
HUMMMMM—
Waves of thick, earthen-yellow halos pulsed outward.
Instantly, an impenetrable layer of [Profound Yellow] armor encased Qianji and his elite puppets.

chapters.title: Chapter 166 Junior Sister, You’ve Grown Stronger
paragraphs: As Daoist Qianji spoke, several more formidable puppets stepped out of the void to flank him. His laughter grated against the stone ruins, filled with arrogant pride.

"I am a legion," he declared, spreading his arms. "I control a thousand puppets and enact ten thousand techniques. One man is enough to crush an entire Sect. Today, I will show you children the true Dao of Puppetry."

Li Fuxi didn't blink. She stared fixedly at the puppet of Master Wangchuan, which radiated a terrifying Nascent Soul aura despite its stiff movements. Behind it stood the towering figure of her Senior Brother, Wang Pan, channeling the [Profound Yellow Mountain-Suppressing Stele].
Killing intent boiled in her veins, so thick it was nearly tangible.

Zhang Xian sensed the sheer power radiating from her and inwardly nodded. Master has advanced to Dual Heavenly Spiritual Roots and broke through to the eighth level of Golden Core. She’s a completely different beast now.
He glanced at Zhiyin. "Supervisor Zhiyin, what’s the status of the other fronts?"

Zhiyin scanned the battlefield, her expression calm. "Stable. Elder Qing Shi and Long Zhi from the Spirit Ruins Sword Sect have breached the Imperial Mausoleum's outer perimeter and are assaulting the core. His Majesty and Lin Xiaozhu are commanding the center. We only need to focus on the enemy in front of us."
As the last syllable left her lips, her body blurred.
Fwip-fwip-fwip!

She split instantly into thirteen identical clones! Excluding her main body, Zhiyin One, the clones—numbered Two through Fourteen—were all peak Golden Core puppets. The fourteen figures scattered instantly, an invisible control field locking down the battlefield.
The puppet war was about to erupt.
Suddenly, the towering puppet of Wang Pan opened its mouth. The voice was low, muffled, and distorted, yet it carried a trace of eerie, heartbreaking familiarity.
"Junior Sister... you've grown stronger."
Li Fuxi froze.
Immediately after, the Nascent Soul-level puppet of Wangchuan slowly turned its head. Its empty eyes bored into Li Fuxi as it spoke in a halting, mechanical rasp.
"You... are... quite good..."
"Do not listen," Zhiyin warned sharply. "They are dead. Their Dao is extinguished. The Old Demon is using residual memory fragments to destabilize your mind."
Li Fuxi took a deep breath. When she spoke, her voice was colder than profound ice.
"I know."

Daoist Qianji let out a piercing cackle. "Destabilize? Please. I disdain such cheap tricks. I preserved their memories and combat instincts for optimization. It allows them to exert greater strength... and makes the game far more entertaining."

He glanced at the Wangchuan puppet with a look of genuine regret. "It's a pity about this material, though. The swordsman's soul was severely damaged before death. Incomplete. He can't unleash 100% of his original power. Otherwise, he would have been the perfect tool."
Zhang Xian took a deep breath, quickly assigning roles. "That Nascent Soul puppet was refined using the core I lost. He hasn't fully mastered it yet. Master and I will handle him and the big guy.
He turned to the others. "Zhiyin, Brother Xia—can you handle Qianji’s main body and his mob?"
"Easy money!" Xia Chengyan grinned, his fighting spirit blazing. He pointed his Crimson Flame Sword at the villain. "Old fart, get ready to meet your maker!"
Li Fuxi closed her eyes.
When she opened them a second later, the pain, hesitation, and grief were gone. All that remained was pure, crystalline resolve.
"This is why I came."
BOOM!

She launched herself forward, transforming into a streak of sword-light that tore through the air, charging fearlessly at Wangchuan. Zhang Xian followed close behind, wind element spiraling around him to match her speed.
The battlefield exploded into chaos.

On the left, Zhiyin's thirteen clones moved in a terrifyingly synchronized dance, intercepting the dozens of peak Golden Core puppets controlled by Qianji. It was a storm of precision versus brute force—shields clashed, spells detonated, and spiritual light blinded the eye.
On the right, Xia Chengyan and Zhiyin One dove straight for Daoist Qianji.

Qianji wasn't a frontline fighter, but his Third Stage Nascent Soul cultivation gave him deep reserves. He drifted like smoke through the ruins, dodging Xia Chengyan’s scorching strikes while multitasking like a supercomputer.
He commanded his elite puppets to intercept.

General Han Lie’s puppet spun his wrought-iron spear, his attacks heavy and sweeping, forcing Xia Chengyan to parry or be crushed. Meanwhile, the Star Concealment puppet laid down annoying starlight formations that slowed their movement and drained their qi.
"Damn it, stop running!" Xia Chengyan roared, his sword clashing with Han Lie’s spear. He and Zhiyin were locked in a high-speed dogfight, unable to pin down the slippery puppeteer.
In the center, the most intense duel unfolded.

Li Fuxi’s dual swords stabbed straight for Wangchuan’s brow. Her Dual Heavenly Spiritual Roots erupted at full power—Water imbued her strikes with bone-chilling cold, while Metal gave them unstoppable penetration.
The Wangchuan puppet moved stiffly, but his muscle memory was flawless. He had no sword, so he used his fingers.
Shing!
He thrust two fingers forward, and a condensed beam of golden sword qi shot out—the signature move of the Spirit Sword Peak, the [Heavenly Palace Azure Cloud Sword]!
CLANG!!!
Ice-blue sword light collided with golden sword qi.

Li Fuxi swayed but didn't retreat an inch. Her style shifted. She fused the dense, fluid agility of the [Cloud Mist Sword Scripture] with the majestic power of the [Heavenly Palace Azure Cloud Sword].
Her blade work became a masterpiece. One moment it was a churning sea of clouds, pervasive and formless; the next, it was a thunderbolt, heavy and unstoppable.

Zhang Xian watched, stunned. He had worried she would falter fighting her loved ones. Instead, she was channeling her grief into power. With peak Golden Core cultivation, she was fighting a Nascent Soul puppet to a standstill.
Master has grown up, Zhang Xian thought, feeling a surge of relief.
He turned his attention to his own target: the Wang Pan puppet.
But Wang Pan seemed to have learned his lesson.
Unlike their previous encounter where the earth-attribute puppet tanked everything face-first, this time, Wang Pan adopted an incredibly shameless "kite" strategy.
The moment Zhang Xian raised a Spirit Treasure, Wang Pan sprinted backward, maintaining a strict safety distance.
Zhang Xian tried to close the gap. Wang Pan ran.
Zhang Xian stopped. Wang Pan stopped, turned around, and chucked a [Profound Yellow Mountain-Suppressing Stele] at him from downtown to harass him, or jumped in to block a stray shot for Wangchuan.
"Mao Zedong tactics? Really?" Zhang Xian cursed. 'Enemy advances, we retreat; enemy retreats, we harass.'
It wasn't just Wang Pan. Zhang Xian realized with growing frustration that everyone was avoiding him.

Even Daoist Qianji, who was busy fighting the Prince, and the Wangchuan puppet locked in combat with Li Fuxi, would instinctively flinch and widen the gap whenever they sensed Zhang Xian getting too close.
They knew.
They knew he was a walking nuke who solved problems by detonating high-grade artifacts.
"Hey! You cowards!" Zhang Xian yelled, shaking a glowing talisman in the air. "Come fight me! Stop running!"

He had a backpack full of bombs and unlimited funds, but nobody wanted to play. He stood there, awkwardly chasing Wang Pan in circles while the rest of the battlefield raged in an epic clash of steel and magic.

chapters.title: Chapter 167 You’ve Done Really Well, Xi’er
paragraphs: Seizing a fleeting gap in Wangchuan's defense, Li Fuxi struck. Her spirit sword dissolved into a streak of biting frost, aiming straight for his heart. But Wang Pan’s support arrived in the blink of an eye; a heavy, earthen-yellow barrier of light instantly condensed before Wangchuan to intercept the blow.

The spirit sword slammed into the barrier, sending shards of ice exploding outward. The shield shuddered violently, a web of fractures instantly spreading across its surface. A cold, ruthless light erupted in Li Fuxi’s eyes. She held nothing back, pouring every ounce of her spiritual power into the blade until the tip shone with a blinding, piercing radiance.
CRACK!
Unable to withstand the pressure, the barrier shattered into motes of light.

The Wangchuan puppet raised his sword-fingers to block Li Fuxi’s lethal strike. On that stiff, artificial face, the corners of the mouth twitched, pulled upward with visible difficulty. A rough, distorted voice rasped from its throat, mimicking a tone from the past:
"You’ve done really well, Xi’er."
"You’ve worked hard all these years."
The voice carried a trace of warmth—a sickeningly perfect imitation of the real Wangchuan.
Li Fuxi’s hand trembled violently. But deep within her icy pupils, there was no hesitation, only a surge of profaned fury.
She did not withdraw. Instead, she drove the sword forward, channeling the full weight of her body and soul into the thrust.

The air around the blade instantly froze, crystallizing into countless shards of diamond-hard ice. More terrifying was the resonance between her chaotic emotions and her Dual Heavenly Spirit Roots. Above the plaza, the lead-gray clouds churned as if stirred by an invisible hand, and without warning, wisps of freezing rain began to drift down.
A phenomenon born of pure spiritual resonance!
Meanwhile, deep within the ruins of the Imperial Tomb at the far end of the Secret Realm.

The two Nascent Soul elders of the Lingxu Sword Sect, Qingshi and Long Zhi, combined their strength to blast open the final restriction. As the dust settled, they saw a figure clad in black robes, a pitch-black mask covering his face, sitting calmly beside a broken stone table.
He sat upright, motionless, as if he had been waiting for them for an eternity.
"You’ve come." His voice filtered through the mask—calm, even, yet carrying a chill that made the heart palpitate.

Far away in the center of the battlefield, Xia Xuanyin frowned the moment his gaze landed on the figure. He sensed a faint, almost imperceptible trace of Imperial Qi leaking from the man. Though it was buried under thick layers of demonic corruption, Xia Xuanyin—an Emperor himself—was acutely sensitive to the aura of a ruler.
"It’s him!" Xia Xuanyin understood instantly. This was the mad tyrant the Xuan Zhou team had encountered in the past—the Old Emperor who had not hesitated to sacrifice his entire dynasty for power.
Daoist Qingshi, sensing the dense, suffocating evil radiating from the man, felt his anger spike. "Evil creature! Was it you who slaughtered every living being in this realm?
The black-robed figure slowly stood up, letting out a sinister, rattling chuckle. "Slaughter? Hmph! They were my subjects. To offer their Life Essence for my grand ascension is their supreme glory!"
Xia Xuanyin’s voice cut through space like a blade of ice. "If I’m not mistaken, it wasn’t just this Secret Realm. The great world outside... that was once your kingdom too, wasn't it?"

"For this wretched power—neither human nor ghost—you sacrificed your entire nation. Hundreds of millions of subjects. Within that imperial city were countless descendants of your own bloodline! Do you possess even a shred of humanity?"

"Humanity?" The Black Venerable laughed as if he had heard the world's greatest absurdity. His voice rose to a shriek, trembling with insane obsession. "Emperor of Great Xia, you disappoint me! You hold the throne, yet you possess the bleeding heart of a woman!"

"If I had been given a few hundred more years... once I ruled the world, the entire five domains of the cultivation world would have prostrated at my feet! Mere mortal ants—if they die, they die. Their sacrifice is nothing but dust on the road to supreme hegemony!"
Long Zhi had no interest in debating a monster. She raised a jade-like hand and uttered a single, clear command. "Fall."
BOOM!
A bolt of purple lightning, thick as a water barrel, tore through the gloomy sky and crashed directly onto the black-robed figure’s head.

The Black Venerable did not dodge. His right hand shot up, palm churning with black mist, and he grabbed the lightning bolt mid-air. A piercing screech of tearing energy erupted as the black mist and violet thunder clashed violently.
The next second, the Black Venerable’s fingers clenched.
SNAP!
He crushed the violent thunderbolt with brute force, scattering the sparks into the wind.
Long Zhi’s eyes remained cold and clear. She exchanged a glance with Qingshi, and the two charged forward in unison. Their stance was clear: no more words. Only a fight to the death.
Xia Xuanyin and Lin Xiaozhu did not immediately join the fray. The Emperor’s gaze swept across the chaotic battlefield. The enemy's numbers were far greater than anticipated.

Beyond Daoist Qianji’s puppets, there were scores of cultivators like Jianchen—traitors corrupted by [Desire] who had actively defected. Among them were notorious Old Demons at the peak of the Golden Core realm. These were the true backbone of the Demon Nest.

He saw Lin Yinyin wielding a spirit sword that flowed with liquid light, fiercely battling an Old Demon skilled in poison. Her swordsmanship was agile and remarkably resilient. He saw Daoist Wangya, his sword momentum like a rainbow, suppressing several evil cultivators shrouded in blood-light. He saw Yun Wanqing surrounded by defensive artifacts, waving a crimson feather fan that scattered a sky full of burning plumes, holding her ground against two late-stage Golden Core enemies.

All thanks to Zhang Xian, Xia Xuanyin thought grimly. Without Zhang Xian pinpointing the Demon Nest’s location and bankrolling the alliance with massive resources, this battle would have been a catastrophe. The Demon Nest’s expansion speed was far beyond their worst nightmares.
But just as he surveyed the field, the situation shifted.
An insidious streak of dark blue sword light shot abruptly from the void behind Yun Wanqing. It was silent, swift, and aimed ruthlessly at her heart.
"Careful!" Xia Xuanyin reacted instantly.

The might of the Emperor erupted! Without moving his body, he pointed a finger into the air. A beam of condensed golden sword qi—arriving late but striking first—slashed precisely into the dark blue ambusher. The blue light shattered with a crisp ring.
Xia Xuanyin didn't stop. His left hand opened, fingers splayed, and he clawed at the empty air. "Get out here!"
It was as if an invisible mirror had been crushed. Space distorted violently, and a figure wearing a white mask was forcibly squeezed out of the void.
It was the White Venerable.

Yun Wanqing spun around, startled. When she saw the figure, and the familiar lingering intent of the Cloud Mist Sword Scripture, her body froze as if struck by lightning. Her eyes filled with disbelief and a deep, crushing despair.
Was it really Xuan Zhou? Zhen'er's father... he... he actually tried to kill me?

The White Venerable’s sneak attack had failed. The eyes beneath the mask were icy and annoyed. He ignored Yun Wanqing entirely, his figure flickering as he prepared to melt back into the shadows. As he moved, his hands flicked rapidly—several more sinister blue sword lights shot out like arrows, this time targeting Lin Yinyin in the distance.

"Despicable!" Daoist Wangya roared. He parried his own opponent with a heavy blow, then released his grip. His longsword flew out, transforming into a shocking rainbow that intercepted and annihilated the sword lights aimed at Lin Yinyin.
"Fellow Daoist Lin, I leave this area to you!" Xia Xuanyin’s voice trembled with suppressed rage. All three Nascent Soul demons had revealed themselves; he no longer had any reason to hold back.
He took a single step forward and vanished.

When he reappeared, he was already standing at the edge of the shadows where the White Venerable had faded. His terrified Divine Sense swept the void like a tsunami, instantly locking onto a faint ripple in space.
With a wave of his sleeve, Xia Xuanyin tore a jagged rift in reality and stepped into the void without hesitation, giving chase.

An insidious streak of dark blue sword light shot abruptly from the void behind Yun Wanqing.
It was silent, swift, and aimed ruthlessly at her heart.
"Careful!" Xia Xuanyin reacted instantly.
The might of the Emperor erupted!
Without moving his body, he pointed a finger into the air.
A beam of condensed golden sword qi—arriving late but striking first—slashed precisely into the dark blue ambusher.
The blue light shattered with a crisp ring.
Xia Xuanyin didn't stop.
His left hand opened, fingers splayed, and he clawed at the empty air.
"Get out here!"
It was as if an invisible mirror had been crushed.
Space distorted violently, and a figure wearing a white mask was forcibly squeezed out of the void.
It was the White Venerable.
Yun Wanqing spun around, startled.
When she saw the figure, and the familiar lingering intent of the Cloud Mist Sword Scripture, her body froze as if struck by lightning.
Her eyes filled with disbelief and a deep, crushing despair.
Was it really Xuan Zhou?
Zhen'er's father... he... he actually tried to kill me?
The White Venerable’s sneak attack had failed.
The eyes beneath the mask were icy and annoyed.
He ignored Yun Wanqing entirely, his figure flickering as he prepared to melt back into the shadows.
As he moved, his hands flicked rapidly—several more sinister blue sword lights shot out like arrows, this time targeting Lin Yinyin in the distance.
"Despicable!" Daoist Wangya roared.
He parried his own opponent with a heavy blow, then released his grip.
His longsword flew out, transforming into a shocking rainbow that intercepted and annihilated the sword lights aimed at Lin Yinyin.
"Fellow Daoist Lin, I leave this area to you!" Xia Xuanyin’s voice trembled with suppressed rage.
All three Nascent Soul demons had revealed themselves; he no longer had any reason to hold back.
He took a single step forward and vanished.
When he reappeared, he was already standing at the edge of the shadows where the White Venerable had faded.
His terrified Divine Sense swept the void like a tsunami, instantly locking onto a faint ripple in space.
With a wave of his sleeve, Xia Xuanyin tore a jagged rift in reality and stepped into the void without hesitation, giving chase.

chapters.title: Chapter 168 Killing His Wife to Prove the Dao
paragraphs: Yun Wanqing snapped out of her daze, the last glimmer of hope in her eyes finally extinguished. Her knuckles turned white as she gripped the Red Feather Fan, her voice trembling but resolute.
"We’re going too!"
Daoist Wangya nodded grimly. The two of them followed closely, stepping into the closing spatial rift.
Space warped and shifted, depositing them in a desolate wilderness.

Not far ahead, a high-speed chase was unfolding. Xia Xuanyin was hunting down the fleeing black-robed figure, his speed clearly superior. As he flew, the Emperor relentlessly tossed out golden, pestle-shaped artifacts.
Each golden spike that fell acted like a divine anchor, nailing itself into the void and locking down the surrounding space.

The White Venerable’s movement technique was bizarre and ghostly, but under the layers of spatial confinement, he was slowing down. He tried to take another step, but his figure merely flickered, unable to truly pierce the blockade.
"You have nowhere left to run!" Xia Xuanyin’s icy voice rang out like a final judgment.
The White Venerable slowly turned around. His white mask faced the three pursuers, the eyes behind it cold and indifferent.
Yun Wanqing steadied herself, her gaze fixed intently on him. "Take off your mask."
The White Venerable remained silent for a moment before his voice filtered through the mask, dripping with disdain. "You? You aren't worthy."
Daoist Wangya took a deep breath, suppressing the turmoil in his heart. "Fellow Daoist, stop this. Turn back now. Perhaps it isn't too late."
"Turn back?" The White Venerable let out a self-mocking sneer. "Save your hypocrisy, Wangya. After all these years, you’re still absolute trash."

Xia Xuanyin didn't waste words. The Imperial Aura around him surged like a physical tide, a crushing pressure descending upon the White Venerable like a falling mountain. The air itself seemed to solidify under the weight of his authority.
Yun Wanqing stared at the figure—so familiar, yet so terrifyingly alien. Seeing the inhuman indifference in his eyes, the last shred of fantasy in her heart shattered.
She slowly raised the Red Feather Fan, her voice terrifyingly calm.
"No need for words. Let our strength decide the truth. Whoever he used to be... it doesn't matter anymore."
Her tone was crisp and frigid. "He is nothing but a puppet dancing on the strings of [Desire]."
Before her voice could even fade—

A vicious glint exploded in the White Venerable’s eyes. Ignoring Xia Xuanyin and Wangya entirely, he launched himself forward like a specter. A pitch-black water sword materialized in his hand, radiating bone-chilling killing intent as he thrust it straight at Yun Wanqing’s throat.
The strike was ruthless, decisive, and devoid of hesitation. He intended to erase the woman he had once vowed to cherish!
"Watch out!"
Daoist Wangya’s pupils constricted. Being closest to Yun Wanqing, he reacted on instinct, flashing forward to intercept the blow with his own blade.
CLANG!
The water sword slammed into Wangya’s defense, erupting with violent force. Wangya grunted, the impact sending him staggering back several steps.

But the White Venerable didn't stop. Failing to kill in one hit, he didn't retreat but advanced! With a flick of his wrist, his blade snaked around Wangya’s guard, stabbing once more toward Yun Wanqing’s heart.
The speed was blinding, the intent pure ice.
"Audacity!"
Xia Xuanyin roared. He stepped in, the Imperial Jade Seal in his hand smashing down to deflect the sword and shielding Yun Wanqing behind him.
"To be so utterly devoid of humanity," Xia Xuanyin growled, his face dark. "I intend to see exactly what kind of face hides behind that mask!"
Meanwhile, back at the chaotic plaza.

The duel between Li Fuxi and Wangchuan had reached a fever pitch. Every collision between her twin spirit swords and his golden sword qi triggered shockwaves that plowed deep furrows into the stone floor.
As the battle raged, Zhang Xian noticed something disturbing. Wisps of white mist were beginning to rise from the ground, actively merging into Daoist Qianji and his puppets.
"Life Essence!"

Zhang Xian’s expression tightened. This was the pure energy distilled from the stolen lifespans of mortals. The enemy was using it to rapidly replenish their spirit and repair damage. No wonder they could fight with such endless stamina.
However, Zhang Xian wasn't exactly poor.
His gaze swept across the battlefield. He saw Xia Chengyan locked in a stalemate with Daoist Qianji’s main body, a chaotic mix of golden flames and black puppet qi exploding between them.
Without hesitation, Zhang Xian pulled a jade bottle from his Storage Ring. With a flick of his finger, the bottle shot toward the prince like a meteor.
"Brother Xia, catch!"
Xia Chengyan, in the middle of parrying a strike, snatched the bottle out of the air. He swept it with his Divine Sense and nearly fell out of the sky.
The bottle was stuffed to the brim with Earth-Grade Spirit Recovery Pills. Every single one was perfect, round, and glowing with potency.
"Holy sh*t!"
Xia Chengyan couldn't help but curse out loud.

He was one of the Central Continent’s Ten Outstanding Youths! A core disciple of the Tianyuan Alliance! The Crown Prince of the Great Xia Dynasty! And even he usually only popped High-Grade pills sparingly.
Who the hell hands out Earth-Grade pills by the bottle? Compared to this guy, the Prince felt like a country bumpkin who had never seen real money.
"You're a badass, Brother Zhang!"
Xia Chengyan’s morale skyrocketed. With this bottle, he could grind the old bastard Qianji down until the end of time. He popped a pill into his mouth immediately.
BOOM.
Spiritual power rushed through his meridians like a flooding river, instantly refilling his reserves.
On the other side of the plaza, the melee between Zhiyin and Qianji’s puppet army was even more brutal. Puppets from both sides were being torn apart in a grinder of metal and flesh.
Zhang Xian watched calmly. Whenever one of Zhiyin’s clones was destroyed, he would swoop in to retrieve the core—waste not, want not.
But whenever he saw one of Qianji’s "flesh-and-blood" puppets get destroyed, he immediately summoned a bolt of lightning to vaporize the remains into ash, preventing any recovery.
Seeing the enemy numbers dwindling but still fighting with suicidal ferocity, Zhang Xian made a move.
Four puppet clones—identical to his main body—materialized instantly.
"Go!"
Zhang Xian gave a low shout. The four clones scattered like ghosts. As they moved, their hands blurred, tossing dozens of talismans into the air.
It looked like celestial maidens scattering flowers—except the flowers were high-explosive lightning talismans.
In an instant, thunderclouds choked the sky above the plaza. A forest of lightning bolts crashed down, hammering the enemy puppets.
"Hmph, cheap parlor tricks!" Daoist Qianji sneered, dodging Xia Chengyan’s attacks while micromanaging his puppets to evade the lightning. "Did you think my puppets were sitting ducks?"
Zhang Xian ignored him. He just kept making it rain.
Finally, one of the flesh-and-blood puppets showed a microscopic hesitation while dodging.
That tiny opening was enough. A bolt of lightning grazed its shoulder.
ZZZT!
Sparks exploded, and the puppet’s body seized up, paralyzed by the electric shock.
"Not good!" Daoist Qianji’s pupils shrank.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
Three thicker bolts of lightning locked onto the paralyzed target instantly, hammering down with pinpoint precision.
"Wang Pan!" Qianji shouted urgently.
The massive Wang Pan puppet reacted with incredible speed, conjuring a thick, earthy-yellow light shield over the frozen puppet’s head.
But he was a step too slow.
The first two bolts shattered the hastily formed shield. The third bolt slammed into the puppet without resistance.
Then came the fourth. Then the fifth.
Under the relentless bombardment, the Golden Core peak puppet didn't just break—it was vaporized, leaving not even a speck of dust behind.

chapters.title: Chapter 169 You Might Profit, But I Never Lose
paragraphs: "Hahaha!"

Zhang Xian threw his head back and laughed, shouting at the ashen-faced Daoist Qianji. "Old ghoul! You traded a half-wrecked puppet for over a dozen of my Earth-Grade Thunder Talismans. You made a killing on that exchange! Pure profit!"
Beneath his mask, Daoist Qianji’s mouth twitched uncontrollably.

These weren't simple wood and metal constructs. These flesh-and-blood puppets were refined from the mutilated remains of powerful cultivators. The higher the cultivation realm, the rarer the materials and the longer the refinement process. Losing even a single Golden Core peak puppet caused him physical heartache!
But Zhang Xian was the type to press his advantage until the bitter end. His gaze, sharp as lightning, instantly locked onto another puppet—one that had just lost a leg to Zhiyin’s blade.
"Here, have another!"
Whoosh! Whoosh!
Dozens more Earth-Grade Thunder Talismans flew out as if they were trash paper. The sky lit up with blinding arcs of electricity, instantly locking onto the crippled target.
Under Daoist Qianji’s horrified gaze, another precious flesh-and-blood puppet was reduced to ash.
"Look at that! You won again!" Zhang Xian jeered.
"You bastard!" Daoist Qianji roared, his composure finally cracking.
Not far away, the battlefield shifted abruptly.

A dense, earthy-yellow light shield materialized around Li Fuxi, forming a solid spherical cage that trapped her inside. The barrier flowed with heavy energy, completely isolating her from the outside world.

Simultaneously, the Wangchuan puppet—which had been locked in a fierce duel with Li Fuxi—froze. It immediately pivoted, abandoning her to charge straight at Zhang Xian, its golden sword aura swelling with lethal intent.
Inside the cage, Li Fuxi slashed furiously at the barrier. Her spirit sword struck the walls, rippling the energy but failing to break through.

Outside, the tall, hulking figure of the Wang Pan puppet stood with both palms pressed against the shield. He was pouring endless earth-attribute spiritual power into the structure, maintaining its impregnable defense.
Slowly, his metallic face turned toward Li Fuxi inside the barrier. His throat worked, emitting a raspy, mechanical voice that somehow carried a terrifyingly familiar warmth.
"Little Junior Sister... just rest for a while."
The words traversed two hundred years of time and slammed into Li Fuxi’s heart like a sledgehammer.

For a split second, she was back at Spirit Sword Peak, a timid young girl who had just joined the sect. Whenever she followed her Eldest Senior Brother and Second Senior Sister down the mountain for training, whenever danger loomed, Eldest Senior Brother would always smile gently.
"Little Junior Sister, you rest for a while."
Then, he would cast this exact shield over her, standing tall to protect her from the world.
The memories surged like a tidal wave. But instead of warmth, they brought a scalding, overwhelming fury.
"AHHH!"
Li Fuxi let out a shriek of grief and indignation. Her spirit sword erupted with blinding blue light as she slashed wildly at the cage, hacking at the memory of her brother's protection.
On the other side, facing the sudden ambush of the Wangchuan puppet, Zhang Xian didn't panic. He grinned.
"Finally, a decent sparring partner."

He spun on his heel, a longsword appearing in his hand, flowing with spiritual light. As he raised the blade, his stance shifted. It carried the ethereal agility of the Cloud Mist Sword Scripture and the majestic, crushing weight of the Heavenly Palace Azure Cloud Sword.
It was the exact fusion sword art Li Fuxi had spent days in seclusion trying to perfect.
"What?"

Trapped inside the shield, Li Fuxi caught a glimpse of Zhang Xian’s movements. Her heart skipped a beat. She had poured her blood and sweat into merging those two great arts and had only just scratched the surface.
Zhang Xian had seen it once. And he had already mastered it?
Clang! Clang! Clang!
Sparks flew as Zhang Xian and the Wangchuan puppet clashed, fighting to a standstill.
"Grandmaster, are you testing your grand-disciple's skills?" Zhang Xian stared straight into the dead eyes of the Wangchuan puppet, his mouth running as fast as his sword.
The puppet remained silent, its movements becoming stiffer and more mechanical.
"Tsk!" Zhang Xian curled his lip. "You were chatty enough with Xi'er. Why the silent treatment for your most outstanding grand-disciple? That’s blatant favoritism!"
Nearby, the Wang Pan puppet ignored the chaos. He kept his hands on the shield, continuing his eerie, earnest conversation with the trapped Li Fuxi.
"Little Junior Sister, how is Second Senior Sister doing? Why haven't I seen her?"
"It’s been so long. Back then, you were just a little Foundation Establishment girl."
"Did you practice diligently yesterday? No slacking off?"
"Did you practice diligently yesterday? No slacking off?"
The repetition struck Li Fuxi’s mind like a physical blow.
Her body stiffened. She looked through the translucent barrier at the face of her Eldest Senior Brother. A chill unlike anything she had ever felt crawled up her spine.

The memory of the morning assemblies at Spirit Sword Peak flashed before her eyes. Eldest Senior Brother Wang Pan, always smiling, walking down the line to inspect her and Second Senior Sister. His first question was always the same.
And she and Second Senior Sister would always blush and shout at the top of their lungs: "No!!"
Then they would train until they dropped.
"How is Spirit Sword Peak now?" The puppet continued, stuck in its loop of care.
"Enough!" Li Fuxi screamed.
The Wang Pan puppet paused, its head tilting slightly. "Hmm?"
It was the first time she had responded to him.
"I SAID ENOUGH!!"

Li Fuxi’s roar erupted like a dormant volcano. The power of her Dual Heavenly Spirit Roots ignited completely. The blue light on her blade intensified tenfold, and a storm of soul-freezing frost exploded outward from her core.
CRACK! CRACK!

The supposedly indestructible [Profound Yellow Mountain-Suppressing Boulder] shield began to fracture. The metallic arms of the Wang Pan puppet, still pressed against the barrier, shattered inch by inch under the extreme cold and violent sword intent, turning into a cloud of ice crystals.
BOOM!
Li Fuxi shattered the cage and stepped out, looking like a descending Goddess of Ice and Snow.
She gazed at the broken, mutilated puppet of Wang Pan. Her eyes held a storm of complex emotions—reluctance, pain, grief—but they eventually settled into a clear, icy resolve.
"Eldest Senior Brother..."
She looked at the puppet, but her gaze seemed to focus on something far, far away.
"Spirit Sword Peak is doing very well. I’ve taken in a few disciples. They are far more outstanding than we ever were."
She paused, as if bidding a final farewell to a lifetime of memories.
"You can rest in peace now."
With those words, her spirit sword transformed into a pillar of absolute zero light, piercing through heaven and earth to engulf the Wang Pan puppet. The terrifying cold froze time itself.
The puppet—along with the residual flesh, blood, and metallic bones inside it—disintegrated into glittering dust, vanishing into nothingness.
Li Fuxi didn't pause for even a breath. She spun around, her sword edge turning toward the Wangchuan puppet battling Zhang Xian.
"Kill!"
The Wangchuan puppet was already struggling to match Zhang Xian. With Li Fuxi joining the fray, it was instantly pushed to the brink of collapse.
Just then, a streak of light cut across the horizon.
Lin Xiaozhu arrived, drifting gracefully atop a Bagua array disk.
"Xiaozhu!" Xia Chengyan shouted, his spirits lifting. "I’m almost done here! How did it go on your end?"
"The two Nascent Soul seniors of the Lingxu Sword Sect have personally slain the Black Venerable. The demon’s minions have been purged."

Before her sentence ended, she swooped down from the array disk like a diving swan. Her hand flicked out, launching a profound talisman seal that stamped directly onto the Star Concealment puppet lurking on the perimeter of the formation.
The Star Concealment puppet froze instantly, as if its strings had been cut, and crashed to the ground.
Lin Xiaozhu’s arrival was the final straw.

Daoist Qianji’s face darkened to the color of charcoal. He glanced at the few remaining flesh-and-blood puppets on the field, then at the Wangchuan puppet being systematically dismantled by Li Fuxi and Zhang Xian.
A flash of intense financial agony crossed his eyes.
"Hmph! I will remember the 'gift' you gave me today!" Daoist Qianji barked.
He waved his sleeve violently.
Whoosh! Whoosh!
Invisible threads tightened, and the remaining puppets were instantly sucked into his sleeves. The Wangchuan puppet was yanked backward uncontrollably, retreating into the void.

Why the silent treatment for your most outstanding grand-disciple?
That’s blatant favoritism!"
Nearby, the Wang Pan puppet ignored the chaos.
He kept his hands on the shield, continuing his eerie, earnest conversation with the trapped Li Fuxi.
"Little Junior Sister, how is Second Senior Sister doing?
Why haven't I seen her?"
"It’s been so long.
Back then, you were just a little Foundation Establishment girl."
"Did you practice diligently yesterday?
No slacking off?"
"Did you practice diligently yesterday?
No slacking off?"
The repetition struck Li Fuxi’s mind like a physical blow.
Her body stiffened.
She looked through the translucent barrier at the face of her Eldest Senior Brother.
A chill unlike anything she had ever felt crawled up her spine.
The memory of the morning assemblies at Spirit Sword Peak flashed before her eyes.
Eldest Senior Brother Wang Pan, always smiling, walking down the line to inspect her and Second Senior Sister.
His first question was always the same.
And she and Second Senior Sister would always blush and shout at the top of their lungs: "No!!"
Then they would train until they dropped.
"How is Spirit Sword Peak now?" The puppet continued, stuck in its loop of care.
"Enough!" Li Fuxi screamed.
The Wang Pan puppet paused, its head tilting slightly.
"Hmm?"
It was the first time she had responded to him.
"I SAID ENOUGH!!"
Li Fuxi’s roar erupted like a dormant volcano.
The power of her Dual Heavenly Spirit Roots ignited completely.
The blue light on her blade intensified tenfold, and a storm of soul-freezing frost exploded outward from her core.
CRACK!
CRACK!
The supposedly indestructible [Profound Yellow Mountain-Suppressing Boulder] shield began to fracture.
The metallic arms of the Wang Pan puppet, still pressed against the barrier, shattered inch by inch under the extreme cold and violent sword intent, turning into a cloud of ice crystals.
BOOM!
Li Fuxi shattered the cage and stepped out, looking like a descending Goddess of Ice and Snow.
She gazed at the broken, mutilated puppet of Wang Pan.
Her eyes held a storm of complex emotions—reluctance, pain, grief—but they eventually settled into a clear, icy resolve.
"Eldest Senior Brother..."
She looked at the puppet, but her gaze seemed to focus on something far, far away.
"Spirit Sword Peak is doing very well.
I’ve taken in a few disciples.
They are far more outstanding than we ever were."
She paused, as if bidding a final farewell to a lifetime of memories.
"You can rest in peace now."
With those words, her spirit sword transformed into a pillar of absolute zero light, piercing through heaven and earth to engulf the Wang Pan puppet.
The terrifying cold froze time itself.
The puppet—along with the residual flesh, blood, and metallic bones inside it—disintegrated into glittering dust, vanishing into nothingness.
Li Fuxi didn't pause for even a breath.
She spun around, her sword edge turning toward the Wangchuan puppet battling Zhang Xian.
"Kill!"
The Wangchuan puppet was already struggling to match Zhang Xian.
With Li Fuxi joining the fray, it was instantly pushed to the brink of collapse.
Just then, a streak of light cut across the horizon.
Lin Xiaozhu arrived, drifting gracefully atop a Bagua array disk.
"Xiaozhu!" Xia Chengyan shouted, his spirits lifting.
"I’m almost done here!
How did it go on your end?"
"The two Nascent Soul seniors of the Lingxu Sword Sect have personally slain the Black Venerable.
The demon’s minions have been purged."
Before her sentence ended, she swooped down from the array disk like a diving swan.
Her hand flicked out, launching a profound talisman seal that stamped directly onto the Star Concealment puppet lurking on the perimeter of the formation.
The Star Concealment puppet froze instantly, as if its strings had been cut, and crashed to the ground.
Lin Xiaozhu’s arrival was the final straw.
Daoist Qianji’s face darkened to the color of charcoal.
He glanced at the few remaining flesh-and-blood puppets on the field, then at the Wangchuan puppet being systematically dismantled by Li Fuxi and Zhang Xian.
A flash of intense financial agony crossed his eyes.
"Hmph!
I will remember the 'gift' you gave me today!" Daoist Qianji barked.
He waved his sleeve violently.
Whoosh!
Whoosh!
Invisible threads tightened, and the remaining puppets were instantly sucked into his sleeves.
The Wangchuan puppet was yanked backward uncontrollably, retreating into the void.

chapters.title: Chapter 170 He Was Just a Puppet After All
paragraphs: "Trying to run?"
A cold light erupted in Li Fuxi’s eyes. A blade of condensed sword qi tore through the void, striking with pinpoint accuracy at the invisible threads connecting Daoist Qianji to the Wangchuan puppet.
SNAP.
A crisp sound echoed, like a lute string breaking under tension.
Daoist Qianji’s figure swayed slightly. He shot a venomous glare at Li Fuxi, then wasted no more time.
BANG!
His entire body detonated into a cloud of thick blood mist. The mist churned and contracted, drilling into a spatial rift that split open silently before vanishing without a trace.
With Qianji’s escape, the final thread of power sustaining the Wangchuan puppet was severed.
The puppet instantly froze. Eerie black flames erupted silently across its body, rapidly carbonizing the flesh and metal.

In the final moment before he turned to ash, his hollow eyes seemed to shift. He looked at Li Fuxi, standing just inches away. His lips moved with agonizing difficulty, as if trying to form words, but no sound came out.
Li Fuxi stared blankly as the familiar figure dissolved into the black fire.

The flames died out, leaving only a scorched, blackened sphere on the ground. It let out a metallic clang as it settled—it was precisely the special puppet core Zhang Xian had "lost" earlier to track the enemy.
Zhang Xian stepped forward and silently picked it up.
Xia Chengyan sheathed his sword, staring at the spot where Qianji had vanished. He couldn't help but curse.
"Motherf*cker, that guy can run. Puppeteers are such a pain in the ass to kill. I bet that wasn't even his real body just now."
Realizing Zhiyin was standing right there, he coughed awkwardly. "Uh, Fellow Daoist Zhiyin, I didn't mean you. You're cool."
"It is fine." Zhiyin’s expression remained calm.

With a thought, countless palm-sized Zhiyin clones surged out like a tide, beginning to methodically sweep the battlefield for loot and debris. One of the mini-Zhiyins fluttered over to Zhang Xian, extending a pair of tiny hands.
Zhang Xian smiled and placed the retrieved puppet core into her hands.
He surveyed the ravaged plaza, watching the dust settle. "Did they catch the White Venerable?" he asked Lin Xiaozhu.
"His Majesty the Emperor has trapped him in a formation," Lin Xiaozhu replied. "We have the absolute advantage."
Zhang Xian looked at Li Fuxi beside him. "Master, I’m going to go check on them."
Li Fuxi nodded, her voice heavy with fatigue. "Go. I will stay here and help clean up."
Zhang Xian summoned his sword and took to the air. Following the trail of Xia Xuanyin’s powerful aura, he soon arrived at a desolate plain on the outskirts of the Imperial Tomb.
The scene below was unexpected.
Xia Xuanyin, Daoist Wangya, and Yun Wanqing stood in a triangle formation, surrounding a thoroughly wretched figure.

It was the White Venerable. His black robes were soaked in blood. chaotic black and white energies coiled around him, trying desperately to knit his wounds, but his aura had withered to the breaking point. He was an arrow at the end of its flight.

But what made Zhang Xian’s heart tighten was the state of the attackers. Xia Xuanyin and Wangya were calm and composed. Only Yun Wanqing looked disheveled—her hair was messy, and there were several distinct tears on her snow-white sleeves, revealing faint bloodstains.
She was the only one injured!
Xuan Zhou actually attacked Yun Wanqing?
Zhang Xian was genuinely surprised. In the memory fragments of Jianchen, Xuan Zhou possessed an unshakeable obsession with his wife and daughter.
Did I cuckold him so hard he completely snapped? Is this some twisted 'Kill the Wife to Prove the Dao' mental breakdown?
Zhang Xian dove down, landing beside Yun Wanqing. "Are you alright?"
"I’m fine," Yun Wanqing whispered, pursing her lips.

Throughout the battle, the White Venerable had ignored the Emperor and Wangya, focusing all his manic rage on Yun Wanqing. Every move was ruthless, filled with a heaven-toppling hatred. Although he wore a mask, she had recognized his movement techniques and his gaze.
He was Xuan Zhou.
Daoist Wangya looked at the dying White Venerable, then glanced at the heartbroken Yun Wanqing. His eyes filled with conflict and pity.

"White Venerable," Wangya called out, his voice carrying a plea. "Black Venerable and Qianji have fallen. You’ve lost! If you are truly controlled by [Desire] and still have a shred of consciousness, surrender! We can find a way to separate the corruption—"
"Separate?"
The White Venerable jerked his head up, interrupting him. Beneath the mask, his mouth curled into a mocking sneer. His voice was hoarse and deranged.
"This Venerable is [Desire]! What is there to separate? Hahaha!"

His laughter was cut short by a sudden explosion of ferocious light in his eyes. It was the final burst of vitality before death—a huiguangfanzhao. Ignoring the Emperor and Wangya, he dragged his broken body forward, radiating a tragic, suicidal intent as he charged straight at Zhang Xian with a pitch-black water sword.
Zhang Xian’s eyes narrowed. He instantly raised his sword to block.
CLANG!
The blades collided, ringing clearly across the plain.
Simultaneously, Xia Xuanyin smashed the Imperial Jade Seal down toward the White Venerable’s back.
The White Venerable didn't dodge. He didn't even try to defend. He took the Emperor's full-force blow directly on his spine.
PFFT!
A fountain of blood mixed with black threads sprayed from his mouth. But instead of collapsing, his momentum increased.

Using the force of the blow, he lunged closer to Zhang Xian. In that instant, a giant net woven from countless black threads exploded from his body, descending to trap both Zhang Xian and Yun Wanqing.
It was a mutual destruction attack.
Buzz!

The [Orange Heart Pendants] on both Zhang Xian’s and Yun Wanqing’s chests instantly erupted with soft, warm yellow light. Simultaneously, their high-tier defensive artifacts activated, layering shield after shield around them.
The black net slammed into the paid-for protection, sizzling and dissolving with a piercing corrosive sound.
Seizing the momentary opening, Zhang Xian thrust his Water Spirit Sword forward.
A curtain of condensed, impossibly pure water surged like an inverted heavenly river, smashing into the White Venerable’s chest and piercing him through.
CRACK!
A corner of the white mask shattered.
But beneath the mask... there was no face.
There was no Xuan Zhou. Only a blurry, writhing mass of greyish-white mist, formless and shifting.
The White Venerable’s body stiffened. His eyes—filled with venom and madness—were locked onto Zhang Xian’s face. Then, slowly, they shifted to Yun Wanqing standing behind him.
The gaze held an indescribable complexity—Hatred? Unwillingness? Regret?
Then, the light in those eyes faded rapidly.
A gust of wind blew across the plain. The stiffened body crumbled like dried sand, turning into ash and drifting away on the breeze.
Clatter.

The only thing left was a fragment of the white mask, which fell to the ground. Alongside it, a dim Golden Core, tainted with black and white threads, rolled out. Inside the translucent core, a tiny, curled-up phantom could faintly be seen.
A second later, the Golden Core disintegrated into dust, leaving no trace behind.
"It’s over."
Daoist Wangya looked at the lonely mask fragment on the ground and let out a long, heavy sigh. His voice was filled with exhaustion and relief.

"He wasn't Xuan Zhou. I believe that even if Xuan Zhou fell into the demonic path, he would never raise a sword against his own wife. That thing... was just a [Desire] puppet possessing Xuan Zhou’s memories."
Yun Wanqing stood quietly, saying nothing.
She walked over to Zhang Xian, reached out, and gently brushed the dust and bloodstains from his robes. Her movements were soft, focused, and intimate.
Zhang Xian looked up at the sky.
Unnoticed, the lead-gray clouds that had shrouded the Secret Realm for so long had finally dispersed. A single ray of warm sunlight pierced through the gloom, spilling gold onto the scarred earth.

chapters.title: Chapter 171 I Acknowledge You as My Big Brother
paragraphs: It was over. The demons had fallen, the Nest had crumbled, and the sun was shining once again.
Yet, a strange, lingering unease gnawed at Zhang Xian’s heart.

It had gone too smoothly. So smoothly, in fact, that it felt wrong. The Black Venerable had been slain by the Lingxu Sword Sect. Daoist Qianji had fled. The White Venerable had self-destructed. A Demon Nest that had been painstakingly built over hundreds of years had collapsed in a single day like a house of cards.
Zhang Xian swept his gaze over the sunlit ruins, suspicion growing in his mind. But where was the flaw? He couldn't put his finger on it.
Eventually, he shook his head with a self-deprecating chuckle. Maybe I’ve just read too many web novels. I’m so used to plot twists that a straightforward victory feels unnatural.
"I’m probably overthinking it," he muttered, tightening his grip on Yun Wanqing’s slightly cool hand.
The brutal battle that had raged for an entire day finally drew to a close.

The Southern Region’s Righteous Alliance had launched a thunderous raid on the Demon Nest and achieved total victory. Thousands of demonic minions were either slaughtered or captured. The core forces that had entrenched themselves here for centuries were uprooted in twenty-four hours.

Led by Lin Xiaozhu, a team of cultivators proficient in divination and arrays swept through the Secret Realm and the desolate minor worlds surrounding it. They left no stone unturned, eradicating the last pockets of resistance and capturing nearly a hundred remnants who still retained a shred of sanity.

At the edge of the plaza, on a hastily erected Clear Heart Platform, countless captured cultivators knelt prostrate on the stone. Righteous elders sat in a circle around them, chanting incantations in an attempt to purify their souls and strip away the corruption of [Desire].
"Ugh... Grahhh!"
"Kill... Kill them all! It’s all mine!"
"Hehe... Beauties... mine..."
Some captives immediately let out bestial roars. Their eyes turned bloodshot, and black mist churned around their bodies as they struggled against their magical restraints like rabid animals.
Lin Xiaozhu watched with an impassive expression. She stepped up to a captive deeply entrenched in madness and fired a Clear Heart rune into his chest.
The man convulsed violently. The red light in his eyes faded for a split second, only to be replaced by an expression of even greater agony and confusion before the madness took hold again.
Lin Xiaozhu shook her head. "The [Desire] has taken root in his marrow. His Golden Core is corroded beyond repair. There is no saving him."
Her words sealed the fate of these wretches. They were slaves to their own cravings, lost in self-woven illusions. Their bodies were nothing more than walking corpses.
Other captives reacted differently to the baptism.
Some froze as if struck by lightning. Their bodies trembled violently, tears and mucus streaming down their faces as they let out heart-wrenching wails.
"I was wrong! I was wrong! I’m not human! Please, just kill me!"

It was as if they had woken from a long, terrible nightmare, crushed by the weight of their sins. Others clutched their heads and rolled on the ground, screaming in sheer psychological agony. These were the ones whose corruption was lighter; their eyes still held fear and a desperate will to survive.

"Take them away and guard them strictly," Xia Xuanyin ordered, his voice carrying the unquestionable authority of an Emperor. "When we return to the Southern Capital, they will be handed over to the Ministry of Justice and the sect elders for interrogation. We will uncover the cause of their fall and the extent of their crimes before passing judgment!"
Two days later.
The flying boats of the various sects began to rise into the sky, embarking on the journey home.
Li Fuxi was clearly in a foul mood. Since the battle ended, she had locked herself in her quiet room, refusing to see anyone.

In contrast, Lin Yinyin was buzzing with excitement. Her face was flushed as she dragged Zhang Xian around, chattering non-stop. This was her first large-scale war. She had gone from nervousness to the thrill of combat, and now to the joy of victory. Her mental state had undergone a baptism by fire, and her cultivation showed faint signs of improvement.
Yun Wanqing, however, had shed her usual armor of toughness. She buried herself in Zhang Xian’s arms and cried until she had no tears left.

The complete dissipation of the White Venerable had severed the last thread connecting her to the past. The resolute killing intent he showed, and the tainted Golden Core turning to ash, told her clearly that the man she had waited two hundred years for was gone.
What remained had been nothing but a monster twisted by [Desire], wearing her husband's memories like a skin suit.
Zhang Xian held her silently, feeling the tremors in her body until she exhausted herself and fell into a deep sleep.
He tiptoed out of the room, closing the door softly behind him.
As he turned into the corridor, he saw Xia Chengyan leaning against the wall, a meaningful, roguish grin plastered on his face.
"Yo, Brother Zhang. Fancy meeting you here."
Zhang Xian opened his mouth to explain, but Xia Chengyan waved him off with a knowing look.
"Say less, bro. I know exactly what went down in there." He threw a heavy arm around Zhang Xian’s shoulder. "Come on, let’s go to my cabin. Have a seat, drink some tea."
Zhang Xian smiled helplessly and let himself be dragged along.
Inside the Prince's cabin, Lin Xiaozhu was sitting primly by a tea table. In front of her were two transparent jade bottles.
One contained a wisp of black energy that writhed like a living parasite, emitting a cold, sinister aura—a remnant of [Desire]. The other held a few drops of white liquid radiating rich Life Essence.
She was fully focused on manipulating a delicate array disk, projecting complex holograms of light to analyze the substances.
Xia Chengyan poured Zhang Xian a cup of spirit tea, then pulled out a familiar object. It was the bottle of Earth-Grade Spirit Recovery Pills Zhang Xian had tossed him during the fight.
"Brother Zhang, here. I’m returning this treasure to you."

Before Zhang Xian could speak, the Prince continued. "Xiaozhu and I have to head back to the Central Continent immediately, so we won't be saying goodbye to the others. Meeting you on this trip to the Southern Region... it’s been a real pleasure, man."

"The thing is, the 'Seven Emotions Evil Thoughts' are running rampant back home, and the Alliance Leader is breathing down our necks. If my old man hadn't sent a message, I wouldn't have dragged Xiaozhu out here. Now that the Demon Nest is gone, we gotta bounce."

Lin Xiaozhu didn't look up, but she added, "The [Desire] and Life Essence samples from this place are invaluable for our research into the source of the evil thoughts in the Central Continent. This battle provided us with new data."
Zhang Xian didn't even glance at the bottle of pills. He pushed it back across the table.

"Although the [Desire] here is gone, the Central Continent sounds like a mess. Keep them. To me, these pills are just worldly possessions—pocket change. But for you guys? They might be an extra life when it counts. Take them. Consider it a parting gift."
Lin Xiaozhu finally looked up. Her clear, analytical eyes flashed with rare surprise.

Earth-Grade Spirit Recovery Pills were strategic resources. Even in the Central Continent, major powers fought wars over them. The value of this single bottle was enough to buy a small sect, yet Zhang Xian was giving it away like it was a box of cheap snacks?
Xia Chengyan stared at him, finally understanding the true depth of Zhang Xian’s wealth.
"Holy sh*t. Brother Zhang... you’re actually serious?"

Xia Chengyan slammed his hand on the table, grinning ear to ear. "You’re a badass! I, Xia Chengyan, officially acknowledge you as my Big Brother. Seriously, when you come to the Central Continent, I’m rolling out the red carpet. I’ll make sure you’re treated like a king."
He didn't refuse again, solemnly storing the pills away.
Zhang Xian smiled and nodded. "It’s a promise."
He paused, then turned his gaze to the scholarly girl. "Miss Xiaozhu, in your professional opinion... how can [Desire] be completely eradicated?"
"It is very difficult." Lin Xiaozhu set down her array disk and slowly shook her head.

She stepped up to a captive deeply entrenched in madness and fired a Clear Heart rune into his chest.
The man convulsed violently.
The red light in his eyes faded for a split second, only to be replaced by an expression of even greater agony and confusion before the madness took hold again.
Lin Xiaozhu shook her head.
"The [Desire] has taken root in his marrow.
His Golden Core is corroded beyond repair.
There is no saving him."
Her words sealed the fate of these wretches.
They were slaves to their own cravings, lost in self-woven illusions.
Their bodies were nothing more than walking corpses.
Other captives reacted differently to the baptism.
Some froze as if struck by lightning.
Their bodies trembled violently, tears and mucus streaming down their faces as they let out heart-wrenching wails.
"I was wrong!
I was wrong!
I’m not human!
Please, just kill me!"
It was as if they had woken from a long, terrible nightmare, crushed by the weight of their sins.
Others clutched their heads and rolled on the ground, screaming in sheer psychological agony.
These were the ones whose corruption was lighter; their eyes still held fear and a desperate will to survive.
"Take them away and guard them strictly," Xia Xuanyin ordered, his voice carrying the unquestionable authority of an Emperor.
"When we return to the Southern Capital, they will be handed over to the Ministry of Justice and the sect elders for interrogation.
We will uncover the cause of their fall and the extent of their crimes before passing judgment!"
Two days later.
The flying boats of the various sects began to rise into the sky, embarking on the journey home.
Li Fuxi was clearly in a foul mood.
Since the battle ended, she had locked herself in her quiet room, refusing to see anyone.
In contrast, Lin Yinyin was buzzing with excitement.
Her face was flushed as she dragged Zhang Xian around, chattering non-stop.
This was her first large-scale war.
She had gone from nervousness to the thrill of combat, and now to the joy of victory.
Her mental state had undergone a baptism by fire, and her cultivation showed faint signs of improvement.
Yun Wanqing, however, had shed her usual armor of toughness.
She buried herself in Zhang Xian’s arms and cried until she had no tears left.
The complete dissipation of the White Venerable had severed the last thread connecting her to the past.
The resolute killing intent he showed, and the tainted Golden Core turning to ash, told her clearly that the man she had waited two hundred years for was gone.
What remained had been nothing but a monster twisted by [Desire], wearing her husband's memories like a skin suit.
Zhang Xian held her silently, feeling the tremors in her body until she exhausted herself and fell into a deep sleep.
He tiptoed out of the room, closing the door softly behind him.
As he turned into the corridor, he saw Xia Chengyan leaning against the wall, a meaningful, roguish grin plastered on his face.
"Yo, Brother Zhang.
Fancy meeting you here."
Zhang Xian opened his mouth to explain, but Xia Chengyan waved him off with a knowing look.
"Say less, bro.
I know exactly what went down in there." He threw a heavy arm around Zhang Xian’s shoulder.
"Come on, let’s go to my cabin.
Have a seat, drink some tea."
Zhang Xian smiled helplessly and let himself be dragged along.
Inside the Prince's cabin, Lin Xiaozhu was sitting primly by a tea table.
In front of her were two transparent jade bottles.
One contained a wisp of black energy that writhed like a living parasite, emitting a cold, sinister aura—a remnant of [Desire].
The other held a few drops of white liquid radiating rich Life Essence.
She was fully focused on manipulating a delicate array disk, projecting complex holograms of light to analyze the substances.
Xia Chengyan poured Zhang Xian a cup of spirit tea, then pulled out a familiar object.
It was the bottle of Earth-Grade Spirit Recovery Pills Zhang Xian had tossed him during the fight.
"Brother Zhang, here.
I’m returning this treasure to you."
Before Zhang Xian could speak, the Prince continued.
"Xiaozhu and I have to head back to the Central Continent immediately, so we won't be saying goodbye to the others.
Meeting you on this trip to the Southern Region... it’s been a real pleasure, man."
"The thing is, the 'Seven Emotions Evil Thoughts' are running rampant back home, and the Alliance Leader is breathing down our necks.
If my old man hadn't sent a message, I wouldn't have dragged Xiaozhu out here.
Now that the Demon Nest is gone, we gotta bounce."
Lin Xiaozhu didn't look up, but she added, "The [Desire] and Life Essence samples from this place are invaluable for our research into the source of the evil thoughts in the Central Continent.
This battle provided us with new data."
Zhang Xian didn't even glance at the bottle of pills.
He pushed it back across the table.
"Although the [Desire] here is gone, the Central Continent sounds like a mess.
Keep them.
To me, these pills are just worldly possessions—pocket change.
But for you guys?
They might be an extra life when it counts.
Take them.
Consider it a parting gift."
Lin Xiaozhu finally looked up.
Her clear, analytical eyes flashed with rare surprise.
Earth-Grade Spirit Recovery Pills were strategic resources.
Even in the Central Continent, major powers fought wars over them.
The value of this single bottle was enough to buy a small sect, yet Zhang Xian was giving it away like it was a box of cheap snacks?
Xia Chengyan stared at him, finally understanding the true depth of Zhang Xian’s wealth.
"Holy sh*t.
Brother Zhang... you’re actually serious?"
Xia Chengyan slammed his hand on the table, grinning ear to ear.
"You’re a badass!
I, Xia Chengyan, officially acknowledge you as my Big Brother.
Seriously, when you come to the Central Continent, I’m rolling out the red carpet.
I’ll make sure you’re treated like a king."
He didn't refuse again, solemnly storing the pills away.
Zhang Xian smiled and nodded.
"It’s a promise."
He paused, then turned his gaze to the scholarly girl.
"Miss Xiaozhu, in your professional opinion... how can [Desire] be completely eradicated?"
"It is very difficult." Lin Xiaozhu set down her array disk and slowly shook her head.

chapters.title: Chapter 172 Kept Above the Clouds
paragraphs: Lin Xiaozhu continued her explanation, her voice steady and analytical. "Uncle once broke it down for me. The Seven Emotions Evil Thoughts aren't tangible entities in the traditional sense. They are more like the physical manifestation of a rule, or a concept. The demons we slaughtered before? They were merely empty shells, biological hosts parasitized to carry their power."

She paced slightly, gesturing to emphasize her point. "Desire is like a seed. It burrows into the host's heart, inducing their deepest obsessions, and then feeds on that chaotic energy to nourish itself. To completely eradicate such a thing, there are only two ways."
She held up two slender fingers. "First: Locate its core aggregate—the main body—and annihilate its spirit and soul. You must utterly obliterate the very source of its existence."

"Second..." She paused, her tone weighing heavy with gravity. "Is to fuse with it. Absorb it, refine it thoroughly, and turn it into your own power. But this path is fraught with extreme peril. The slightest lapse in will results in a backlash, transforming the cultivator into a new, even more terrifying demon."
Zhang Xian’s heart stirred. "That is the path Lele chose."
He quickly followed up, "In your opinion, was the Black Venerable we killed the core aggregate of Desire?"

Lin Xiaozhu pondered for a moment before nodding with certainty. "Based on my perception, the aura of Desire on him was the purest and most potent, far surpassing any other demon. The moment he died, the corrupt black energy on the remaining demons weakened significantly. There is no doubt—he was the primary source."

However, a frown creased her forehead. "That said... after the main body dissipated, the remaining seeds of Desire didn't vanish along with it. That is indeed an anomaly. I’ll need to return and consult Uncle to understand why."

Hearing Lin Xiaozhu’s firm judgment, the knot of worry in Zhang Xian’s chest loosened slightly. Perhaps Desire was like a virus from his previous life; as long as the human heart harbored the seven emotions and six desires, it could never be fully eradicated. Perhaps one could only suppress it and purge the infected carriers.
"Senior Brother, I'm so tired. I don't want to practice the sword anymore."
"Little Xi'er, listen to your Senior Brother. If you break through to Foundation Establishment by the end of the year, I’ll buy you your favorite Honey Cloud Cakes. A whole box!"
"Wuwu... but it's so hard. Can I eat less cake and practice a little less?"
"Absolutely not. If you don't cultivate properly, Master will smack your palms, and even I won't be able to stop him."
"Alright, alright, Senior Brother, quit scaring Junior Sister. She's still young, let her take it slow."
"Second Junior Sister, you're spoiling her again. You play with her every day—careful Master doesn't punish you too!
"Hehe, Senior Brother is the best! He’d never tattle on us!"
Li Fuxi jerked awake from the dream, her back drenched in cold sweat. She stared blankly out of the cabin window, her chest heaving, the familiar, warm voices of the past still echoing in her ears.
"Senior Brother... Second Senior Sister..." she murmured, her vision blurring with mist.

After a long silence, she slowly sat up. She hesitated for a moment before reaching toward her pillow. Her fingers closed around a warm communication jade talisman. Carved on the front in bold, flamboyant strokes was the character: "Xian."
Three years flew by in the blink of an eye, and the landscape of the Southern Domain shifted quietly but profoundly.

Old Master Yunhe narrowly survived his Heavenly Tribulation, successfully advancing to the Nascent Soul stage. With a true powerhouse at the helm, the Yunshang Pavilion’s prestige exploded. They not only secured their spot among the Southern Domain's six major forces but also aggressively annexed the marketplaces left behind by the Baoqing Workshop’s withdrawal. Their commercial empire expanded rapidly, crowning them the undisputed number one merchant association in the region.

Over at the Yunmiao Sect, Wangya Zhenren also successfully broke through to Nascent Soul. The former Sect Master, Xingjie Zhenren, having been stuck at a bottleneck for too long, left a letter of resignation and quietly departed the sect to seek opportunities in the wider world. Wangya Zhenren naturally took over as the Acting Sect Master, assuming full control.

Li Fuxi officially ascended to the position of Head of Lingjian Peak. Meanwhile, Lin Yinyin’s cultivation skyrocketed. She broke through to the sixth stage of the Golden Core at a terrifying speed, becoming the youngest Supervisor in the sect’s history. Her future was limitless.

On Qingmu Peak, the Head Liu Huaigu finally emerged from the shadow of grief over his friend's death. He resigned from his position and withdrew from public view. His daughter, Liu Qingxuan, entered intense seclusion. upon emerging, she broke through to the late Golden Core stage in a single burst and took over her father's seat.

During these three years, Zhang Xian made a special trip to Penglai Immortal Island to visit Lele. She remained in a deep slumber, her aura steady and profound. Refining and fusing with the concept of Obsession was clearly a long, arduous road.

afterward, Zhang Xian returned to his homeland in the Great Liang Kingdom. He spent three full months burning through a mountain of Spirit Stones to set up Spirit Gathering Grand Formations at major ley lines, rivers, and mountain nodes. It was a massive terraforming project to inject Spiritual Qi into the barren land.
Back at the Yunmiao Sect, the disciples had grown accustomed to the luxurious flying boat perpetually parked above Lingjian Peak. Everyone knew it was Zhang Zhenren's personal vessel.
It was an open secret that Head Li Fuxi and Supervisor Lin Yinyin were "kept" up there year-round.

The gossip mill churned even harder when disciples caught glimpses of other high-profile beauties boarding the ship. The peerlessly elegant Yun Wanqing of the Yunshang Pavilion and the new Head of Qingmu Peak, Liu Qingxuan, were occasional guests.

The only saving grace was that "Old Devil Zhang" seemed to have reformed. He hadn't harassed any other female cultivators in years, allowing many of the sect’s disciples to breathe a secret sigh of relief.
The demon-slaying war of the past seemed to fade into memory, washed away by the flow of time.
Hum.
The stone door of the flying boat's cultivation chamber ground open. Li Fuxi walked out slowly. Her aura was harmonious and restrained, far more profound and stable than it had been three years ago.
Zhang Xian was waiting outside, a gentle smile playing on his lips. "Congratulations, Master. Peak Golden Core realm. You are now just a hair's breadth away from the Great Dao of Nascent Soul."
Li Fuxi shook her head lightly, though the slight upward curve of her lips betrayed her satisfaction. "It isn't as simple as you make it sound. The Nascent Soul realm is not so easily attained."

Her beautiful eyes shifted, sweeping over Zhang Xian with a mix of curiosity and suspicion. "But you... why do I feel your aura becoming increasingly unfathomable? It feels like you're about to overtake your master, yet I rarely see you in seclusion."

"Master, you jest. How could this disciple's meager skills compare to yours?" Zhang Xian laughed it off smoothly. "By the way, Master, how is the refinement of that jade bracelet I gave you coming along?"
At the mention of the bracelet, Li Fuxi’s delicate brows knit together, and she let out a soft sigh. "That bracelet is extraordinary."
She raised her hand, revealing a wrist of snowy white skin. An icy blue jade bracelet circled it, glowing with an inner light and emitting a faint, frosty chill.
"I’ve tried countless times. I’ve exhausted my True Essence and even drew upon the power of my dual Heavenly Spiritual Roots, yet I can barely leave a scratch on its surface."

Her tone carried a trace of helplessness mixed with awe. "There seems to be an incredibly powerful restriction inside the bracelet that resists my refinement. I fear I will have to wait until I truly step into the Nascent Soul realm—using the power of a Nascent Soul to commune with heaven and earth—before I can fully master it."

Zhang Xian nodded, hiding his amusement. He wasn't surprised. That bracelet was a Mid-Grade Defensive Spirit Treasure, created by using the Spirit Treasure Essence from the system to upgrade a base item. Its power was leagues above ordinary low-grade treasures, and naturally, its internal restrictions were formidable.
With Li Fuxi’s cultivation still at the Golden Core stage, refining a Mid-Grade Spirit Treasure was simply asking too much.

It seems that if I want Master and the others to use better gear, they’ll have to break through to Nascent Soul first, Zhang Xian mused. My ability to forcibly refine items via the system is a cheat they don't have access to.
