chapters.title: Chapter 173 No Longer the Same Shape
paragraphs: The following day, inside the sword chamber of the flying vessel, faint arcs of lightning flickered in the air.
Zhang Xian slowly withdrew his energy. The Five Elements Spiritual Light swirling around him receded like a retreating tide, sinking back into his body.

He turned his gaze inward, focusing on his Dantian. Above his perfectly round Golden Core, three spiritual roots—Water, Metal, and Wood—shone like brilliant rivers of stars, radiating the majestic aura unique to Top-Grade Spiritual Roots.
"Golden Core, Eighth Stage."
Sensing the surging power coursing through his veins, the corner of Zhang Xian's mouth lifted in satisfaction.
In the Southern Domain, this cultivation speed would be considered absolutely earth-shattering.

Of course, he knew perfectly well that this was largely due to the heaven-defying passive buff from the [Disciple of High Talent Halo]. Every breakthrough and every flash of enlightenment Li Fuxi achieved acted as a propellant, dragging him forward at breakneck speed.

He had a vague premonition that the Ninth Stage of the Golden Core was not far off. When that time came, his Water and Metal dual roots would likely shatter their shackles together, evolving into Heavenly Spiritual Roots. That would be another qualitative leap in power.
Master really is the best.

However, a trace of imperceptible regret surfaced in his heart. The favorability ratings of the three women—Li Fuxi, Yun Wanqing, and Liu Qingxuan—remained stubbornly stuck in the low 80s. They were always just a hair's breadth away from the critical threshold of 90 points.
Zhang Xian rubbed his chin thoughtfully. Perhaps they need to undergo some kind of deeply etched, life-or-death trial to completely open their hearts?

He glanced toward the wall separating him from Li Fuxi's meditation chamber. The delicate relationship they shared—somewhere between master-disciple and Dao Companions—seemed unable to progress further due to a certain unspoken barrier.
Pushing those thoughts aside, Zhang Xian stood up and walked to the center of the training ground.
"Strike!"
With a low shout, he guided his spirit sword, stirring the ambient Spiritual Qi of heaven and earth.
BOOM!
In an instant, a blinding bolt of thunder crashed down. Lightning exploded, electric snakes danced wildly across the floor, scorching the special tiles black.
"The power is still lacking..." Zhang Xian frowned slightly, inspecting the scorch marks.

This was a simplified thunder technique he had reverse-engineered from his memory of Long Zhi's earth-shattering [Purple Firmament Dragon's Roar True Words], combined with his own Five Elements foundation. Although it was visually spectacular, it lacked the terrifying density and destructive purity of the original version.
He had been diligently cultivating thunder techniques these past few days for two reasons.

First, to prepare for the Heavenly Tribulation he would inevitably face when impacting the Nascent Soul stage. Tempering the body with lightning and familiarizing oneself with the nature of thunder was the golden rule for surviving Tribulation Transcendence.

Second, thunder naturally restrained all Yin, evil, and filthy things. Although [Desire] was formless, its essence was still rooted in Yin corruption. Mastering a powerful thunder technique would give him a distinct advantage when facing the Seven Emotions Evil Thoughts in the future.
Finishing his set, he slowly lowered his stance, his gaze falling on the spirit sword in his hand, which was still crackling with faint strands of purple electricity.

This was the Lei Yin Sword that Long Zhi, the Dragon Princess, had pawned to him years ago. After he had enhanced it with a Mid-Grade Spirit Treasure Essence, not only had all its damage been repaired, but it had also evolved into a Mid-Grade Spirit Treasure.
Even now, the blade retained the unique spiritual imprint left by Long Zhi.

He recalled the awkward yet earnest expression on her face when she said, "I'll redeem it once I have the money." He couldn't help but chuckle. "I should find an opportunity to give it back. The look on her face when she sees her familiar, precious sword is... no longer the same shape she remembers... will definitely be priceless."

"That should trigger another wave of System Returns. Maybe if she's thin-skinned enough, I can even shame her into teaching me the genuine [Purple Firmament Dragon's Roar True Words]. I really am a genius."
Just as Zhang Xian was indulging in his shameless fantasies—
HUM!
The Lei Yin Sword in his hand vibrated violently without warning. The thunder power contained within the blade surged, as if answering a distant yet irresistible summons.
"Hmm?" Zhang Xian was startled, instinctively tightening his grip on the hilt.
The next second—
CLANG!
A clear, piercing sword cry resounded through the chamber. The Lei Yin Sword erupted with blinding light, ripping itself violently from Zhang Xian's grasp.

Like a streak of purple lightning, it whooshed upward, instantly punching through the multiple defensive layers of the flying vessel's ceiling. It left behind a scorched, jagged hole as it vanished into the vast sky. The speed was so terrified that even Zhang Xian had no time to react.
"Holy sh*t!"
Zhang Xian stared dumbfounded at the hole in the roof, the cold wind whistling in. "Did... did Long Zhi just recall it remotely? Without even saying hello? That's just rude!"
Wait. No.
She wouldn't do that without a reason. A sudden, sharp sense of alarm rose in his chest.
BANG!
The chamber door was thrown open. Li Fuxi rushed in, her face pale with anxiety, her breathing unsteady. She had clearly just been jolted out of deep cultivation.
Zhang Xian assumed she had heard the noise. "Master? About the roof, I'll ask Zhiyin to fix—"

Li Fuxi interrupted him, her voice trembling with gravity and urgency. "It's the Lingxu Sword Sect! They've issued a Blood-Colored Distress Token—the highest level of emergency. They claim they are under attack by demons and the Sect is on the brink of total annihilation!
"What?!" Zhang Xian was shaken to the core.

The Yunmiao Sect urgently assembled a strike force of top-tier combatants led by Acting Sect Master Wangya. Unfortunately, the teleportation arrays in the cities surrounding the Lingxu Sword Sect had already been destroyed. The group was forced to travel the long way.
By the time they rushed at breakneck speed to Yujing City, three days had passed.
The scene before them plunged everyone into an icy abyss.

Yujing City, once the second-largest city in the Southern Domain, famous for its white jade foundations and prosperity, had been reduced to a graveyard. The city walls had collapsed. Less than one in ten buildings remained standing. Among the rubble, scorched black marks and dark red bloodstains painted a horrific picture of slaughter.
The air was thick with the heavy, metallic stench of blood.
And beneath that, a familiar, bone-chilling aura—the residual stench of the Seven Emotions Evil Thoughts.
Directly ahead, the iconic Nine-Story Glazed Pagoda of Yujing City had been snapped in half at the waist. Shattered glazed tiles littered the ground, refracting broken light under the setting sun.

Above the ruins of the pagoda, a massive vortex emitting a chaotic five-colored light spun silently. Deep within the vortex, fragmented scenes of broken mountains and rivers were visible. Just as the rumors said, the entrance to the Lingxu Sword Sect's pocket dimension was directly above the city.
Without hesitation, the group stepped into the vortex.
An even denser, more suffocating aura of death washed over them.

The paradise was gone. The immortal islands that once floated majestically above the sea of clouds had been shattered, their debris crashing down onto the broken earth below. At the edges of the flickering protective formation, traces of a viscous, white slime remained—corrupted Life Essence.

The earth was cracked, the spiritual veins severed. The once-pure spirit springs gushed with filthy blood-water. As far as the eye could see, there were only severed limbs, shattered artifacts, and congealed blood.
There was not a single trace of life.
"This..." Lin Yinyin covered her mouth, her face draining of all color.

Several streaks of light flew toward them rapidly. It was Xia Xuanyin, Old Pavilion Master Yunhe, and Zen Master Ming Kui, a Nascent Soul powerhouse from the Mountain Chan Monastery. They had arrived earlier. Their expressions were dark enough to drip water, radiating a suppressed, volcanic fury.
"What is the situation?" Wangya Zhenren asked, his voice dry.
Xia Xuanyin slowly shook his head.

"No survivors. Not a single one. We found the bodies of Qing Shi Zhenren and the Lingxu Sect Master." He paused, forcing the words out through grit teeth. "The Sect Master's Golden Core was shattered, his soul utterly extinguished. Qing Shi Zhenren died fighting... his body was torn to pieces."

sentences.text: The following day, inside the sword chamber of the flying vessel, faint arcs of lightning flickered in the air.
Zhang Xian slowly withdrew his energy.
The Five Elements Spiritual Light swirling around him receded like a retreating tide, sinking back into his body.
He turned his gaze inward, focusing on his Dantian.
Above his perfectly round Golden Core, three spiritual roots—Water, Metal, and Wood—shone like brilliant rivers of stars, radiating the majestic aura unique to Top-Grade Spiritual Roots.
"Golden Core, Eighth Stage."
Sensing the surging power coursing through his veins, the corner of Zhang Xian's mouth lifted in satisfaction.
In the Southern Domain, this cultivation speed would be considered absolutely earth-shattering.
Of course, he knew perfectly well that this was largely due to the heaven-defying passive buff from the [Disciple of High Talent Halo].
Every breakthrough and every flash of enlightenment Li Fuxi achieved acted as a propellant, dragging him forward at breakneck speed.
He had a vague premonition that the Ninth Stage of the Golden Core was not far off.
When that time came, his Water and Metal dual roots would likely shatter their shackles together, evolving into Heavenly Spiritual Roots.
That would be another qualitative leap in power.
Master really is the best.
However, a trace of imperceptible regret surfaced in his heart.
The favorability ratings of the three women—Li Fuxi, Yun Wanqing, and Liu Qingxuan—remained stubbornly stuck in the low 80s.
They were always just a hair's breadth away from the critical threshold of 90 points.
Zhang Xian rubbed his chin thoughtfully.
Perhaps they need to undergo some kind of deeply etched, life-or-death trial to completely open their hearts?
He glanced toward the wall separating him from Li Fuxi's meditation chamber.
The delicate relationship they shared—somewhere between master-disciple and Dao Companions—seemed unable to progress further due to a certain unspoken barrier.
Pushing those thoughts aside, Zhang Xian stood up and walked to the center of the training ground.
"Strike!"
With a low shout, he guided his spirit sword, stirring the ambient Spiritual Qi of heaven and earth.
BOOM!
In an instant, a blinding bolt of thunder crashed down.
Lightning exploded, electric snakes danced wildly across the floor, scorching the special tiles black.
"The power is still lacking..." Zhang Xian frowned slightly, inspecting the scorch marks.

This was a simplified thunder technique he had reverse-engineered from his memory of Long Zhi's earth-shattering [Purple Firmament Dragon's Roar True Words], combined with his own Five Elements foundation.
Although it was visually spectacular, it lacked the terrifying density and destructive purity of the original version.
He had been diligently cultivating thunder techniques these past few days for two reasons.
First, to prepare for the Heavenly Tribulation he would inevitably face when impacting the Nascent Soul stage.
Tempering the body with lightning and familiarizing oneself with the nature of thunder was the golden rule for surviving Tribulation Transcendence.
Second, thunder naturally restrained all Yin, evil, and filthy things.
Although [Desire] was formless, its essence was still rooted in Yin corruption.
Mastering a powerful thunder technique would give him a distinct advantage when facing the Seven Emotions Evil Thoughts in the future.
Finishing his set, he slowly lowered his stance, his gaze falling on the spirit sword in his hand, which was still crackling with faint strands of purple electricity.
This was the Lei Yin Sword that Long Zhi, the Dragon Princess, had pawned to him years ago.
After he had enhanced it with a Mid-Grade Spirit Treasure Essence, not only had all its damage been repaired, but it had also evolved into a Mid-Grade Spirit Treasure.
Even now, the blade retained the unique spiritual imprint left by Long Zhi.
He recalled the awkward yet earnest expression on her face when she said, "I'll redeem it once I have the money." He couldn't help but chuckle.
"I should find an opportunity to give it back.
The look on her face when she sees her familiar, precious sword is... no longer the same shape she remembers... will definitely be priceless."
"That should trigger another wave of System Returns.
Maybe if she's thin-skinned enough, I can even shame her into teaching me the genuine [Purple Firmament Dragon's Roar True Words].
I really am a genius."
Just as Zhang Xian was indulging in his shameless fantasies—
HUM!
The Lei Yin Sword in his hand vibrated violently without warning.
The thunder power contained within the blade surged, as if answering a distant yet irresistible summons.
"Hmm?" Zhang Xian was startled, instinctively tightening his grip on the hilt.
The next second—
CLANG!
A clear, piercing sword cry resounded through the chamber.
The Lei Yin Sword erupted with blinding light, ripping itself violently from Zhang Xian's grasp.
Like a streak of purple lightning, it whooshed upward, instantly punching through the multiple defensive layers of the flying vessel's ceiling.
It left behind a scorched, jagged hole as it vanished into the vast sky.
The speed was so terrified that even Zhang Xian had no time to react.
"Holy sh*t!"
Zhang Xian stared dumbfounded at the hole in the roof, the cold wind whistling in.
"Did... did Long Zhi just recall it remotely?
Without even saying hello?
That's just rude!"
Wait.
No.
She wouldn't do that without a reason.
A sudden, sharp sense of alarm rose in his chest.
BANG!
The chamber door was thrown open.
Li Fuxi rushed in, her face pale with anxiety, her breathing unsteady.
She had clearly just been jolted out of deep cultivation.
Zhang Xian assumed she had heard the noise.
"Master?
About the roof, I'll ask Zhiyin to fix—"
Li Fuxi interrupted him, her voice trembling with gravity and urgency.
"It's the Lingxu Sword Sect!
They've issued a Blood-Colored Distress Token—the highest level of emergency.
They claim they are under attack by demons and the Sect is on the brink of total annihilation!
"What?!" Zhang Xian was shaken to the core.
The Yunmiao Sect urgently assembled a strike force of top-tier combatants led by Acting Sect Master Wangya.
Unfortunately, the teleportation arrays in the cities surrounding the Lingxu Sword Sect had already been destroyed.
The group was forced to travel the long way.
By the time they rushed at breakneck speed to Yujing City, three days had passed.
The scene before them plunged everyone into an icy abyss.
Yujing City, once the second-largest city in the Southern Domain, famous for its white jade foundations and prosperity, had been reduced to a graveyard.
The city walls had collapsed.
Less than one in ten buildings remained standing.
Among the rubble, scorched black marks and dark red bloodstains painted a horrific picture of slaughter.
The air was thick with the heavy, metallic stench of blood.
And beneath that, a familiar, bone-chilling aura—the residual stench of the Seven Emotions Evil Thoughts.
Directly ahead, the iconic Nine-Story Glazed Pagoda of Yujing City had been snapped in half at the waist.
Shattered glazed tiles littered the ground, refracting broken light under the setting sun.
Above the ruins of the pagoda, a massive vortex emitting a chaotic five-colored light spun silently.
Deep within the vortex, fragmented scenes of broken mountains and rivers were visible.
Just as the rumors said, the entrance to the Lingxu Sword Sect's pocket dimension was directly above the city.
Without hesitation, the group stepped into the vortex.
An even denser, more suffocating aura of death washed over them.
The paradise was gone.
The immortal islands that once floated majestically above the sea of clouds had been shattered, their debris crashing down onto the broken earth below.
At the edges of the flickering protective formation, traces of a viscous, white slime remained—corrupted Life Essence.
The earth was cracked, the spiritual veins severed.
The once-pure spirit springs gushed with filthy blood-water.
As far as the eye could see, there were only severed limbs, shattered artifacts, and congealed blood.
There was not a single trace of life.
"This..." Lin Yinyin covered her mouth, her face draining of all color.
Several streaks of light flew toward them rapidly.
It was Xia Xuanyin, Old Pavilion Master Yunhe, and Zen Master Ming Kui, a Nascent Soul powerhouse from the Mountain Chan Monastery.
They had arrived earlier.
Their expressions were dark enough to drip water, radiating a suppressed, volcanic fury.
"What is the situation?" Wangya Zhenren asked, his voice dry.
Xia Xuanyin slowly shook his head.
"No survivors.
Not a single one.
We found the bodies of Qing Shi Zhenren and the Lingxu Sect Master." He paused, forcing the words out through grit teeth.
"The Sect Master's Golden Core was shattered, his soul utterly extinguished.
Qing Shi Zhenren died fighting... his body was torn to pieces."

chapters.title: Chapter 174 A Friend from Nowhere
paragraphs: “The Spirit Ruins Sword Sect’s secret realm is completely isolated from the outside world. Communication is nearly impossible. The distress signal we received came from a Law Enforcement Elder stationed in Yujing City. He detected an abnormal seal locking down the realm’s entrance and sent the message in a moment of desperate urgency. By the time we received it and rushed here... it was already too late.”

An old man, his aura withered to the point of collapse, was helped forward by two cultivators. Zhang Xian recognized him immediately—he was an Elder of the Spirit Ruins Sword Sect he had met at the Demon-Subduing Conference three years ago.
Now, the old man’s eyes were vacant, his face the color of dead ash. He looked as though his soul had been ripped away.

“I... I was handling market affairs in Yujing City,” he murmured, his voice trembling. “Suddenly, I felt violent spatial tremors and a heart-palpitating evil aura erupting from the secret realm entrance...”

His body began to shake uncontrollably. “I rushed to the entrance. It was completely sealed by a layer of black threads, like a massive spider web. I used everything I had—Dharma Treasures, talismans, I even self-detonated my Life-Bound Artifact—but I... I couldn’t even scratch that black net!”

“Then... a man in black robes walked out.” The elder’s eyes widened in terror. “He glanced at me. Just one glance, and I felt my very soul freeze in place. He didn’t even bother to kill me properly. He just waved his hand... and everything went dark.”
“When I woke up... Yujing City was already... already...” The old man broke down, tears streaming down his wrinkled face. His legs gave out, and he collapsed into the arms of his supporters.
Real Man Wangya stepped forward, his voice urgent. “Did you see his face? Any distinguishing features? Is it a new manifestation of the Seven Emotions Evil Thoughts?”
The elder shook his head in agony. “I couldn’t see clearly. I only felt his aura... it was terrifying. Far more tyrannical than the Black Venerable ever was.”
Suddenly, Zen Master Ming Kui’s expression changed drastically.
He snatched the Buddhist prayer beads from his wrist and drove his Divine Sense into them.

“Not good!” He snapped his head up, panic flashing in his eyes. “An intense demonic aura has appeared outside the main altar of the Mountain Zen Monastery! The Guardian Formation has fully activated—we are under attack!”
“What?!”
The group recoiled in horror. The demons were acting with rampant aggression—first annihilating the Spirit Ruins Sword Sect, and now immediately laying siege to the Mountain Zen Monastery?
“Move!” Old Pavilion Master Yunhe roared, his beard and hair bristling with rage. “We must reinforce the Mountain Zen Monastery immediately!”
Meanwhile, hundreds of miles away, at the foot of the Yunmiao Sect.

A figure dressed in the blue-and-white inner sect robes of the Yunmiao Sect strolled calmly through the mountain gate’s restrictions. His face was ordinary, the kind you would forget instantly, but his eyes were exceptionally calm and profound.
He stepped through the gate, his fingers deftly forming a set of hand seals to unlock the secondary restrictions.
Along the path, passing disciples smiled and greeted him. “Good afternoon, Senior Brother.”
He nodded back with a polite smile, his demeanor perfectly natural.

Stepping onto a flying sword, he transformed into an inconspicuous streak of light, heading straight for the summit of Spirit Sword Peak. As he approached, he slowed, his gaze sweeping over the luxurious flying ship hovering above the peak.
He landed softly on the ground, looking up at the vessel. A faint, almost imperceptible smirk tugged at the corner of his mouth.

He walked toward the simple thatched hut that served as the residence. He pushed the door open and entered. The interior was sparse. He scanned the room before his eyes settled on a scroll tucked in the corner.
He walked over and gently unrolled it. The character “Xi” (Dawn)—written with vigorous strokes containing boundless sword intent—leaped off the paper.
He let out a soft, ambiguous chuckle, shook his head, and tossed the scroll back into the corner like trash.

Exiting the hut, he walked to the flat bluestone clearing in the yard. He extended his right index finger. A wisp of golden light coiled around his fingertip—extremely pure, yet tainted with a strange, eerie Buddhist nature.
His movements were elegant and precise, as if he were painting on the canvas of the void. Wherever his finger traced, a trail of condensed, unscattering golden light remained.
Within moments, a complex golden symbol—the Buddhist Swastika “卍”—formed in the air.
He flicked his finger.
The golden symbol turned into a streak of light and melted silently into the air above Spirit Sword Peak. Like a drop of water merging into the sea, it vanished without a ripple.
“The formation is set.” He nodded with satisfaction, as if he had just completed a trivial chore.
He walked over to a nearby stone stool, sat down, and produced a jug of wine and a jade cup. He poured himself a drink, sipping leisurely as he gazed out at the rolling sea of clouds, waiting.
Not long after, a sword light descended steadily onto the peak.

It was Chen Tiexin, an inner sect disciple of Spirit Sword Peak. She was on patrol duty today. From a distance, she had spotted a stranger sitting in this secluded, private area of the summit. Puzzled, she landed to investigate.
“You there, Junior Brother.” Chen Tiexin frowned slightly, her scrutinizing gaze locking onto the young man.
She noted his inner sect robes, but his temperament was jarringly different from any disciple she knew. That utter composure, that stillness... it gave her an inexplicable sense of pressure.
Subconsciously, her hand drifted to the hilt of her sword. “What are you doing here? This is the summit of Spirit Sword Peak. Unauthorized entry is forbidden. How did you get in?”
The young man didn’t pause his drinking. He slowly lifted his eyelids, his flat, emotionless gaze settling on Chen Tiexin.
“You are a disciple of Spirit Sword Peak?”

Chen Tiexin felt a chill run down her spine under his gaze, as if he were stripping her soul bare. She steadied herself and spoke solemnly. “Correct. I am Chen Tiexin, Inner Sect Disciple. May I ask your name? If you are looking for someone, Peak Master Li and Supervisor Lin have both left the mountain.”
As soon as the words left her mouth—
WHOOSH!
A sharp sound tore through the air. A figure dropped from the sky, landing instantly between Chen Tiexin and the mysterious young man.
It was Zhang Xian.

He landed steadily, his breathing even, wearing his habitual gentle smile as if he had just happened to be passing by. He didn’t even look at the young man behind him. Instead, he turned directly to Chen Tiexin, his tone relaxed and breezy.
“Senior Sister Chen, no need to be nervous. This is a friend of mine. He came specifically to see me.”
Chen Tiexin blinked, taken aback. She looked at Zhang Xian, then glanced at the young man, who remained seated and composed.
Zhang Xian’s friend?

She had never heard of him having friends like this. Didn’t most male disciples despise him? And wait... wasn’t Zhang Xian supposed to be at the Spirit Ruins Sword Sect right now? How did he suddenly appear here?
Suspicion surged in her heart. She opened her mouth to ask.
But just as her lips parted—
Zhang Xian’s right hand, hanging loosely at his side and shielded from the stranger’s view, made a sharp, deliberate gesture.
His index and middle fingers pressed together and tapped his thigh three times. Tap. Tap. Tap.
Chen Tiexin’s pupils contracted to pinpoints.
That was the Yunmiao Sect’s highest-level silent code.
Extreme Danger. Flee Immediately.
A blast of cold terror shot from the soles of her feet to the top of her skull.
“Oh... so it’s Junior Brother’s friend.” Chen Tiexin forced herself to speak, crushing the panic rising in her throat. “In that case, this disciple won’t disturb you.”
She didn’t dare look at the young man again. She turned on her heel, her movement crisp and decisive.
The tip of her foot tapped the ground, and she vaulted onto her flying sword. With a clear hum of energy, she shot down the mountain without looking back.

chapters.title: Chapter 175 Master, You Must Have Great Kidneys
paragraphs: Silence descended upon the peak once more, heavy and suffocating.

The young man didn’t seem surprised by Zhang Xian’s sudden appearance. He slowly shifted his gaze, locking eyes with him. ” You flashed the Yunmiao Sect’s highest distress signal right in front of my face. Did you think I wouldn’t recognize it?”

Zhang Xian sat down with bold familiarity, unceremoniously grabbing the wine pot to pour himself a cup. “Ancestor Master, you wound me. I just thought she was getting in the way. I had to scare her off so we could talk.”
The young man remained composed. “Oh? Can that puppet body of yours appreciate fine wine?”
Zhang Xian lifted the cup, sniffed the aroma, and downed it in one gulp. He smacked his lips theatrically. “Tsk. Tasteless. What a tragedy.”

He refilled his cup. “It’s not often I see you, Ancestor Master, in such an elegant mood, drinking alone on a mountain peak. As your disciple’s disciple, isn’t it my duty to accompany you for a drink? Filial piety and all that.”
“You are very clever.” The young man set down his wine pot, his gaze deepening. “I am curious. How did you guess it was me?”
Zhang Xian shook his head, feigning helplessness. “I didn’t guess. The one who figured it out was my Master—your beloved disciple, Li Fuxi.”
“Oh?” A flicker of surprise passed through the young man’s eyes, quickly replaced by keen interest. “Xi’er? How did she deduce it?”

Zhang Xian didn’t answer immediately. He toyed with the jade cup in his hand, his gaze drifting toward the rolling sea of clouds in the distance as if stalling for time. “Ancestor Master, you seem quite leisurely. What exactly are you waiting for?”
The young man picked up his own cup, gently swirling the clear liquid. His voice was flat, yet it carried a bone-chilling coldness.
“Naturally, I am waiting for the annihilation of the Yunmiao Sect.”
The moment the words left his lips, his hand froze.
Without warning, he pressed his index and middle fingers together into a sword mudra and tapped the air in front of him.
BANG!
A beam of golden sword aura erupted point-blank!
Zhang Xian’s figure retreated instantly, blurring with speed, but he was still half a beat too slow.

His left arm and half of his chest exploded. Metal fragments and leaking spiritual energy sprayed into the air. The golden sword aura carried a strange, corrosive white mist that latched onto the remaining half of his body. In seconds, the puppet lost all spirituality, melting into a puddle of metallic sludge.
Clang.
The dim puppet core dropped to the ground, bouncing once before rolling to a stop.
The entire process was lightning-fast. From the young man’s strike to the puppet’s total destruction, it took less than a breath.
But the puppet had bought enough time.
Almost at the exact moment of impact, the massive flying ship hovering above the peak roared to life. The main cannon port on its underbelly lit up with a blinding, sun-like radiance.
BOOM!
A pillar of blazing white light, charged with enough energy to level a mountain, crashed down toward the young man with a deafening roar.
Facing this apocalyptic strike, the young man merely flicked the sword in his left hand.
A golden crescent moon, thin as a cicada’s wing, materialized out of thin air. It expanded against the wind, instantly transforming into a colossal arc of golden light that spanned the heavens.
CRACK!

The golden crescent collided with the white energy beam. Like a hot knife through butter, it split the terrifying pillar of light in two. The golden arc continued its upward momentum, unabated, and slashed viciously into the hull of the flying ship.
SCREECH—!
The sound of tearing metal screamed across the sky. The luxurious vessel, built with countless precious materials and defensive arrays, was sliced open like paper.
Violent sword qi rampaged through the breach, shredding the internal structure. The ship groaned and disintegrated, raining countless fragments and burning debris down onto Spirit Sword Peak.
The young man’s brow furrowed almost imperceptibly.

Through the falling debris, he noticed something wrong. The Golden Swastika Formation he had secretly laid—intended to envelop the entire Yunmiao Sect—was currently blocked. A massive screen of light had appeared out of nowhere, covering his trap.
Runes flickered across this barrier, emitting a powerful, purifying vitality that tangled with his golden formation, preventing it from activating fully.
“Six Paths Buddha Light?” A trace of surprise flashed in the young man’s eyes. “High-level Buddhist magic?”
WHOOSH!
A dazzling streak of light shot toward the peak, faster than before. It slammed into the ground near the young man, kicking up a cloud of dust.

As the dust settled, Zhang Xian’s true body was revealed. His aura was steady, his expression calm. He didn’t seem the least bit heartbroken over the destruction of his expensive puppet or the priceless flying ship.
“Ancestor Master, we were having such a nice chat. Why the sudden violence? That’s hardly proper guest etiquette.”
For the first time, the young man’s gaze turned grave. He looked Zhang Xian up and down. “How did you return from the Spirit Ruins so quickly?”
Zhang Xian didn’t answer. He just smiled.
Crack!
A crisp sound echoed as the space beside Zhang Xian rippled like water. From the center of the distortion, a graceful figure clad in a white sword robe with gold trim stepped out.
It was Li Fuxi.
Her face was frost-cold, her eyes locked onto the young, unfamiliar face of Wang Chuan. Her voice trembled with suppressed emotion.
“Master... it has been a long time.”

The moment he saw Li Fuxi, the young man understood. Years ago, outside Cloud Raiment City, Zhang Xian had escaped using a high-grade teleportation treasure. He hadn’t expected the brat to possess more than one of such priceless items—and be willing to burn them just to use as a glorified bus ticket.
Li Fuxi’s gaze swept upward to the sky, where the Golden Swastika Formation pulsed with ominous light.

The last trace of hope in her heart was extinguished. She had defended her master countless times in her mind, lied to herself that the clues were just coincidences. But this formation... this sinister, ruthless layout... shattered her illusions.

“Is this... the Joy Formation?” Li Fuxi’s voice was icy, piercing, and filled with incredulous pain. “What are you trying to do? Do you intend to turn every female disciple of the Yunmiao Sect into... a cauldron for your evil cultivation?”
Wang Chuan fell silent. His face showed neither guilt nor joy. He merely let out a soft sigh.

“As you can see, most of the Yunmiao Sect disciples cultivate the ‘Nine Revolutions Condensing Jade Scripture.’ Their yin energy is exceptionally pure. It is of great benefit to my cultivation technique.”
Zhang Xian chimed in from the side, his tone dripping with icy sarcasm.

“Ancestor Master, you truly have a voracious appetite. You played ‘Luring the Tiger from the Mountain’ perfectly. First, you wipe out the Spirit Ruins. Then, you feign an attack on the Mountain Zen Monastery to draw away the Southern Domain’s top combatants. And your target all along was this mountain full of female disciples?”
Zhang Xian smirked, his eyes cold. “You want to harvest them all in one go? Tsk tsk. Master, you must have a pair of incredibly strong kidneys to handle that kind of workload.”
Wang Chuan shook his head slightly, ignoring the jab. He didn’t seem in a hurry to attack. Instead, he looked at Li Fuxi with a scholar’s curiosity.

“I believed my plan was seamless. I let the old Emperor die in my place. I had Qianji create a puppet body containing a wisp of my remnant consciousness to act as a decoy. Xi’er... how exactly did you see through it?”
Li Fuxi took a deep breath, forcibly suppressing the grief churning in her chest. Her voice choked with a sob.
“It was Eldest Senior Brother.”
“Oh?”

“Eldest Senior Brother... even though you refined him into a puppet, he must have discovered your true purpose at the very last moment. He knew he was about to become a container for your consciousness.”

Li Fuxi’s eyes reddened. “He must have used a secret technique to forcibly erase his own key memories. He knew he had to deceive himself before he could deceive you. That is why his puppet body revealed small inconsistencies during battle—flaws that shouldn’t have been there.”

sentences.text: Silence descended upon the peak once more, heavy and suffocating.
The young man didn’t seem surprised by Zhang Xian’s sudden appearance.
He slowly shifted his gaze, locking eyes with him. ” You flashed the Yunmiao Sect’s highest distress signal right in front of my face.
Did you think I wouldn’t recognize it?”
Zhang Xian sat down with bold familiarity, unceremoniously grabbing the wine pot to pour himself a cup.
“Ancestor Master, you wound me.
I just thought she was getting in the way.
I had to scare her off so we could talk.”
The young man remained composed.
“Oh?
Can that puppet body of yours appreciate fine wine?”
Zhang Xian lifted the cup, sniffed the aroma, and downed it in one gulp.
He smacked his lips theatrically.
“Tsk.
Tasteless.
What a tragedy.”
He refilled his cup.
“It’s not often I see you, Ancestor Master, in such an elegant mood, drinking alone on a mountain peak.
As your disciple’s disciple, isn’t it my duty to accompany you for a drink?
Filial piety and all that.”
“You are very clever.” The young man set down his wine pot, his gaze deepening.
“I am curious.
How did you guess it was me?”
Zhang Xian shook his head, feigning helplessness.
“I didn’t guess.
The one who figured it out was my Master—your beloved disciple, Li Fuxi.”
“Oh?” A flicker of surprise passed through the young man’s eyes, quickly replaced by keen interest.
“Xi’er?
How did she deduce it?”
Zhang Xian didn’t answer immediately.
He toyed with the jade cup in his hand, his gaze drifting toward the rolling sea of clouds in the distance as if stalling for time.
“Ancestor Master, you seem quite leisurely.
What exactly are you waiting for?”
The young man picked up his own cup, gently swirling the clear liquid.
His voice was flat, yet it carried a bone-chilling coldness.
“Naturally, I am waiting for the annihilation of the Yunmiao Sect.”
The moment the words left his lips, his hand froze.
Without warning, he pressed his index and middle fingers together into a sword mudra and tapped the air in front of him.
BANG!
A beam of golden sword aura erupted point-blank!
Zhang Xian’s figure retreated instantly, blurring with speed, but he was still half a beat too slow.
His left arm and half of his chest exploded.
Metal fragments and leaking spiritual energy sprayed into the air.
The golden sword aura carried a strange, corrosive white mist that latched onto the remaining half of his body.
In seconds, the puppet lost all spirituality, melting into a puddle of metallic sludge.
Clang.
The dim puppet core dropped to the ground, bouncing once before rolling to a stop.
The entire process was lightning-fast.
From the young man’s strike to the puppet’s total destruction, it took less than a breath.
But the puppet had bought enough time.
Almost at the exact moment of impact, the massive flying ship hovering above the peak roared to life.
The main cannon port on its underbelly lit up with a blinding, sun-like radiance.
BOOM!
A pillar of blazing white light, charged with enough energy to level a mountain, crashed down toward the young man with a deafening roar.
Facing this apocalyptic strike, the young man merely flicked the sword in his left hand.
A golden crescent moon, thin as a cicada’s wing, materialized out of thin air.
It expanded against the wind, instantly transforming into a colossal arc of golden light that spanned the heavens.
CRACK!
The golden crescent collided with the white energy beam.
Like a hot knife through butter, it split the terrifying pillar of light in two.
The golden arc continued its upward momentum, unabated, and slashed viciously into the hull of the flying ship.
SCREECH—!
The sound of tearing metal screamed across the sky.
The luxurious vessel, built with countless precious materials and defensive arrays, was sliced open like paper.
Violent sword qi rampaged through the breach, shredding the internal structure.
The ship groaned and disintegrated, raining countless fragments and burning debris down onto Spirit Sword Peak.
The young man’s brow furrowed almost imperceptibly.
Through the falling debris, he noticed something wrong.
The Golden Swastika Formation he had secretly laid—intended to envelop the entire Yunmiao Sect—was currently blocked.
A massive screen of light had appeared out of nowhere, covering his trap.
Runes flickered across this barrier, emitting a powerful, purifying vitality that tangled with his golden formation, preventing it from activating fully.
“Six Paths Buddha Light?” A trace of surprise flashed in the young man’s eyes.
“High-level Buddhist magic?”
WHOOSH!
A dazzling streak of light shot toward the peak, faster than before.
It slammed into the ground near the young man, kicking up a cloud of dust.
As the dust settled, Zhang Xian’s true body was revealed.
His aura was steady, his expression calm.
He didn’t seem the least bit heartbroken over the destruction of his expensive puppet or the priceless flying ship.
“Ancestor Master, we were having such a nice chat.
Why the sudden violence?
That’s hardly proper guest etiquette.”
For the first time, the young man’s gaze turned grave.
He looked Zhang Xian up and down.
“How did you return from the Spirit Ruins so quickly?”
Zhang Xian didn’t answer.
He just smiled.
Crack!
A crisp sound echoed as the space beside Zhang Xian rippled like water.
From the center of the distortion, a graceful figure clad in a white sword robe with gold trim stepped out.
It was Li Fuxi.
Her face was frost-cold, her eyes locked onto the young, unfamiliar face of Wang Chuan.
Her voice trembled with suppressed emotion.
“Master... it has been a long time.”
The moment he saw Li Fuxi, the young man understood.

He hadn’t expected the brat to possess more than one of such priceless items—and be willing to burn them just to use as a glorified bus ticket.

chapters.title: Chapter 176 The Code Phrase Matches
paragraphs: “Eldest Senior Brother, why don’t we come up with a secret code?”
“A code? What for?”
“You know... something Master won’t notice. Like, every morning during lessons, you can say that thing you said yesterday: ‘You cultivated diligently yesterday, didn’t slack off, right?'”
“And then?”

“Stupid! Of the three of us, your Spiritual Sense is the strongest. The moment you say that phrase, Little Fuxi and I will know Master is nearby, secretly checking on us. Then we won’t get caught slacking off!”
“Uh... so basically, you want me to help you be lazy?”
“It’s a great idea! Xi’er listens to Second Senior Sister!”
“Sigh. You two are hopeless.”
Thinking back to that innocent afternoon, tears streamed down Li Fuxi’s face uncontrollably.
That phrase... it was carved into her bones. For years, every time she or her Second Senior Sister heard it, they would jolt to attention, putting on their best behavior.
She never expected that her Eldest Senior Brother, Wang Pan, would use those exact words to wake her up from her delusion.

Wang Pan must have realized his fate before he died. In a desperate final gambit, he must have forcibly erased his own memories regarding the meaning of the code, leaving only the instinct to say the phrase. He gambled on a one-in-ten-thousand chance that the message would get through.
Wang Chuan’s face revealed a complex expression, tinged with a trace of genuine regret.

“What a disciple Wang Pan was... truly worthy of being the one I valued most. I admit, I was too clever for my own good. I shouldn’t have refined him into a puppet; it dulled his brilliance.” He sighed softly, like an artist lamenting a microscopic flaw in a masterpiece.

Hearing Wang Chuan discuss Wang Pan’s tragic sacrifice so lightly—regretting only the imperfection of the tool, not the death of the person—incinerated the last shred of Li Fuxi’s attachment to her teacher.
“Master!”
She took a fierce step forward. The spirit sword in her hand erupted with a piercing, bone-chilling light. The tip pointed directly at Wang Chuan’s throat, her voice trembling with apoplectic fury.
“That is the last time I will ever call you that! What exactly were we to you?”

“Were we just cauldrons you meticulously cultivated? Stepping stones for you to reach the pinnacle? Or has [Desire] completely devoured your soul, extinguishing your last shred of humanity? Is power really that important? Important enough to betray the Sect, refine living beings into monsters, and butcher your own disciples?”
Wang Chuan calmly watched the tears rolling down Li Fuxi’s cheeks. In the freezing aura of her sword, the tears solidified into ice crystals, falling to the ground with a soft clatter.
His eyes held no fluctuation. His voice remained flat, terrifyingly even.
“Very important.”

He paused, deciding that further explanation was a waste of breath. “Your [Nine Revolutions Jade Condensation Scripture] is broken. Your Yin energy is no longer pure. To me, your value has greatly diminished. For the sake of our past master-disciple relationship, I can spare your life today.”
Then, his gaze snapped to Zhang Xian. The indifference vanished, replaced by a sharp, chilling killing intent.
“But this kid... he is deep, scheming, and holds too many hidden cards. He has ruined my grand plans. Since he actively returned to seek death, I cannot let him live.”
The moment the last word left his mouth, Wang Chuan’s figure blurred.
WHOOSH!
He vanished, leaving only a faint afterimage.
The real Wang Chuan appeared instantly in front of Zhang Xian, as if he had teleported. A palm wrapped in blinding golden light slammed viciously toward Zhang Xian’s skull.
BOOM!
The expected shower of blood and brain matter did not happen.

At the critical moment, Zhang Xian had summoned an ancient, bronze buckler shield. He braced it with both arms, forcefully blocking the sure-kill palm strike. A violent shockwave exploded outward, centering on the two combatants.

Zhang Xian was blasted backward, his boots carving deep grooves into the stone floor as he slid back thirty feet. He shook out his numb arms, took a deep breath, and stared sharply into Wang Chuan’s clear, unclouded eyes.
“Old thing! You aren’t being controlled by [Desire] at all, are you? You still have your sanity and your schemes. Good. That means I won’t have any psychological burden when I kill you.”
“Kill me?” Wang Chuan looked at him as if he had heard the world’s funniest joke. “With what? Your money?”
Behind him, Li Fuxi moved.
She thrust her sword, a lethal strike aimed at his back.
CLANG!
A golden halo materialized behind Wang Chuan, easily parrying the blade. The halo rotated like a grinder, dissipating her icy sword energy into nothingness.
“Your sword momentum is decent. But unfortunately, Xi’er, your foundation... it all originates from me.” Wang Chuan’s voice was flat, carrying the tone of a teacher grading a paper.

He struck out with his left palm, unleashing a force like a collapsing mountain to suppress Zhang Xian. Simultaneously, his right hand formed a sword mudra. A beam of golden sword aura shot backward, striking the exact weak point in Li Fuxi’s technique.
RIP!
The protective water screen of the [Cloud Mist Sword Scripture] was torn apart like wet paper. The sharp sword energy grazed her temple, severing several strands of her black hair.
“To be able to stir celestial phenomena at the Golden Core stage... Xi’er, your talent is truly unmatched in the Southern Region.”

Wang Chuan glanced at the freezing rain beginning to fall from the sky. A flash of appreciation crossed his eyes before freezing over. “But thinking you can defeat me with my own techniques? A fool’s dream.”
“Times have changed.”
Li Fuxi’s eyes were cold, devoid of fear.
She tapped the ground and ascended into mid-air, her spirit sword pointing directly at the heavens.

The dark thunderclouds hanging over the peak lowered, suffocating the light. Countless ice crystals, shimmering with lethal cold, poured down like a torrential rainstorm. Each crystal contained enough freezing qi to shatter steel.
Facing this overwhelming bombardment, Wang Chuan snorted.
He formed a seal with one hand. The void behind him instantly filled with densely packed, illusory sword shadows. They arranged themselves into a massive fan, their tips pointing skyward.
The Spirit Ruins Sword Sect’s Ultimate Technique: [Myriad Spirits Return to Ruin].
“Go.”
With a low command, the countless sword shadows shot upward like a reverse waterfall, crashing into the descending rain of ice.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
Dense explosions rang out incessantly. Ice crystals and sword shadows collided violently in mid-air, the shockwaves turning the mountaintop into a cratered wasteland.
However, the moment the ice crystals were shattered, the trap was sprung.
The core of every shattered ice crystal suddenly erupted with dazzling golden light.

Hidden inside the ice were streaks of golden sword aura. Freed from their shells, they accelerated abruptly, tearing through Wang Chuan’s sword shadows and shooting toward him in a concentrated barrage.
It was Wang Chuan’s own signature move: [Heavenly Gate Azure Cloud Sword].
“Hmph! Petty tricks!”
Wang Chuan’s pupils contracted slightly. He hadn’t expected Li Fuxi to fuse her Water and Metal Spiritual Roots to such a seamless degree.
Golden light blazed around his body. He prepared to form his strongest protective barrier to tank the damage.
But suddenly, his instincts screamed. He involuntarily glanced at Zhang Xian.

There, standing thirty feet away, was Zhang Xian. In his hand was a thick stack of Earth-Grade Thunder Talismans—enough to level a small city. He was grinning, waiting for the exact moment Wang Chuan stopped moving to defend against the rain.
That little bastard.
Wang Chuan’s eyebrow twitched. He had no desire to become a stationary target for a bombardment of money.
Forced to abandon his defense, his figure moved like a ghost, weaving rapidly through the storm of golden sword auras, dodging rather than blocking.
Finally, spotting an opening, he twisted his body in mid-air. Abandoning Li Fuxi, he rushed straight at Zhang Xian.
He drew a pitch-black longsword from his sleeve. With the momentum to sever mountains and rivers, he slashed viciously at the wealthy nuisance.
Zhang Xian did not dodge.

The seemingly ordinary longsword in his hand suddenly lit up, five-colored spiritual light flowing along the blade like liquid glass. Simultaneously, the defensive arrays of several Spirit Treasures on his body activated, forming layer upon layer of light shields.
CLANG——!!!
The two swords clashed, erupting with a deafening roar.
This time, Wang Chuan’s expression finally changed.
He clearly felt his overwhelming Nascent Soul spiritual power flooding into his blade... only to vanish the moment it touched Zhang Xian’s sword. It was being dissolved.

chapters.title: Chapter 177 Might As Well Observe On The Spot
paragraphs: What baffled Wang Chuan most was the sword itself.

The blade managed to channel five contradictory elemental attributes simultaneously, a feat that completely overturned his understanding of cultivation theory. Furthermore, the spiritual pressure radiating from the weapon, combined with the absurdly sturdy protective barrier around Zhang Xian, suggested a grade of artifact far beyond ordinary Spirit Treasures.
There’s something wrong with this kid’s gear, Wang Chuan thought, his eyes narrowing.
With a thought, a white mist dense with Life Essence slithered along his own blade, extending toward Zhang Xian’s spirit sword like a viper. He intended to corrode the weapon directly.
However, the moment that usually unstoppable Life Essence touched Zhang Xian’s blade, it hissed and evaporated into nothingness.
“Save your energy, Ancestor,” Zhang Xian grinned, his expression shouting nouveau riche arrogance. “This is an Immortal Artifact. Your cheap parlor tricks can’t corrode it.”
Wang Chuan ignored the taunt. He knew the brat was full of lies, but his methods were undeniably bizarre.
He abruptly expanded his Divine Sense, sweeping over the entirety of the Yunmiao Sect in an instant. The feedback sent a shockwave through his mind.

Spirit Sword Peak was no longer just a mountain; it was a fortress wrapped in layer upon layer of formation screens, each emitting a soft, golden radiance. These formations were nested like intricate clockwork, channeling an endless stream of energy that specifically suppressed the corrosive properties of his Life Essence.
“Pure World Buddha Light?”

Wang Chuan understood instantly, a cold glint exploding in his eyes. “So that’s it. You extracted Jianchen’s memories and established a grand formation specifically targeting the flaws of my cultivation technique. Zhang Xian... you are truly calculating.”
Despite the revelation, the absolute confidence of a mid-stage Nascent Soul cultivator kept panic at bay.
He was still certain he could kill Zhang Xian right here, wipe out the Yunmiao Sect, and retreat without a scratch.
Wang Chuan stopped holding back.
His sword light cascaded like a waterfall, drowning the peak in lethal radiance.

He switched targets fluidly. One moment, his strikes were vicious and tricky, aiming for the weak points in Li Fuxi’s fused swordsmanship. The next, he would snap toward Zhang Xian, unleashing fierce blows at his vital points.

Li Fuxi pushed her dual Heavenly Spiritual Roots to their limit. Her Sword Intent grew sharper, more perfect with every exchange. Though her cultivation realm was inferior, her Sword Heart was clear and bright, allowing her to barely withstand Wang Chuan’s storm-like offensive.
Zhang Xian, on the other hand, fought like an unkillable pay-to-win player.
Every inch of his body shimmered with the light of various Spirit Treasures. When Wang Chuan blasted his protective barrier, the shield would shudder violently and dim.
But then Zhang Xian would casually toss a pill into his mouth or crush a talisman.
Flash.
In the blink of an eye, the dim shield would blaze back to full strength.

The five-colored spirit sword in his hand was even more treacherous. It moved with a mind of its own, parrying Wang Chuan’s killing moves from impossible angles and occasionally launching a counterattack that forced the Nascent Soul ancestor to divert his attention.
As the battle dragged on, horror began to creep into Wang Chuan’s heart.
The resilience of these two ants far exceeded his imagination. Li Fuxi’s talent was heaven-defying; her raw damage output was approaching the threshold of the Nascent Soul realm.
And Zhang Xian? The kid was a bottomless pit.
Earth-Grade pills, high-tier talismans, rare Spirit Treasures—he threw them out as if they were garbage. His recovery rate was actually faster than Wang Chuan’s own reliance on Life Essence!
Even more alarming was Zhang Xian’s physical state.

A pale black flame burned faintly around his body. Driven by extreme Wind spiritual power, his speed and strength had climbed to an unbelievable level. His attacks were simply too fast for a Golden Core cultivator.
What kind of Golden Core stage is this? Even an ordinary early Nascent Soul cultivator might not match this intensity.
BANG!
Wang Chuan slammed another palm against Zhang Xian’s protective barrier. With a crisp CRACK, the shield finally shattered.
But Wang Chuan’s eyes twitched.
Inside the shattered shield... was another shield.
Zhang Xian used the impact force to slide backward, casually flinging a handful of Thunder Talismans into Wang Chuan’s face as a parting gift.

A shadow passed over Wang Chuan’s face. He realized he actually couldn’t break through. This brat’s defensive treasures were like infinite nesting dolls; break one layer, and there was always another. He was as tough as a ten-thousand-year-old turtle.
Forcing down the urge to curse like a sailor, a thought took root in Wang Chuan’s mind: I can’t drag this out.
He began to consider retreating.

It wasn’t fear. It was pragmatism. The battle had lost its meaning. Wang Chuan was a man of purpose; fighting a war of attrition in an enemy trap was foolish. Even if he won, the cost would outweigh the gains.
The Southern Domain was vast. He could always find another chance to kill them later.
Swoosh!
Wang Chuan’s figure shot backward. The space around him began to fluctuate violently as he prepared to tear open a void rift and teleport away.
But just as he was about to slip into the void, a phantom image of a massive chessboard manifested in the sky above the peak without warning.
The board was dotted with stars, radiating an ancient, majestic pressure.
A powerful restraining force slammed down.
The fluctuating space around Wang Chuan solidified instantly, like a lake freezing over in a heartbeat. His teleportation technique was forcibly interrupted.
“What?”
Wang Chuan’s expression turned utterly dark. He jerked his head up at the colossal chessboard in the sky, then looked down at Zhang Xian.
“Ancestor, leaving so soon?”

Zhang Xian stood amidst the chaos, dusting off his robes. “This [Star Dou Spirit Locking Array] is an import from the Central Continent’s Tianyuan Alliance. Just to keep a mighty Nascent Soul expert like you trapped for an hour costs me nearly ten thousand high-grade Spirit Stones. So... do you think I got my money’s worth?”
Only then did Wangchuan realize Zhang Xian hadn’t been joking earlier. He truly intended to kill him here.
“It seems you have gone to great pains,” Wang Chuan said, his voice dropping to a dangerous baritone. “You prepared for this for a long time.”

“Of course it took a long time!” Zhang Xian’s eyes sharpened like knives. “And not just here. Shangjing City, Cloud Raiment City, even the Shanchan Monastery—I set up a trap at every single location. I was just waiting for you, old man, to come knocking and throw yourself into the net!”
“Hahahaha!”
Wang Chuan didn’t rage. instead, he threw his head back and laughed. The sound was filled with absurdity and disbelief.
“Good! Good! Good! Today, I have truly been underestimated! A mere Golden Core dares to dream of keeping me here?”
His laughter cut off abruptly.
“Arrogant! Utterly arrogant!”
Boom!

An even more terrifying aura erupted from his body, a pressure heavy enough to crush the sky and earth. The entire Spirit Sword Peak trembled violently. A floating pavilion on a nearby precipice couldn’t withstand the shockwave; with a thunderous rumble, it collapsed and plummeted into the abyss.
Outside the formation, atop Qingmu Peak.
Liu Qingxuan, Liu Huaigu, and the masses of Yunmiao Sect disciples watched the direction of Spirit Sword Peak with grave expressions.
Although separated by layers of formation screens, the earth-shattering roars and the violent energy fluctuations of a mid-stage Nascent Soul battle were clearly transmitted to them.
Liu Qingxuan clenched her fists, her beautiful eyes filled with worry.

Not long ago, Zhang Xian’s main body had suddenly appeared beside her, dropped a hasty command—”Evacuate everyone from Spirit Sword Peak and activate the highest level of the mountain protection array”—and vanished. Moments later, the apocalypse had started atop the peak.
Liu Huaigu’s face was pale, his eyes wide with shock and helplessness.
He had been at the ninth layer of the Golden Core for years. But feeling the shockwaves from the peak, he finally understood the chasm between himself and a true powerhouse.
The combat power displayed by Zhang Xian and Li Fuxi had completely transcended the scope of the Golden Core realm. And the figure they were besieging was powerful to the point of despair.
“Father, we...” Liu Qingxuan started.
Liu Huaigu stared at the peak, shrouded in chaotic light, and slowly shook his head. “This battle is beyond our ability to intervene. Going up there rashly would only add to their burden.”
He turned to the disciples behind him. “Stop gawking. Organize the evacuation immediately.”
However, the well-known writer Lu Renbing did the opposite.
He casually pulled a small folding stool out of his storage ring and sat down on the cliff edge.

“Old Peak Master, you jest,” Lu Renbing said with a fatalistic shrug. “If Zhang Xian loses, we have absolutely no chance of survival. Against a Nascent Soul monster, running a hundred miles or a thousand makes no difference—we’re dead either way.”
He patted his knees comfortably. “We might as well preserve some dignity and observe on the spot.”
Hearing this, the other disciples paused, then nodded in agreement.
Liu Qingxuan couldn’t help but manage a faint smile. Through her spiritual sense, she realized it wasn’t just Qingmu Peak.
On all the surrounding peaks, scattered disciples were staying put. They gathered at the periphery of the formation, terrified but mesmerized, witnessing a battle that would shock the world.

chapters.title: Chapter 178 Art is Explosion
paragraphs: The sky above Spirit Sword Peak warped and twisted.

When Wang Chuan released the unbridled pressure of a fifth-stage Nascent Soul cultivator, the mountain itself groaned under the weight. The air solidified instantly, crushing down on every inch of space like a physical hammer.
Zhang Xian and Li Fuxi exchanged a glance. Both saw the same grim realization in the other’s eyes: Wang Chuan was far stronger than he had been at the Demon Subjugation Assembly three years ago.
“Xi’er, let’s start with you.”

A cold light exploded in Wang Chuan’s eyes as he lunged. His assessment was brutal and precise: Zhang Xian was a cockroach—an unkillable nuisance with endless defensive treasures. Li Fuxi, however, was a glass cannon. Her swordsmanship was divine, but her defense was fragile. She was the core of their offense.
If she died, Zhang Xian would be nothing more than a turtle waiting to be cracked.
Wang Chuan’s sword light split into thousands of fractals, sealing off every possible escape route for the sword maiden.
Zhang Xian tried to intercept, but Wang Chuan didn’t even look at him. He simply threw out a backhanded palm strike.
BOOM!
The strike carried the vast, oceanic power of a mid-stage Nascent Soul. It was like a mountain collapsing. Zhang Xian’s sword light shattered instantly, and he was swatted out of the air like a fly.
Li Fuxi gritted her teeth. Her spirit sword danced, weaving layers of water curtains as she pushed the [Cloud Mist Sword Scripture] to its absolute limit.
But the gap in cultivation was an impassable chasm.
Amidst the cacophony of metal clashing against metal, a sickening thud resonated.

Li Fuxi couldn’t block it all. A beam of tricky sword qi pierced her defense, tearing into her shoulder. If not for her defensive artifacts flaring to life and neutralizing the bulk of the impact, that single strike would have taken her arm.
She stifled a groan, plummeting from the sky and stumbling several steps before steadying herself on the rocky ground.
Wang Chuan had the upper hand instantly.

Zhang Xian took a deep breath. The [Shadow Flame] burning around him roared to life, the black fire expanding until it nearly consumed him. He was pushing the secret technique to its breaking point, burning resources to forcibly elevate his aura past the shackles of the Golden Core, touching the hem of the Nascent Soul realm.
Li Fuxi looked up at Wang Chuan, who hovered like a descending demon god. Then she glanced at Zhang Xian, who was practically immolating himself with Shadow Flame.
A flash of resolve hardened her gaze.
Without hesitation, she retrieved two pills from her storage ring: a Taichu Creation Pill and an Earth-Grade Spirit Recovery Pill.
She tossed them back and swallowed.

Simultaneously, her hands flew through a series of seals. A violent, scorched-earth energy detonated within her meridians. Her aura skyrocketed like a launched rocket—Half-step Nascent Soul, First Stage, Second Stage.
Piercing blue-gold light radiated from her skin like burning ice.

The cost was astronomical. An unnatural flush stained her cheeks as she overdrew her Life Essence and soul power. Since she had already consumed a [Taichu Creation Pill] three years ago during her “Jade Shattering” moment, her body had built a resistance. The second pill’s efficacy was slashed in half.
She could feel the clock ticking in her blood. This state would last less than a hundred breaths.
“Hmph. Death throes.”

Wang Chuan watched their auras surge, outwardly calm but internally alarmed. The potential of these two juniors was terrifying. If he hadn’t been cautious enough to accumulate power in seclusion before attacking, he might have actually capsized in the gutter today.
He didn’t wait. He dove toward Li Fuxi again. He had to snap this spent arrow before she could fire.
The three collided once more. The sky filled with flashing spiritual lights, a chaotic stalemate of desperate offense against overwhelming power.
Suddenly, Zhang Xian shouted.
“Fall!”
He pointed his spirit sword at the heavens.
CRACK!
A thick bolt of purple lightning tore through the clouds, hammering down straight toward Wang Chuan’s skull.

“Purple Firmament Dragon’s Roar True Words?” Wang Chuan sneered, disdain dripping from his voice. “That Nascent Soul brat from the Lingxu Sword Sect is ten times stronger than you, and even he couldn’t scratch me. You think you can?”
He swung his sword casually. A golden wave of sword qi surged upward, shattering the lightning bolt with effortless grace.
“How long can you maintain this boosted state? A hundred breaths? Fifty? The moment your technique fades, you die.”
Li Fuxi bit her lip until it bled, remaining silent. His eyes were too sharp. Her limit was indeed fifty breaths.
Zhang Xian ignored the taunt. He shouted again.
“Bind!”
This time, it wasn’t a single bolt. Countless serpentine arcs of purple electricity wove together in the air, instantly forming a massive electrified net that descended over the peak.
“Petty tricks!”
Wang Chuan swept his golden longsword horizontally, unleashing a crescent of energy that obliterated the net, tearing a massive hole in the lightning cage.
But the moment the net exploded—
Whoosh! Whoosh! Whoosh!
Five figures shot out from the dissipating lightning like ghosts.

They were five identical Zhang Xians, all fully geared, all emanating the powerful aura of the peak Golden Core stage. They moved in perfect unison, encircling Wang Chuan and unleashing a barrage of artifact attacks.
“Puppets?”
Wang Chuan’s pupils constricted. He recognized this as one of Zhang Xian’s trump cards. He didn’t dare be negligent—being besieged by five peak-level puppets was dangerous even for him.
He raised his sword to parry, planning to dismantle them one by one.
But the moment he moved, the five Zhang Xian puppets began to glow.
A blinding, heart-stopping light erupted from their cores. The scent of imminent annihilation filled the air.
“FUCK!!”
Wang Chuan’s composure shattered. He cursed internally, recognizing the move instantly. Self-destruction again?!
He didn’t think. He tried to retreat immediately.

But the puppets were positioned with lethal precision. Their energy signatures overlapped, creating a sealed kill box. Wang Chuan only had time to push his protective aura to the absolute maximum and ram toward the weakest point of the encirclement.
BOOM——!!!
Five earth-shattering explosions merged into one.
A tsunami of destructive energy swept outward, vaporizing rocks and shaking Spirit Sword Peak to its foundations.

Wang Chuan tore through the edge of the blast radius, but the shockwave still hammered him. He grunted, blood trickling from the corner of his mouth. His qi churned violently; he had taken actual damage.
But before he could even stabilize his stance—
Zhang Xian and Li Fuxi were on him.
Relentless as maggots in the bone, they seized the fleeting opening, launching a synchronized assault.

Wang Chuan roared in fury and shock. He forcibly suppressed his roiling qi, knocking Zhang Xian’s five-colored sword aside with a brute-force swing. Then, with a backhand motion, he executed an exquisite [Moon Gazing Stance], thrusting his blade directly at Li Fuxi’s heart.
It was a fatal counter.
However.
Facing death, Li Fuxi didn’t dodge.
She didn’t block.
She stepped into the blade, allowing the golden longsword to punch clean through her abdomen.
Thuck.
Simultaneously, her hand clamped down on Wang Chuan’s sword arm like an iron vice.
“What?”
Alarm bells screamed in Wang Chuan’s mind.
I’ve been played.
The texture was wrong. The blood was wrong. This wasn’t Li Fuxi.
It was another puppet.
In his panic to deal with Zhang Xian and the five suicide bombers, he had lost track of the real bodies.
“Explode,” Zhang Xian’s voice cut through the chaos, cold and devoid of mercy.

Locked in the grip of the false Li Fuxi, Wang Chuan watched in horror as the “woman” before him swelled. Her torso glowed with the blinding radiance of several mid-grade Spirit Treasures reaching critical mass.
Zero distance.
Point-blank range.
Wang Chuan’s roar was swallowed by the light.

Simultaneously, her hand clamped down on Wang Chuan’s sword arm like an iron vice.
“What?”
Alarm bells screamed in Wang Chuan’s mind.
I’ve been played.
The texture was wrong.
The blood was wrong.
This wasn’t Li Fuxi.
It was another puppet.
In his panic to deal with Zhang Xian and the five suicide bombers, he had lost track of the real bodies.
“Explode,” Zhang Xian’s voice cut through the chaos, cold and devoid of mercy.
Locked in the grip of the false Li Fuxi, Wang Chuan watched in horror as the “woman” before him swelled.
Her torso glowed with the blinding radiance of several mid-grade Spirit Treasures reaching critical mass.
Zero distance.
Point-blank range.
Wang Chuan’s roar was swallowed by the light.

chapters.title: Chapter 179 All Dharmas Are Like Illusions
paragraphs: The second explosion was exponentially more violent than the first.
A blinding sphere of white light devoured the peak, obliterating sound and vision alike. Wang Chuan’s protective spiritual light held for a fraction of a second before shattering like glass.
“Gah—!”
A massive fountain of blood erupted from his mouth. Wang Chuan was blasted backward, slamming into a distant cliff face with enough force to collapse the rock wall, burying him instantly.
Despite his tyrannical Nascent Soul physique, he was riddled with terrifying wounds. Bone was visible in a dozen places, and his blood gushed like a broken spring.
“Cough... cough...”
Wang Chuan struggled to crawl out of the rubble. He was drenched in crimson, his aura flickering like a candle in the wind. His eyes were wide with shock and disbelief.

He had operated from the shadows for years, a puppet master manipulating the Southern Domain. He had never suffered such a catastrophic injury. And he certainly never imagined he would be driven to the brink of death by two Golden Core juniors.
But Zhang Xian and Li Fuxi gave him no time to breathe.
Sword light, sharp and cold, heralded their arrival as they pounced for the kill.
Am I really going to die here?
For the first time, a spike of genuine terror pierced Wang Chuan’s heart. He forcibly rallied his remaining spiritual power, staggering to his feet to defend himself.
He was, after all, a Fifth-Stage Nascent Soul expert. Even heavily injured, a starving camel was still bigger than a horse. His counterattacks were heavy and desperate.
Zhang Xian and Li Fuxi, meanwhile, were running on fumes. The explosive power they had gained from pills and secret arts began to recede. Their auras dipped.
They’ve reached their limit! Confidence surged back into Wang Chuan’s veins. I can win this.
Right at that moment—
“Master.”
A familiar voice whispered in his ear.
Wang Chuan’s soul juddered. A tall, honest-looking figure materialized from the smoke. It was his eldest disciple, the one he had once valued above all others—Wang Pan.
“What?”
In that split second of stunned confusion, the “Wang Pan” spread his arms.
A thick, earthy-yellow dome of light instantly condensed, trapping both of them inside.
[Xuanhuang Zhenyue Pan]!
Simultaneously, the familiar, blinding light of a self-destruct sequence ignited within Wang Pan’s chest.
“You little beast! Using the same trick twice?! Break!”
Wang Chuan roared in fury, slashing his sword viciously at the earthen shield.
CRACK!
The shield shattered on impact.
But the moment the shards fell away, Wang Chuan’s pupils shrank to the size of needles.
Outside the shattered shield... was another shield.
And standing outside that shield was a second Wang Pan.
How many puppets does he have? How many bloody Spirit Treasures?!
He raised his sword to slash at the second [Xuanhuang Zhenyue Pan].
Too late.
Inside the second shield, a second point-blank detonation erupted.

This time, the horror was absolute. The explosion was contained within the narrow, unbreakable confines of the outer shield. The energy had nowhere to go but inward, compressed to the extreme, wasting not a single joule of destructive force.
“PFFT—!!!”
Wang Chuan was like a withered leaf tossed into a blast furnace.
The destructive energy tore through his flesh, incinerating his remaining defenses. He couldn’t even scream; the agony was too total, too consuming.
The dust hadn’t even settled when the next wave arrived.
Zhang Xian and his remaining puppets stood at the edge of the crater. In their hands were thick stacks of Earth-Grade Thunder Talismans.
With the casual motion of feeding fish in a pond, they threw them.
Hundreds of talismans, worth a king’s ransom, rained down into the pit as if they were worthless paper.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
The summit of Spirit Sword Peak transformed into a thunder purgatory. Lightning poured down like a torrential storm, turning the crater into a blinding pool of electric death.
At first, a faint glimmer of spiritual light struggled to survive in the pit.
It lasted less than three breaths.
Crack!
The light shattered.
“AAAAHHH—!!!”
A shrill, inhuman wail pierced through the thunder.

For a cultivator like Wang Chuan, whose power relied on [Desire] and corrupted Life Essence, the pure Yang energy of lightning was anathema. It dealt double damage. This wasn’t just physical pain; it was the ultimate torture of having his very soul scorched and purified.
He tried to beg. He tried to struggle. But the relentless bombardment reduced him to a howling beast.
Zhang Xian watched with an impassive face. He didn’t stop.
Dead or alive, the rule was simple: empty the inventory first.
Only when the last puppet threw its final talisman did Zhang Xian wave his sleeve, summoning a breeze to clear the smoke.
At the bottom of the scorched pit, a charred, humanoid shape lay curled in the fetal position.
The skin was carbonized, emitting a pungent stench of burnt meat. Half his face was burned away, leaving bone exposed. One eye stared blankly at the sky; the other was a hollow, black cavern.
His mouth hung open, emitting a leaking, wheezing sound. “Hhh... hhh...”

He had been on the verge of death after the second contained explosion. He had planned to swallow pills or use a blood escape art. But the rain of thunder talismans had extinguished that hope completely.
Li Fuxi dragged her exhausted body to the edge of the pit.

She looked down at the unrecognizable piece of charcoal. Tears slid silently down her cheeks. This thing... this monster... was once her revered master. The man who had led her onto the path of immortality.
“Hhh... save... save...”
The charcoal-like Wang Chuan seemed to sense her presence. His remaining eye swiveled with agonizing slowness to look at her. A charred, trembling hand lifted, reaching out as if to grasp a lifeline.
Li Fuxi trembled. The hand gripping her sword shook violently.
“My master died long ago,” Li Fuxi said, her voice flat and desolate. “From the moment he was parasitized by [Desire], he was dead.”
“I... I was... wrong...” Wang Chuan’s voice was broken, filled with unprecedented fear and pathetic pleading. “Blinded by desire... I’m awake now... save me...”
Then, a shadow fell over him.
It was Zhang Xian.
He crouched down at the edge of the pit, a smile on his face that looked gentle but felt colder than absolute zero.
“Grandmaster wants to turn over a new leaf? As your disciple and grand-disciple, of course we should give you a chance to reform.”
Zhang Xian’s tone was light, as if discussing the weather.
“But words are wind. Grandmaster, you’ll have to endure a little hardship. Let your grand-disciple take a peek at your memories. Just to verify your innocence, of course. How about it?”
“No... Don’t!”
Pure, unadulterated terror erupted in Wang Chuan’s single eye. He knew exactly what a Soul Search entailed—the complete destruction of the self.
“You little beast! I’d rather die than—”
He suddenly convulsed. The last dregs of power in his body surged madly toward his center. He was trying to detonate his Nascent Soul to take them all with him.
Zhang Xian grabbed Li Fuxi and prepared to flash away.
But the earth-shattering explosion never came.
Pfft.
A soft, wet sound echoed, like a rotten fruit bursting underfoot.
At Wang Chuan’s charred dantian, the spiritual core that barely maintained his life didn’t explode. Instead, it cracked open silently.
There was no blinding golden light. No majestic release of spiritual pressure.
Only a viscous, foul-smelling gray slime oozed out of the fissure, flowing like pus from an infected wound.
Wang Chuan’s expression froze, forever locked in that final moment of ferocious, impotent spite.
Li Fuxi stared blankly at the lifeless husk, then at the disgusting pool of gray sludge. Slowly, she closed her eyes.
Zhang Xian gently patted her shoulder and let out a silent sigh.
The mountain wind blew, sweeping up the scorched earth and dust, carrying with it a chill that felt like liberation.
