chapters.title: Chapter 187 Fortunately, There Was a Gullible Fool
paragraphs: The brilliance of the teleportation light faded, depositing Lin Xuanwei and Lu Yao into a suffocating darkness. It was pitch-black, the kind of absolute void where one couldn’t even see their own hand in front of their face. The air was heavy, damp, and bitingly cold, carrying the musty stench of ancient, decaying earth.
“Ah!” Lu Yao let out a short, sharp cry. Her body swayed, involuntarily leaning toward Lin Xuanwei for support.

“Miss Lu, don’t panic!” Lin Xuanwei’s voice rang out, eager to play the hero. He flipped his palm, and a cluster of soft, brilliant Spiritual Fire ignited instantly. It hovered in the air, banishing the encroaching shadows and illuminating the rugged, moss-covered walls of the cave for several zhang around them.

“Whew.” Lu Yao patted her chest, her face pale with a mix of lingering fear and delicate vulnerability. “That scared me to death. I’ve always been terrified of the dark.” As she spoke, she shrank even closer to Lin Xuanwei, her shoulder almost brushing against his.
Lin Xuanwei froze slightly at the sensation of her warmth near his arm. He quickly straightened his posture, puffing out his chest. “Rest assured. I am here.”

With a flourish, he reached into his robes and retrieved the [Connected Branches Token] that Ouyang Chen had distributed. He infused a strand of Spiritual Qi into it, expecting a signal. However, the wooden token remained inert. It didn’t light up, nor did it transmit the faintest hum of connection.
“Eh? That’s strange. Why isn’t this token reacting at all?”
Lu Yao’s expression shifted. She hurriedly produced her own token to check. The jade surface was dull and lackluster, resembling nothing more than a piece of dead wood.

“This is impossible,” she muttered. “The sensing range of the [Connected Branches Token] is massive. Even in the depths of a large secret realm, they should resonate with one another. Unless... something is forcefully suppressing the connection.”
Alarm bells rang loudly in her heart. An ominous premonition began to coil in her gut.

Seeing the gravity on Lu Yao’s face, Lin Xuanwei’s mask of confidence cracked. Panic seeped into his features. “Th-then what do we do?” he stammered, his eyes darting around the shadows nervously. The confident “I am here” demeanor from moments ago had vanished without a trace.

Seeing him crumple so easily, Lu Yao couldn’t help but roll her eyes internally. Her contempt deepened. Just a moment ago, he was acting like a fearless, arrogant young master. The moment we hit a minor snag, he falls apart. Truly, a gilded exterior hiding rotten stuffing.
She suppressed her disdain, pursed her lips, and forced a calm tone. “Don’t panic yet. We need to move. Have your puppet groom lead the way and scout ahead.”
“Wh-which way?” Lin Xuanwei asked, his voice thick with hesitation and cowardice.

Useless, Lu Yao cursed silently. She gathered her focus and attempted to spread her Divine Sense to probe their surroundings. The result made her face turn even paler. Her Divine Sense was slammed back by an invisible pressure, barely able to extend a few zhang beyond her skin.
She took a deep breath, fighting to maintain her composure. “The situation is grim. Let’s hold our position. Have your puppet pick a direction and scout it out first.”

Lin Xuanwei gave a bitter, helpless smile and spread his hands. “Miss Lu, that won’t work. My groom... he can’t leave my side. If he goes beyond a ten-zhang range, he becomes ineffective.” He pointed to a formation disk hanging at his waist, which pulsed with a weak glow. “See? He’s entirely controlled by this.”
Lu Yao felt a wave of exhaustion wash over her. She pointed resignedly toward the dark passageway on their right. “Fine. Then we walk this way together. Put the puppet in front.”
“Okay, I’ll listen to you.” Lin Xuanwei nodded vigorously, looking at her as if she were his only lifeline.

The puppet groom stepped forward silently, his heavy boots leading the way into the right-hand tunnel. Lin Xuanwei and Lu Yao followed closely behind. The pale light of the Spiritual Fire flickered in the deep, oppressive darkness, casting long, distorted shadows that danced nervously against the walls.

The passageway was winding and treacherous. After walking for roughly the time it takes an incense stick to burn, a faint glimmer of light appeared ahead. Their spirits lifted, and they quickened their pace.
The light led them into a relatively spacious stone chamber. In the center stood several decayed wooden shelves, scattered with dusty jade boxes and porcelain bottles.

Lu Yao hurried forward, carefully prying open several boxes. Empty. She grabbed a few jade bottles and pulled the stoppers. A pungent, moldy stench wafted out. The pills inside had long since shriveled into black pebbles, their Spiritual Qi completely dissipated. They were nothing but useless dregs.
“This is a storage room!” A glint of understanding flashed in Lu Yao’s eyes. “Usually, storage rooms like this aren’t too far from the master’s Secluded Cultivation chamber.”
Hearing this, Lin Xuanwei’s face lit up with delight. “Then let’s hurry! If we find his Secluded Cultivation chamber, does that mean we pass this trial?”

“Correct,” Lu Yao nodded. “According to the rules, as long as we find the Senior’s remains and properly collect them, it counts as a success—even if we haven’t fully explored the cave mansion. Once we do that, the jade talismans we carry will automatically activate their teleportation function, and we can leave this damned place.”

“Great!” Lin Xuanwei slapped his thigh. “Then what are we waiting for? Let’s clear this and get out quickly. This place... it’s for dead people. It feels eerie and creepy, makes my skin crawl. What if that Daoist Long Wu was a twisted lunatic who set up some vicious trap before he died? Wouldn’t we be doomed?” He spoke with a look of lingering fear, clutching his sleeves.

Hearing his rambling, Lu Yao’s heart skipped a beat. The failed tokens, the suppressed Divine Sense, the inability to contact Ouyang Chen—these abnormalities were piling up, gnawing at her confidence.

However, she reconsidered. Daoist Long Wu was, after all, a Senior of the Guiyuan Sect. Even if he left behind trials, he wouldn’t go so far as to murder his own sect’s juniors. His lineage’s teachings are still being passed down in the sect, after all.
Moreover, these “Keyed” cave mansions had been personally inspected by the sect’s Nascent Soul grandmasters. Unless the exploration team was pathetically weak, death was highly unlikely.

At this moment, Lu Yao had effectively become the team’s pillar. She began directing their path. Although Lin Xuanwei was a coward, he had the singular advantage of being obedient, always keeping his high-level puppet at the very front.

Along the way, they triggered several mechanisms: hidden Spiritual Arrows shooting from the gloom, floors collapsing into spike pits, and corrosive gas spraying from the walls. But every threat was easily blocked or neutralized by the Late Golden Core stage puppet.
Lu Yao secretly assessed the situation. The power of these traps is mediocre. Forget the puppet; even Lin Xuanwei, a mere Early Golden Core cultivator, could handle them if he wasn’t such a coward.

They passed through several more stone chambers: a dusty alchemy room with a cold furnace, and a study filled with decaying bookshelves where the ancient texts had long since turned to dust. Apart from some worthless junk, they found absolutely nothing.
As they proceeded without incident, Lin Xuanwei’s arrogant “young master” confidence began to return. He started intentionally drifting closer to Lu Yao, his tone carrying a hint of frivolity.
“Miss Lu, look, this cave mansion isn’t much to look at. What a waste of this young master’s Spirit Stones. But... having Miss Lu’s company makes it bearable. Not a total loss, eh?”
Lu Yao felt a surge of annoyance but responded perfunctorily, her heart heavy with disappointment.

She had roamed the Guiyuan Mountain Range for hundreds of years; she knew the signs. Having explored this far, she had basically concluded that this [Daoist Long Wu Cave Mansion] was just an ordinary, perhaps even shabby, place where a poor Senior had sat in meditation until he died.
If Senior Brother Zheng hadn’t dragged in Lin Xuanwei, this gullible fool, to foot the bill, she thought bitterly, this expedition would have been a massive financial disaster.

chapters.title: Chapter 188 Plenty of Chances to Get Intimate
paragraphs: Lu Yao finally led Lin Xuanwei to a halt before a heavy stone gate. It was sealed tight, but her eyes immediately locked onto the carvings on the adjacent wall—the embryonic texture of a Taiji symbol.

Her lips curved into a triumphant smile. She had found it. This was the specific marking that denoted the master’s Secluded Cultivation chamber. The remains of Daoist Long Wu were undoubtedly behind this stone slab.
The trial was nearly over. Not only would she clear the objective, but she was also about to collect the exorbitant bonus Lin Xuanwei had promised. Her mood soared instantly.

She spun around, fixing Lin Xuanwei with a smile that was equal parts dazzling and predatory. Her voice dropped into a sugary, coquettish register as she employed the art of sajiao. “Brother Xuanwei, I’ve done all the hard work bringing you here alone. Don’t you have a... special expression of gratitude for me?”

Lin Xuanwei blinked, looking as though her smile had blinded him. His gaze turned infatuated, a perfect mask of a smitten fool. He thumped his chest enthusiastically. “Miss Lu, rest assured! Of course I do! This Young Master is a man of his word. I’ll pay you an extra twenty thousand Middle Grade Spirit Stones, right now!”
Twenty thousand? Separately?

Lu Yao’s heart hammered against her ribs. Combined with her previous cut, this sum rivaled the total earnings of several years of life-threatening exploration. The sheer windfall made her breath hitch.
“Here!” Lin Xuanwei didn’t hesitate for a second. He fished out an exquisite storage pouch and tossed it to her as if it were a bag of trash.

Lu Yao caught the pouch, her Divine Sense sweeping into it immediately. Piles of shimmering stones greeted her mind’s eye. Twenty thousand, exactly. A shiver of pure greed ran through her body, and her smile became blindingly brilliant, her voice dripping with cloying sweetness. “Thank you, Brother Xuanwei! You’re so good to me!”

“Hahaha, this is merely a trifle!” Lin Xuanwei flicked his folding fan open with a sharp snap, fanning himself with affected elegance. He leaned in, his eyes swimming with suggestive intent. “Miss Lu, if we were to take things... a step further... this Young Master has plenty more Spirit Stones where those came from.”
A step further?

Lu Yao instantly caught the drift. She looked him over. While Lin Xuanwei was undeniably handsome, had a frighteningly deep background, and spent money like water... his core personality was that of a spineless dandy. The way he had cowered earlier was a major turn-off.
However, for the sake of Spirit Stones, she didn’t mind playing the long game. She needed to give him just enough sugar to keep him on the hook without actually swallowing the bait.
Her smile didn’t waver. “Brother Xuanwei is truly kind,” she purred, “but matters of the heart cannot be rushed. Let’s start by being... good friends.”
“Naturally, naturally,” Lin Xuanwei agreed, undeterred. “There will be plenty of opportunities to understand each other... deeply... in the future.”
“Mmh!” Lu Yao nodded vigorously, then pointed a slender finger at the gate. “Brother Xuanwei, let’s open this first. Daoist Long Wu’s remains should be inside.”
“Right, right! I don’t want to stay in this damn place a second longer.” Lin Xuanwei nodded. “Groom! Open it!”
The armored puppet stepped forward silently. It planted its heavy palms against the stone slab and shoved.
Grind—
The heavy gate groaned, slowly pivoting inward. A blast of stagnant air rushed out, carrying the smell of ancient dust mixed with a strange, metallic fishy stench.

Behind the door lay a modest meditation chamber. In the center, a figure clad in the tattered, dust-gray Daoist robes of the Guiyuan Sect sat cross-legged, facing the entrance. The flesh had long since rotted away, leaving a complete skeleton maintaining an eternal meditative posture.
“Found him!” Lu Yao’s heart leaped. She stepped forward to collect the remains.
But the moment her foot lifted, the atmosphere shattered.

On the spinal column of the dried skeleton, faint, purplish-black threads suddenly materialized without warning. They writhed like living worms, pulsating with a sickening rhythm. In the blink of an eye, the threads exploded outward like a chaotic spiderweb, wrapping around every inch of the bone, radiating an aura of pure, heart-stopping malice.
“RETREAT!!”

The moment Lu Yao saw the purple-black threads, her pupils shrank to pinpricks. Her face drained of all blood. She screamed the word, her body launching backward with the explosive speed of a startled hare.
Lin Xuanwei seemed stunned by the sudden turn of events, freezing for a split second before his survival instincts—or perhaps just panic—kicked in. He turned and scrambled after her.

Lu Yao didn’t look back. Relying on her memory of the tunnels and sheer adrenaline, she sprinted madly until she burst back into the storage room they had passed earlier. She slammed her back against the cold stone wall, chest heaving violently, gasping for air. Her eyes were fixed on the dark corridor, her longsword already drawn, the blade humming with cold light.
Moments later, Lin Xuanwei came stumbling in, his face a mask of terror.

“Don’t come any closer!” Lu Yao shrieked. Her sword tip snapped up, pointing directly at his throat. Cold killing intent poured off her. She kept a distance of several zhang, her muscles coiled like a spring.
“W-what’s wrong, Miss Lu?” Lin Xuanwei trembled, raising his hands in surrender. “W-what are you doing?”

“I said don’t move!” Lu Yao barked. To emphasize her point, she slashed her sword. A sharp beam of Sword Qi hissed through the air, slicing a deep gouge into the stone floor inches from Lin Xuanwei’s toes.
Lin Xuanwei’s knees buckled, and he nearly collapsed. “Okay! I won’t move! I won’t move! Miss Lu, what is happening? My Groom... I can’t sense the puppet anymore!”

Hum!
The jade erupted with a soft white light. Like a searchlight, the beam swept over Lin Xuanwei from head to toe. The light remained pure; there was no reaction, no dark resonance.
Only then did Lu Yao’s taut nerves snap loose. She let out a long, shuddering breath and sheathed her sword, her voice heavy with exhaustion. “Alright. You can come over.”
Lin Xuanwei looked as if he had been granted amnesty from execution. He scurried to her side, still shaking. “What the hell was that just now? My puppet... is it...”
“That was [Hatred],” Lu Yao whispered, the name tasting like ash in her mouth. Her eyes were wide with genuine fear. “Your family is in Jinyuan City... how do you not know of [Hatred]?”

“[Hatred]?” Lin Xuanwei yelped, his face losing the last of its color. “I... I’ve only heard my father mention it! He said it’s a terrifying calamity. Anyone possessed by it goes instantly mad, recognizing no one, slaughtering their own kin. But how... how could it be here?”
Lu Yao shook her head, fear lingering in her eyes. “I’ve only heard my Master and Senior Brothers speak of it. I’ve never seen it with my own eyes until today.”

“This is too bizarre,” she muttered, pacing nervously. “How could a manifestation of [Hatred] appear in Daoist Long Wu’s final resting place? This cave has a serious problem. We must terminate the trial immediately.”
Without hesitation, she produced an emergency jade token engraved with the Guiyuan Sect’s insignia and crushed it in her fist.
Crack.
A dazzling stream of light shot out from the shattered fragments, piercing through the rock and speeding toward the outside world to alert the sect.

“We’re finished. It’s over,” Lin Xuanwei moaned, his face looking like he was attending his own funeral. “My dad sent me to the Guiyuan Sect specifically to avoid the [Hatred] battlefield near Jinyuan City! He said it was safe here! And now this evil thing pops up? Is there nowhere safe in this damn world?”

Lu Yao slid down the cold wall, hugging her knees. Her face was still chalk-white. “With [Hatred] involved, this is no longer something we can handle. The only thing we can do is sit tight and wait for the Sect Elders to come save us.”

chapters.title: Chapter 189 At Most, I’ll Pay Extra for the Trouble
paragraphs: Time crawled by in the suffocating silence of the storage room. Fear hung heavy in the air, thick enough to taste.
After about a quarter of an hour, the sound of hurried, chaotic footsteps echoed from the corridor outside.
Lin Xuanwei and Lu Yao shot to their feet instantly, weapons drawn, knuckles white.
The footsteps grew louder, closer. Then, a familiar voice rang out before the figure even appeared—a distinct cultural marker of urgency.
“Junior Sister!”
Ouyang Chen and Lu Shu burst into view. They looked disheveled but unharmed.
“Senior Brother!” Lu Yao gasped, looking at Ouyang Chen as if he were a savior descended from the heavens. “What happened? Why did you crush the emergency communication talisman?”
“I saw [Hatred]!” Lu Yao’s voice trembled.
“What?”
“[Hatred]?”
The color drained from Ouyang Chen’s face. Beside him, Lu Shu stiffened.
“Miss Lu!” Lin Xuanwei suddenly shrieked, cowering behind her. “Watch out! Check them! What if they’re possessed?”

His panicked outburst snapped Lu Yao back to reality. She immediately raised the milky-white unpolished jade she had used earlier. Spiritual light flared as she scanned Ouyang Chen and Lu Shu from head to toe. Only when the jade remained pure white, confirming no trace of the dark corruption, did she finally exhale.
Ouyang Chen, realizing the gravity of the situation, pulled out his own detection artifact. He swept it over Lu Yao and Lin Xuanwei, confirming their safety in turn.

The group huddled together, their nerves fraying. Lu Yao recounted the encounter in the meditation chamber—the skeleton, the purple-black threads, the overwhelming malice. Her description left the others shaken to the core.

“So that explains it,” Ouyang Chen muttered, his expression grim. “The moment we entered the cave, we were trapped in a bizarre illusion formation. No matter which direction we chose, we ended up walking in circles. If the light from your emergency talisman hadn’t pierced the array, we would still be wandering blindly right now.”
A heavy silence fell. No one dared suggest checking the meditation chamber again.

They gathered in the center of the storage room. Ouyang Chen set up a simple defensive formation at the entrance. It hummed with faint spiritual light, offering a sliver of psychological comfort against the encroaching darkness.

Seeing the dejected, terrified looks on their faces, Ouyang Chen forced a confident expression. “Everyone, pull yourselves together. Discovering traces of [Hatred] is a massive merit in itself. The Sect will reward us heavily for this intelligence. The value of this information far exceeds whatever scrapings we might have found in an ordinary cave.”
Hearing the promise of sect contribution points and rewards, the gloom lifted slightly. Heads nodded in agreement.
“Then what about my trial?” Lin Xuanwei interjected, his voice whiny. “Does this count as a pass? I paid good money for this slot.”

Ma Kun, who had been nursing a grudge against the rich playboy since the beginning, snapped. “You should be thanking the heavens you’re still breathing! You’re worried about a pass grade? That ghostly thing could tear us to shreds in the next second!”
Lin Xuanwei shrank back, muttering resentfully under his breath, acting the part of the scolded child perfectly.

“Damn it,” Ma Kun’s voice rang out in the private Sound Transmission channel shared by the Guiyuan Sect disciples. “How could [Hatred] appear in the Guiyuan Mountains? This is too sinister! Could this kid be behind it?”

“Unlikely,” Lu Yao replied via transmission. “I saw it clearly. The [Hatred] manifested directly from Daoist Long Wu’s skeleton. Besides, this guy has been a jittery coward the entire way. No matter how good his acting is, surely he couldn’t fake that level of incompetence?”

“There’s something fishy going on,” Ouyang Chen’s voice cut in, cool and calculating. “We must remain vigilant. Don’t forget, the conflict between our Guiyuan Sect and the Heavenly Abyss Alliance has been escalating. He came from their territory. The more profound an old monster’s cultivation, the more they enjoy ‘playing the pig to eat the tiger.’ We need to find an opportunity to test him.”
In the storage room, time seemed to stretch.
The group sat within the defensive circle, senses extended, watching the dark corridor that led to the boss room.
A faint rustle broke the silence.
A small paper effigy, folded from yellow talisman paper, fluttered back from the darkness. It landed on Zheng Tong’s open palm, scorched and trembling.

Zheng Tong shook his head, his face ugly. “No good. The way back is blocked again. It’s that illusion array—my paper scout can’t find a way out.” He paused, pointing toward the meditation chamber. “And whenever the scout gets close to that room... it’s instantly annihilated by an invisible force. It didn’t even have time to react.”

Ma Kun’s expression turned thunderous. “This is completely abnormal. Junior Sister Lu sent the emergency signal ages ago. By all rights, a Nascent Soul Elder should have arrived by now. Why is it dead silent outside?”
Ouyang Chen scanned the room. His gaze lingered on Lin Xuanwei, who was huddled in the corner, pale-faced and avoiding eye contact.

He took a deep breath, suppressing the rising panic in his chest. “We can’t wait any longer. The [Hatred] entity has trapped us here; it likely has a scheme in motion. The longer we delay, the more danger we’re in.”

He switched to a commanding tone. “Based on Junior Sister Lu’s report, the [Hatred] in the meditation room is currently anchored to a corpse. It hasn’t shown active aggression yet—it seems to be dormant or gestating.”

“Add in Brother Lin’s rogue puppet, and the enemy’s active combat power should be manageable. There are six of us. As long as we are cautious, avoid direct corruption, and strike together, we can suppress it.”

The mention of the rogue puppet made Ma Kun’s temper flare again. He pointed a trembling finger at Lin Xuanwei. “It’s all because of this useless good-for-nothing! If not for him, how would we have provoked that ghost?”

Lin Xuanwei stiffened his neck, shouting back with false bravado. “How was I supposed to know?! I didn’t do it on purpose! Look, if it’s a big deal, I’ll just give you guys more Spirit Stones as compensation when we get out!”
“You think this is about Spirit Stones?!” Ma Kun roared. “We might all be buried here today!”
“Enough!” Ouyang Chen barked. “No internal strife! Brother Lin, that puppet of yours—what are its specs? Realm? Special abilities?”

“Uh... Golden Core seventh layer,” Lin Xuanwei stammered. “Water-attribute core. Skilled in sword arts. It... uh... it has a few Xuan-grade defensive talismans stuck to it. And... in a pinch, it can self-destruct a few of its magical artifacts.”
“Self-destruct magical artifacts?!” Ma Kun looked ready to have an aneurysm. “You rich bastard, I ought to—”

“Silence!” Ouyang Chen cut him off again. “Daoist Long Wu was only at the eighth layer of the Golden Core in life. Even enhanced by [Hatred], he can’t have become a god out of thin air. I will handle the skeleton and the [Hatred] corruption.”

“Junior Brother Ma, Junior Sister Lu Shu—the puppet is close to your cultivation level. You two handle it. Junior Brother Zheng, Junior Sister Lu Yao—you provide support from the center. Keep your distance. Do not engage in melee. Silently recite the Heart-Cleansing Mantra to stabilize your minds against the corruption.”
Ouyang Chen assigned tasks with rapid clarity. The Guiyuan Sect disciples, being inner sect elites, quickly shook off their panic and nodded, readying their weapons.
Suddenly, a weak voice piped up from the corner.
“Um... I don’t know the Heart-Cleansing Mantra...”
A vein throbbed violently on Ouyang Chen’s temple. He squeezed his eyes shut, fighting the urge to scream. “Then stay far away! Junior Sister Lu Yao, keep an eye on him. Don’t let him cause trouble!”
Lu Yao sighed and nodded helplessly.
After confirming the final details, the group mustered their courage. Step by step, they began to creep toward the meditation chamber.

Zheng Tong nodded, forming complex hand seals. Two paper talismans fluttered into the air, transforming into small figures that carefully pushed against the heavy stone slab.
Swish!
A beam of sharp, icy light shot out from within—the Puppet Groom, lying in ambush.
“Go!”
Ouyang Chen shouted low in his throat. His longsword erupted with blinding golden brilliance, accurately intercepting the puppet’s attack while simultaneously blasting the stone door wide open.
His gaze instantly locked onto the center of the meditation chamber.

The moment it sensed the intruders, the skeleton raised a hand, condensing the purple-black evil Qi into a twisted, jagged longsword.
It lunged.
Chaos erupted in the narrow chamber. Sword lights and the radiance of Dharma Treasures collided, sending shockwaves rippling through the air.

Although the construct had high defense and self-destruct mechanisms, it lacked the fluidity of a living cultivator. Against two opponents of similar cultivation, it was quickly suppressed.

Clang!

The beam was too fast, aiming directly for Lin Xuanwei’s dantian.

At the critical moment—
Hum!
A dazzling, brilliant golden light erupted from Lin Xuanwei’s body without warning. It formed a solid sphere, encasing him completely.
The purple-black Sword Qi slammed into the barrier. A deafening boom shook the room, and both the golden shield and the sword energy dissipated simultaneously.
“Such a powerful defensive Magical Artifact?”
Ouyang Chen caught the flash of gold from the corner of his eye but didn’t pause. He turned his focus back to the [Hatred] skeleton.
Lin Xuanwei, snapping out of his daze, scrambled on hands and knees to hide behind Lu Yao.
“Miss Lu! Save me! That scared me to death!”
Lu Yao felt a surge of disdain. Suppressing the urge to kick him away, she snapped, “Don’t cause trouble!”

The battle reached its climax. The puppet groom fought tenaciously, but it couldn’t withstand the combined assault. Lu Shu found an opening and severed its core with a precise strike. The construct collapsed, lifeless.
On the other side, Ouyang Chen saw his chance. He parried the skeleton’s blade with a backhanded slash, while his left hand slammed a shimmering golden talisman onto its forehead.
“Suppress!”

The talisman exploded into a cage of golden light, instantly trapping the purple-black skeleton. Runes flowed across the surface of the barrier, exerting a crushing pressure. Inside, the skeleton struggled violently. The purple-black threads of [Hatred] writhed like mad worms, hissing as they corroded against the holy light, but they couldn’t break free.
“Quickly!”
The team moved in perfect sync, placing Spirit Stones around the cage to reinforce the seal. The golden light stabilized, and the entity within gradually ceased its struggles.
“It’s done!”
Everyone let out a collective breath, wiping cold sweat from their brows.
Lu Shu stared at the trapped entity with lingering fear. “Is this... [Hatred]?”
“Correct,” Ouyang Chen confirmed, nodding gravely. “I have fought cultivators tainted by [Hatred] before. This venomous, frenzied aura is unmistakable.”
As he spoke, Ouyang Chen cast a subtle, imperceptible glance at Ma Kun.
Ma Kun caught the signal instantly.
He suddenly grunted, staggering back a few steps. He clutched his forehead, his face twisting in exaggerated pain. “Ugh... my head... it hurts...”
“Senior Brother Ma! What’s wrong?” Lu Yao asked immediately, her voice pitched with just the right amount of panic.
“ARGH!”

Ma Kun let out a bloodcurdling scream. Strands of black energy—feigned or summoned—surged around his body. He spun around, eyes wild, and without a word of warning, launched a palm strike directly at Lin Xuanwei.
The strike was vicious, carrying lethal killing intent.
Boom!
The golden light on Lin Xuanwei’s body flared again. His automatic defense artifact activated, barely intercepting the sneak attack. The impact sent him stumbling, gasping for air.

“Save me! Brother Ouyang! Miss Lu! He’s gone mad!” Lin Xuanwei shrieked, his soul seemingly flying out of his body in terror. He scrambled backward, trying to put distance between himself and the assailant.
“Fall back! Quickly!” Ouyang Chen roared, his face a mask of shock and anger. “Junior Brother Ma has been corrupted by [Hatred]! Get away from him!”
The group scattered immediately, leaving Lin Xuanwei isolated.
Ma Kun, seeing his first strike fail, let out a feral growl. Like a demon possessed, he pounced on Lin Xuanwei again.
Lin Xuanwei tried to defend himself, raising his arms in panic, but his meager cultivation and lack of combat experience were laughable before a Late Golden Core cultivator like Ma Kun.
The protective golden light flickered violently under Ma Kun’s storm-like assault. Lin Xuanwei was beaten back repeatedly like a sandbag, blood spraying from his mouth with every heavy blow.
Crack!
Finally, the expensive defensive artifact reached its limit. The golden barrier shattered into dust.
Ma Kun grinned savagely. He gathered his Qi into a condensed blade of light and slashed viciously across Lin Xuanwei’s chest.
“Ahhh!!”

Lin Xuanwei let out a miserable scream. His body was flung backward, slamming heavily into the cold stone wall before sliding down to the floor. A pool of bright red blood rapidly expanded beneath him.
Seeing Lin Xuanwei lying motionless in the blood, Ma Kun dropped the act instantly.
He straightened up, cracked his neck, and clicked his tongue, looking down at the unconscious body with sneering contempt. “Tsk. So fragile.”
Lu Shu frowned slightly. “Ma Kun, you went too hard.”
Ma Kun shrugged, wiping his hands. “I thought a rich young master like him would have more life-saving Dharma Treasures. I didn’t hold back. Who knew he was this useless?”
Ouyang Chen walked over, his expression impassive. “Forget it. We didn’t intend to take his life, just to test him. In a place like this, one can never be too cautious.”
The others nodded. There was no guilt on their faces, only cold calculation.

Lu Yao’s gaze lingered on Lin Xuanwei for a brief second before shifting away. She felt no remorse, only a faint regret that her cash cow was now broken. What a shame. I won’t be able to milk him for any more Spirit Stones.
“I just received a response from the Elder,” she said, changing the subject. “They should be arriving soon.”
“Good. We wait here,” Ouyang Chen decided.
Lu Shu looked at Lin Xuanwei, whose life was hanging by a thread, his breath coming in shallow, ragged gasps. “If we leave him like that... he’ll be dead in moments, won’t he?”

Zheng Tong, who usually looked like a simple, honest man, spoke up from the side. “Junior Sister Lu, he was injured by Senior Brother Ma Kun while Ma Kun was ‘possessed’ by [Hatred]. What does that have to do with us?”
His tone was flat, factual.
Ma Kun let out a low, weird chuckle.

Lu Shu sighed softly. She couldn’t quite harden her heart completely. With a wave of her hand, she cast a gentle Wood Element technique. A screen of soft green light descended over Lin Xuanwei, sealing his wounds and protecting his heart meridians, temporarily halting death’s advance.
Lu Yao curled her lip in mockery. “Hah. Look at you, playing the saint.”
“I’m just preserving his life for now,” Lu Shu replied calmly. “We’ll let the Elder decide his fate when they arrive.”

chapters.title: Chapter 191 This Is Also His Karmic Tribulation
paragraphs: Not long after, a sharp streak of light tore through the air, solidifying at the entrance of the meditation chamber. As the brilliance faded, it revealed a middle-aged Daoist nun with a stern, hawk-like visage.
It was Elder Chen of the Guiyuan Sect’s Enforcement Hall.
“Greetings, Elder Chen!” Ouyang Chen and the others bowed deeply, their posture respectful and submissive.

Elder Chen’s gaze swept over the room, landing first on the purplish-black skeleton trapped within the golden barrier. Sensing the familiar, violent, and chaotic aura radiating from it, she nodded slowly. “It is indeed [Hatred].”
Then, her eyes drifted to the corner where Lin Xuanwei lay in a pool of blood, enveloped by a faint green light screen. Her brow furrowed slightly. “What is the meaning of this?”

Ouyang Chen stepped forward. With concise precision, he recounted the events: the encounter with the entity, the suppression, and the “unfortunate accident” where Ma Kun, in his zeal to test for corruption, had critically injured Lin Xuanwei. He hid nothing.

Elder Chen listened in silence, her expression impassive. Finally, she nodded. “You did well. In such a dangerous place, one can never be too cautious. Especially regarding someone of unknown origin.”
Her tone carried a hint of approval for their ruthlessness, and total indifference toward the dying man.

Lu Shu hesitated for a moment before speaking up, her conscience nagging her. “Elder Chen... can he still be saved? If we treat him now, there is still hope. We can simply claim he was injured by the [Hatred] entity later. He doesn’t know the truth.”
Elder Chen pondered for a moment. She paced over to Lin Xuanwei, looking down at the young man whose breath was shallow and ragged.

She extended a withered finger, sending a wisp of Qi to probe his internal state. Her frown deepened. “Ma Kun, your strike was too heavy. The sword energy has invaded his heart meridians and Dantian. To save him now would require at least a Tier-4 Meridian Restoration Pill.”
Ma Kun lowered his head, his voice trembling slightly. “This disciple was worried he possessed hidden defensive artifacts and struck with full force. Please punish me, Elder.”
Elder Chen sighed lightly, her voice devoid of warmth. “Forget it. This is simply his karmic tribulation. Who told him to have such bad luck, bumping into [Hatred] of all things?”
As she spoke, she made a casual hooking motion with her finger.
Whoosh.

The Storage Bag at Lin Xuanwei’s waist detached and flew into Elder Chen’s palm. A faint spiritual light flickered at her fingertip, effortlessly erasing the weak owner restriction Lin Xuanwei had placed on it.

Her Divine Sense swept inside. The mountain-like pile of Middle Grade Spirit Stones made her eyelids twitch involuntarily. However, her face remained as placid as an ancient well. With a smooth turn of her wrist, the bag disappeared into her wide sleeve.
Ouyang Chen, Ma Kun, and the others watched with burning eyes, but no one dared to make a sound.

“Alright,” Elder Chen said, turning her back on the dying man, her authority returning. “You may leave. I will handle things here. For discovering and suppressing [Hatred], I will record a merit for your team.”
“Yes! Thank you, Elder!”
The group responded in unison, a heavy weight lifting from their hearts. They turned to leave, eager to put this mess behind them.
But the moment they turned their backs—
A calm, steady voice rang out in the silent chamber, cutting through the air like a blade.

“I seem to recall that a Meridian Restoration Pill costs only ten thousand Middle Grade Spirit Stones. Elder... that Storage Bag you just pocketed holds enough to buy several hundred of them. Are you truly so determined to watch me die?”
The air in the chamber froze instantly.
Ouyang Chen and the others stiffened, whipping their heads around in disbelief.

Elder Chen’s pupils constricted to pinpricks. Her reaction was instantaneous. Without even turning her head, she slashed her hand backward. A beam of terrifying Sword Qi, backed by the crushing pressure of a Nascent Soul cultivator, shot straight toward the source of the voice.
It was a silencing strike. Lethal. Absolute.
DING!!
A crisp, resonant chime echoed through the room.

The fragile green light screen that had covered Lin Xuanwei was gone, replaced by a solid, impenetrable golden barrier. Elder Chen’s lethal strike slammed into the surface, rippling like a pebble in a pond before dissipating into nothingness.
Under the horrified gazes of the group, Lin Xuanwei stood up steadily.

The bloodstains on his robes were still glaring, but his posture was straight, his presence dominating. His eyes were deep, unfathomable pools of cold indifference. There was no trace of the cowardly, spoiled young master they had mocked.

“Who... who exactly are you?” Elder Chen’s voice carried a barely perceptible tremor. She stared at him, a storm of shock raging in her heart. Her full-power strike hadn’t even scratched his protective light.
Lin Xuanwei casually brushed a speck of dust from his sleeve. “As you can see, I am merely a disciple here for the trial.”
The moment the words fell, he moved.
There was no earth-shattering explosion of Qi, no flashy technique. He simply raised his hand and flicked his fingers.
Thud. Thud. Thud.
Three invisible bursts of force pierced the air like teleporting needles.

Ouyang Chen, Ma Kun, and Zheng Tong didn’t even have time to scream. Their bodies jolted violently, eyes bulging in supreme terror. Their Dantians shattered instantly, their Golden Cores pulverized into dust.
They collapsed like puppets with their strings cut, dead before they hit the ground.
Only the two women, Lu Shu and Lu Yao, were spared. They stood frozen, blood draining from their faces, trembling so violently they could barely stand.
“You dare kill Inner Disciples of the Guiyuan Sect?!” Elder Chen shrieked, her voice shrill with panic and rage.
Lin Xuanwei looked at her with eyes devoid of humanity, as if observing a corpse. “They were killed by the [Hatred] entity. What does that have to do with me?”
Before the sentence finished, his wrist flicked. A simple horizontal slash.

It looked unadorned, almost slow. Yet, in Elder Chen’s eyes, the shadow of death eclipsed the world. She roared, unleashing the full might of her Second Layer Nascent Soul cultivation. Her life-bound Dharma Treasure, a radiant longsword, erupted with blinding light as she blocked with everything she had.
CLANG.
It sounded like a blade slicing through parchment.
The Dharma Treasure that had accompanied Elder Chen for centuries snapped in half effortlessly.
Lin Xuanwei’s sword momentum didn’t even pause. It shore through her protective spiritual aura like hot knives through butter.
Blood sprayed in a fountain!
Elder Chen felt a sudden chill at her waist, followed by an agonizing, world-shattering pain. She looked down, her eyes widening in horror, to see her lower body separating from her torso.
She had been bisected.
“No... impossible...” Elder Chen gasped, her vision fading. “I am a Nascent Soul... how can a Golden Core ant...”
Lin Xuanwei remained expressionless. He stepped forward, reached out his left hand, and pressed his palm directly against her forehead.
A tyrannical surge of Divine Sense crashed into her mind.
Soul Searching!
“AHHH!!” Elder Chen let out a curdling scream as her very soul was flayed open.

However, just as Lin Xuanwei’s consciousness was about to breach her core memories, a complex golden talisman deep within her Sea of Consciousness flared to life. A powerful backlash erupted, forcefully repelling his intrusion.
“Hmm?” Lin Xuanwei frowned, withdrawing his hand as he sensed the resistance. “A soul protection mechanism? The Guiyuan Sect has some tricks after all.”

chapters.title: Chapter 192 I Know Many Techniques
paragraphs: Only now did Elder Chen realize, far too late, just what Lin Xuanwei intended to do.
Immense, suffocating terror shattered her mental defenses.
“No! Don’t Soul Search me! Spare me, I beg you!” she shrieked, her voice cracking. “What do you want to know? I can tell you! I’ll tell you everything!”
Lin Xuanwei’s gaze remained glacial. He looked down at Elder Chen’s face—twisted into a mask of excruciating pain and abject fear—as if he were a god looking down at a frantic ant.
Slowly, deliberately, he raised his right hand.
His index finger extended, the tip gently tapping against the center of Elder Chen’s forehead.
“Unnecessary.”
A faint, almost inaudible pop echoed in the silence.
The light in Elder Chen’s eyes was instantly snuffed out. The terror, the pleading, the agony—it all froze on her face as her life force was severed.
She slumped to the floor, a lifeless husk.
A deathly silence descended upon the quiet room, heavy and oppressive. The thick, metallic scent of blood began to permeate the air.
Lin Xuanwei turned around. His indifferent gaze fell upon the two sisters, Lu Shu and Lu Yao.
Feeling the weight of his attention, both women stiffened simultaneously, trembling uncontrollably.
He walked over to Lu Shu first. His voice was flat, devoid of any fluctuation. “I could kill you. But I won’t.”

Lu Shu’s body shuddered. She raised her head, her eyes swimming with a mixture of terror and gratitude. She knew the truth—it was that one insignificant shred of goodwill she had shown him earlier that had saved her life.
Had she not spoken up for him then, she would be a cold corpse on the floor right now.
“However, as you can see,” Lin Xuanwei continued, “the Guiyuan Sect is no longer a place you can stay. I will allow you to leave. Go wherever you wish.”
A flicker of hope sparked in Lu Shu’s eyes, but it dimmed just as quickly.
“I... I can’t leave the Guiyuan Sect,” she whispered bitterly. “I have... on my body...”
“I know,” Lin Xuanwei interrupted. “Your master is Hu Yanqing. And you and your sister are his Cultivation Furnaces.”
He looked at her calmly. “I can remove the [Devouring Origin Curse] he planted in you.”
“What?”
Lu Shu and Lu Yao cried out in unison. A light of pure disbelief exploded in their eyes.
“Really?” Lu Shu’s voice trembled violently.
Lin Xuanwei nodded.
“Good!” Lu Shu’s eyes filled with sudden, desperate resolve. “As long as you can remove this curse mark, I will leave the Guiyuan Sect immediately. I will never return!”
Lin Xuanwei’s gaze shifted to the side, landing on Lu Yao.
Meeting those cold, dead eyes, Lu Yao shuddered. She desperately forced a cute, pitiable smile onto her face, her voice dripping with a sickening mix of flattery and fear.
“B-Brother Xuanwei... actually, I wanted to save you earlier too! Really! It’s just... Ouyang Chen and Elder Chen were too powerful. I... I couldn’t do anything! I was forced!”
Lin Xuanwei’s eyes held no warmth. “The only reason you are still breathing is out of consideration for your sister.”
Lu Yao felt her scalp tingle under his stare. Panic rose in her throat. She hurriedly stammered, “I... I can also leave the Guiyuan Sect! I’ll go with my sister! I promise—”
“No. It’s not that simple.”
Lin Xuanwei flipped his palm.
A pitch-black pill appeared in his hand. On its surface, countless tiny black runes writhed and twisted like living worms.
“Eat it.”
He extended the pill toward Lu Yao, his tone brooking no argument. “I want you to return to the Guiyuan Sect. You will do some things for me.”

Lu Yao stared at the black pill. It emitted an eerie, ominous aura. Her throat bobbed involuntarily as she swallowed hard. She thought of her master, Hu Yanqing, and his twisted, perverse methods. Her body began to shake.

“Brother Xuanwei... I... I can serve you...” She tried to struggle, her voice turning tearful and seductive. “I know many techniques... really... If I go back, Master will definitely suspect something! He’ll kill me!”
Lin Xuanwei’s expression remained stone. “Swallow it, or die right now.”

Lu Yao looked into his utterly emotionless eyes, then glanced at the cooling corpses of Elder Chen and the others scattered across the floor. She had no doubt—if she hesitated for even a second longer, she would follow in their footsteps.
Trembling, she reached out. Her fingertips were icy cold.
It took all her strength just to pick up the black pill. As soon as it touched her skin, a bone-piercing chill shot up her arm.
She squeezed her eyes shut and shoved the pill into her mouth.
The pill dissolved instantly.
It didn’t feel like medicine; it felt like swallowing a mouthful of liquid nitrogen. It transformed into thousands of icy needles, surging through her meridians and burrowing into her bones.
Intense, screaming agony swept through her entire body in a heartbeat.
“Ahhh!!!”
Lu Yao let out a shrill, blood-curdling scream. She curled up on the ground, her body convulsing violently. Cold sweat instantly soaked through her robes.
Beside her, Lu Shu couldn’t bear it. “Senior, my sister, she...”
“Don’t worry, she won’t die,” Lin Xuanwei said indifferently. “As long as she does her job well, I will grant her freedom.”
It took a long time for the agony to recede like a tide.
Lu Yao lay limp on the floor, gasping for breath, her face as pale as paper. The look she gave Lin Xuanwei was now filled with bone-deep terror.
Only then did Lin Xuanwei reveal a faint smile. “Good. You’ve completed the first step.”
He crouched down, leaning close to Lu Yao’s ear. His voice was low, commanding, and dangerous.
“Next, do exactly as I say...”
He whispered a few instructions. As Lu Yao listened, her body couldn’t stop trembling.
After delivering his orders, Lin Xuanwei stood up. He paused, as if remembering something trivial.
“Oh, right. You can try asking your master for help, or find someone else to detoxify it.”
He looked down into Lu Yao’s terrified eyes. “However, I suggest you consider the consequences privately before you try anything stupid.”
The two women left, utterly dispirited.
Only when they were gone did the icy mask on Lin Xuanwei’s face fade, replaced by a deep, profound calm. He walked over to Elder Chen’s still-warm corpse.
“Bind.”
He lightly spat a single word.
An extremely faint wisp of spiritual consciousness was forcibly extracted from the corpse, swirling into his hand before being sealed inside a jade vial.
“This way, her Soul Lamp won’t extinguish for a while.”
He needed Elder Chen’s status to appear normal to avoid alerting the Guiyuan Sect’s higher-ups too early.
Next, he flicked his finger.
A spark of spiritual fire landed on the corpse. It burned silently, without smoke or smell. Within moments, the body was reduced to nothingness, not even a trace of ash remaining.
After handling everything, Lin Xuanwei finally let out a sigh of relief.
He wiped his hand over his face. The disguise melted away, revealing a handsome, steady visage.
It was Zhang Xian.

Six months ago, his System had successfully upgraded. Zhang Xian had immediately ‘gifted’ a massive wave of resources, triggering a windfall of returns. He had obtained so many Top Grade Spirit Treasures and Heaven Grade Techniques that his hands practically went soft from counting them.
However, his cultivation base remained at the peak of the Golden Core realm.
While the System’s upgrade removed the restriction on using high-level items, his own limitations meant he couldn’t fully unleash the potential of Top Grade artifacts yet.
But even so, facing Elder Chen—a cultivator at the second level of the Nascent Soul stage—he could still insta-kill her.
Money really was the greatest superpower.
Six months ago, Zhang Xian had piloted his upgraded flying vessel, spending a full three months to reach the Central Continent headquarters of the Heavenly Abyss Alliance.
Upon arrival, he found Xia Chengyan on the verge of death. Without hesitation, Zhang Xian had pulled out a [Primordial Creation Pill], dragging the prince back from the gates of hell.

during that time, Zhang Xian had gained a comprehensive understanding of the situation in the Central Continent and the wider cultivation world, both from Xia Chengyan and the Alliance’s intelligence network.
The world was divided into five regions: the Central Continent, the Eastern Sea, the Southern Region, the Western Region, and the Northern Ridge.
The Central Continent was the strongest, possessing the deepest foundations—the true heart of the cultivation world. The other four regions were roughly equal in strength.
However, the Western Region had already fallen.
[Hatred].

It spread like a plague. In just a few short years, it had swept through the entire Western Region. Countless cultivators were infected, their minds erased, turning them into maddened demons that knew only slaughter.
The flames of war had already reached the western borders of the Central Continent.
The Heavenly Abyss Alliance headquarters was located precisely on that frontier. They were the first line of defense, bearing the brunt of the assault and enduring immense, crushing pressure.

chapters.title: Chapter 193 Both Ends Are Dead Ends
paragraphs: The Guiyuan Sect stood as one of the two titans of the Central Continent.

Although they held long-standing grievances against the Heavenly Abyss Alliance—the two factions were like fire and water—the apocalyptic disaster of [Hatred] sweeping across the world forced their hands. They had no choice but to temporarily shelve their enmity and form a united front against the encroaching darkness.
However, the grudges ran deep.

While open warfare had ceased, the undercurrents were turbulent. Small-scale conflicts, private sabotage, and attempts to trip each other up never ceased. They simply kept it below the boiling point, careful not to completely tear off the mask of civility.
The incident where Xia Chengyan was critically injured was a vicious escalation of this shadow war.
Yang Poxiao had attacked brazenly, nearly crippling the Prince of Great Xia. This event had shaken the entire Central Continent.

On the surface, the Guiyuan Sect flatly denied any involvement. They insisted it was the work of [Hatred] infected cultivators, shirking all responsibility with practiced ease. The two superpowers engaged in a furious war of words, but ultimately, with the greater threat looming, the matter was left unresolved.
Recalling that battle, a lingering fear still gripped Xia Chengyan.
He had always prided himself on his supreme talent. But in front of Yang Poxiao, a cultivator of the same realm, he had been utterly powerless.
Strength, speed, reaction time, and even the mastery of Daoist Techniques—Yang Poxiao surpassed him in every single metric by a full tier.
If the Divination Grandmaster Lin Xiaozhu hadn’t arrived in the nick of time, Xia Chengyan would have perished on the spot.
Zhang Xian understood this gap perfectly.
He knew that Yang Poxiao had been taken in as a personal disciple by the Guiyuan Sect’s legendary Supreme Elder, Grandmaster Taichu.
Grandmaster Taichu. A half-step Soul Formation entity. An existence hailed as invincible in the current cultivation world.

Yang Poxiao had triggered the genuine [High-Level Disciple Halo]. With the terrifying backing of such a master and the massive surge of Providence that followed, his cultivation progress was bound to skyrocket like a rocket. His strength was already leagues above his peers.

After nearly killing Xia Chengyan, Yang Poxiao had caused a massive uproar. To avoid suspicion—and likely to consolidate his gains—he withdrew from the Western Region battlefield. He returned to the core restricted area of the Guiyuan Sect for secluded cultivation.
And he, Yang Poxiao, was the ultimate target of Zhang Xian’s trip to the Central Continent.
Zhang Xian intended to strangle this future calamity in the cradle before he could fully mature.

To achieve this, Zhang Xian had infiltrated the Guiyuan Mountain Range. This area was the sect’s doorstep, but it was also a place where dragons and snakes mingled, making it perfect for hiding one’s identity and gathering intel.
While maintaining his cultivation, he secretly collected intelligence on the sect’s core defenses, Yang Poxiao’s specific location, and the various secret realms within the mountains.
When he accidentally discovered Ouyang Chen’s team preparing to explore the Longwu Cave Mansion—and noting they were short a “scapegoat” to test for traps—a plan instantly formed in his mind.
He donned the “vest” of the “Son of the Richest Man in Jinyuan City,” assumed the alias Lin Xuanwei, and easily bought his way into the team.
His original intention was merely to secure a low-key identity as a Guiyuan Sect disciple to probe deeper into the sect.
However, he had intercepted Ouyang Chen’s secret voice transmissions. They were planning a “black-eating-black” scenario—betrayal and murder for profit.
Zhang Xian had sneered inwardly.
Coincidentally, he had collected a faint, withered remnant of [Hatred] at the edge of the Western Region. It came in handy perfectly.
Using this remnant, he meticulously directed the horror show in the quiet room, thoroughly muddying the waters and framing the chaos on the disaster.
He had originally held a sliver of hope for the Guiyuan Sect. He thought that perhaps, as a self-proclaimed Righteous Sect, they might possess a baseline of morality in critical moments.
But Elder Chen’s appearance and actions shattered that final illusion.

This Enforcement Hall Elder spouted high-sounding, righteous rhetoric, yet she wouldn’t even part with a single [Meridian Restoration Pill] to save a dying disciple. Instead, she greedily snatched away his Storage Bag.
Greedy. Hypocritical. Cold-blooded.
This was the true face of the Guiyuan Sect’s higher-ups.
Since that was the case, Zhang Xian didn’t mind repaying them in kind. He was going to play a very big game right in the heart of their territory.
A temporary stronghold at the foot of the Guiyuan Mountain Range.
Inside a deathly silent room.

Lu Yao, looking utterly soul-lost, pushed open the door and slumped weakly against the cold wood. Cold sweat had soaked through her back robes, and her heart was still hammering against her ribs like a trapped bird.
The bloody scenes from the quiet room played on a loop in her mind.
The gruesome sight of Elder Chen being bisected at the waist. The horror of Ouyang Chen and the others dying instantly as their Dantians shattered.
And those eyes. “Lin Xuanwei’s” icy, emotionless eyes.
Subconsciously, she touched her lower abdomen. The phantom pain of the soul-rending agony she felt when the ice needle entered her body still lingered there.
Two sinister forces were now coiled within her like venomous snakes.
On one side was the [Devouring Origin Curse] planted by her master, Hu Yanqing. It clung to her bones like a maggot, controlling her life and death.
On the other side was the [Ice Needle Poison] from “Lin Xuanwei,” a torture that promised even greater agony.
Caught between two masters. Both ends were dead ends.
Lu Yao couldn’t hold it back any longer. She let out a choked sob, suppressed to the extreme.

She slid down the door to sit on the floor, hugging her knees tightly. She buried her face in her arms, her body trembling violently. Fear, despair, resentment, hatred—a tidal wave of negative emotions drowned her.
Buzz. Buzz.
Suddenly, the communication jade talisman at her waist vibrated intensely.
Lu Yao froze.
With trembling hands, almost terrified to touch it, she picked up the jade talisman. She sent a wisp of Divine Sense inside.
A line of icy, piercing words floated into her Sea of Consciousness:
[How did Lu Shu’s Soul Lamp go out? What happened?]
It was a message from her master, Hu Yanqing.
An indescribable surge of bitterness and acid jealousy instantly flooded her heart.
She remembered that seemingly casual gesture from “Lin Xuanwei” before they left the quiet room.

He had used some unknown secret technique. He hadn’t just removed the [Devouring Origin Curse] that had tormented them for hundreds of years—he had used an extremely sophisticated method to completely erase Lu Shu’s aura from the world.
Lu Shu’s Soul Lamp within the Sect had extinguished.
From that moment on, Lu Shu was truly free. She had escaped the Guiyuan Sect. She had escaped Hu Yanqing’s demonic clutches.
But what about her?
What about Lu Yao?

Not only was she still trapped, but she now carried the terrifying [Ice Needle Poison] in her veins. She had to return to the Guiyuan Sect alone and face a master who was more terrifying than a devil.
Why?
Why could her sister be freed, while she had to bear all this?
Intense grievance and twisted resentment made her want to scream. But soon, a deeper, primal fear crushed her anger.
She clutched the jade talisman, her knuckles turning white from the force. A violent struggle raged in her mind.
Two paths lay before her.

The first: Confess everything to her master. Tell him how Elder Chen and Ouyang Chen died. Reveal “Lin Xuanwei’s” entire plan. Her master was a grand Nascent Soul cultivator; surely, he would have a way to remove this damned poison?

The second: Submit to “Lin Xuanwei.” He could kill Elder Chen with a single finger and easily dissolve the [Devouring Origin Curse]. Perhaps his cultivation base was far above her master’s? Moreover, Senior “Lin Xuanwei” had promised freedom and resources if she completed his task.
But siding with “Lin Xuanwei” meant standing against the entire Guiyuan Sect. The number one sect in the cultivation world...
Lu Yao made her choice.
Trembling, she channeled her spiritual energy into the jade talisman, preparing to carve a message of betrayal.
I have to tell Master...
“AHHH!!!”
The very instant the intent to confess formed in her mind, a terrifying pain—ten times, a hundred times more intense than before—erupted from the depths of her soul without warning.

It clung to her bones like a maggot, controlling her life and death.
On the other side was the [Ice Needle Poison] from “Lin Xuanwei,” a torture that promised even greater agony.
Caught between two masters.
Both ends were dead ends.
Lu Yao couldn’t hold it back any longer.
She let out a choked sob, suppressed to the extreme.
She slid down the door to sit on the floor, hugging her knees tightly.
She buried her face in her arms, her body trembling violently.
Fear, despair, resentment, hatred—a tidal wave of negative emotions drowned her.
Buzz.
Buzz.
Suddenly, the communication jade talisman at her waist vibrated intensely.
Lu Yao froze.
With trembling hands, almost terrified to touch it, she picked up the jade talisman.
She sent a wisp of Divine Sense inside.
A line of icy, piercing words floated into her Sea of Consciousness:
[How did Lu Shu’s Soul Lamp go out?
What happened?]
It was a message from her master, Hu Yanqing.
An indescribable surge of bitterness and acid jealousy instantly flooded her heart.
She remembered that seemingly casual gesture from “Lin Xuanwei” before they left the quiet room.
He had used some unknown secret technique.
He hadn’t just removed the [Devouring Origin Curse] that had tormented them for hundreds of years—he had used an extremely sophisticated method to completely erase Lu Shu’s aura from the world.
Lu Shu’s Soul Lamp within the Sect had extinguished.
From that moment on, Lu Shu was truly free.
She had escaped the Guiyuan Sect.
She had escaped Hu Yanqing’s demonic clutches.
But what about her?
What about Lu Yao?
Not only was she still trapped, but she now carried the terrifying [Ice Needle Poison] in her veins.
She had to return to the Guiyuan Sect alone and face a master who was more terrifying than a devil.
Why?
Why could her sister be freed, while she had to bear all this?
Intense grievance and twisted resentment made her want to scream.
But soon, a deeper, primal fear crushed her anger.
She clutched the jade talisman, her knuckles turning white from the force.
A violent struggle raged in her mind.
Two paths lay before her.
The first: Confess everything to her master.
Tell him how Elder Chen and Ouyang Chen died.
Reveal “Lin Xuanwei’s” entire plan.
Her master was a grand Nascent Soul cultivator; surely, he would have a way to remove this damned poison?
The second: Submit to “Lin Xuanwei.” He could kill Elder Chen with a single finger and easily dissolve the [Devouring Origin Curse].
Perhaps his cultivation base was far above her master’s?
Moreover, Senior “Lin Xuanwei” had promised freedom and resources if she completed his task.
But siding with “Lin Xuanwei” meant standing against the entire Guiyuan Sect.
The number one sect in the cultivation world...
Lu Yao made her choice.
Trembling, she channeled her spiritual energy into the jade talisman, preparing to carve a message of betrayal.
I have to tell Master...
“AHHH!!!”
The very instant the intent to confess formed in her mind, a terrifying pain—ten times, a hundred times more intense than before—erupted from the depths of her soul without warning.

chapters.title: Chapter 194 The Performance of a Lifetime
paragraphs: This time, the pain was different.

It felt as if billions of burning ice needles were savagely piercing every inch of her flesh, burrowing into every single thought that flickered through her mind. The agony surpassed the limits of the physical body, drilling directly into the origin of her soul, threatening to tear her very consciousness into shreds.
Thud!
Lu Yao collapsed heavily to the ground. She clutched her head with both hands, her fingers digging into her scalp, and let out a shrill, inhuman scream.
“No! No! Senior Lin, I was wrong! I won’t do it again! Spare me! Please, spare me!”
Mucus and tears streamed down her face as she wailed incoherently, her voice cracking with absolute, primal terror.
In that moment of soul-rending torture, she finally understood what “Lin Xuanwei” had meant by “consider the consequences carefully in private.”
This [Ice Needle Poison] wasn’t meant to control her body. It was a shackle for her soul.
Even the slightest thought of betrayal or resistance would trigger this ultimate punishment.
However, her wails were destined to go unanswered in the empty room. Only the soul-flaying torment washed over her, wave after crashing wave.
She didn’t know how long it lasted before the terrifying agony finally, slowly receded.
Lu Yao lay sprawled on the cold floor like a fish thrown onto dry land, gasping for air in great, heaving gulps. Her eyes were vacant, stripped of all light.
trembling violently, she reached out and picked up the communication jade talisman.
Her fingers shook as she carved her message:

[Reporting to Master: Your disciple encountered a remnant of “Hatred” while exploring the cave dwelling. The situation was extremely perilous. Elder Chen attempted to suppress it but was unfortunately corrupted by the “Hatred.” When your disciple awoke, Elder Chen and the other fellow disciples had all disappeared without a trace.]
Send.
The jade talisman slipped from her sweaty grip and clattered to the floor.

Lu Yao’s body trembled uncontrollably. She knew that the moment this message was sent, there was no turning back. Betraying the Sect, deceiving her Master—either crime was enough to condemn her to eternal damnation without hope of reprieve.
But now, she had no choice.
Not long after, the jade talisman vibrated again. The response contained only two cold words:
[Come back.]
Staring at those two characters, Lu Yao felt a chill surge from the soles of her feet straight to the crown of her head.
The image of Hu Yanqing instantly rose in her mind—that face which seemed so gentle and refined on the surface, yet hid a cruel, tyrannical monster beneath.

She remembered the nights tormented by the [Devouring Origin Curse], a fate worse than death. She remembered the pain of being used as a Cultivation Furnace, feeling her hard-earned cultivation being drained away drop by drop. She remembered his perverse, sadistic punishments.
She felt as if she had been plunged into an ice cellar.
Her scalp went numb, and her blood ran cold. But she had to go back. She had to brace herself and walk into the lion’s den.
Her only hope now was that the mysterious and terrifying “Lin Xuanwei” truly possessed superior means and would honor his promise.
Golden Zen Palace, Entrance of the Palace Master’s Hall.
The Guiyuan Sect was divided into thirty-six Palaces, each overseen by a Nascent Soul Grandmaster. Lu Yao and her sister Lu Shu belonged to the Golden Zen Palace, and Hu Yanqing was its Master.
Half a day later, Lu Yao forcibly suppressed the terror clawing at her heart and returned to the Golden Zen Palace. It felt like marching to her own execution.
She knelt before the cold, solemn doors of the main hall, her head bowed low, her body shivering despite her best efforts to control it.
Finally, the hall doors opened silently.
A young man with a refined face and an ethereal, scholarly demeanor walked out slowly.
This was Hu Yanqing—Palace Master of the Golden Zen Palace, and the Young Master of the Central Continent’s renowned Baoqing Workshop.
He walked up to Lu Yao, looking down at her from his elevated position. His voice was flat, devoid of fluctuation, yet it carried a crushing, invisible pressure.
“Speak. Why have you returned alone?”
Lu Yao’s heart pounded against her ribs like a war drum. Forcing herself to remain calm, she kept her head lowered and recited the explanation she had rehearsed a thousand times in her mind.

Her story was consistent with the message, only supplemented with more gruesome details. She described the terror of the [Hatred], the tragic state of Elder Chen as she was corrupted, and emphasized that when she woke up, the cave dwelling was empty.
“Oh?”
Hu Yanqing’s eyebrows lifted almost imperceptibly. He neither affirmed nor denied her story.
Suddenly, he leaned down. He extended two long, pale fingers and gently pinched Lu Yao’s chin, forcing her to look up at him.
Their eyes met.
Deep within Hu Yanqing’s seemingly gentle pupils, a sharp, piercing cold light flickered—a gaze that seemed capable of dissecting the human heart.
“My obedient disciple,” his voice remained soft, yet a razor-thin chill laced the edges, “you wouldn’t be lying to this Master, would you?”
Lu Yao’s pupils contracted to pinpricks. She felt her blood freeze in her veins.
Almost instinctively, she let out a shrill cry. “Your disciple wouldn’t dare! Every word is true! Master, please see clearly!”
A faint, almost mocking curve lifted the corner of Hu Yanqing’s mouth. The fingers gripping her chin exerted a slight pressure.
The [Devouring Origin Curse] activated.
“Argh!”
Lu Yao let out a wretched scream. She braced herself for the familiar agony, the sensation of ten thousand ants gnawing at her bone marrow.
However—
It hurt. It truly hurt.
But... it was only about one-tenth of the usual intensity.
Lu Yao realized it instantly—it was the [Ice Needle Poison]!
The poison planted by Senior “Lin Xuanwei” didn’t just punish rebellious thoughts; it actually suppressed the [Devouring Origin Curse]!
But she dared not show the slightest hint of relief.
Immediately, she delivered the performance of her lifetime.

She bit down hard on her lower lip until her gums burst, blood trickling from the corner of her mouth. Letting out heart-rending screams that echoed through the courtyard, she desperately kowtowed, smashing her forehead against the cold jade tiles again and again.
Thud! Thud!
“Master! Your disciple truly did not deceive you! I beg you! Please stop! Your disciple can’t take it anymore! Master!!”
Her cries were shrill, desperate, and filled with utter despair. It was a flawless performance.
Hu Yanqing watched her wail and beg for mercy with indifferent eyes. His face remained expressionless, as if he were watching a boring play.
Slowly, he stood up, turned his back, and walked toward the hall.
He left only one cold sentence hanging in the air: “Think it over clearly, then speak to this Master.”
The heavy doors groaned and slowly closed, shutting Lu Yao outside.
Lu Yao’s forehead was already split open, fresh blood staining the pristine white jade. But as the doors sealed shut, her heart sank into an icy abyss.
Time passed. Minute by minute. Second by second.
Lu Yao kept acting until she felt numb. Her voice grew hoarse from screaming. Just when she thought he really intended to torture her to death, the hall doors opened silently once more.
Hu Yanqing reappeared.
He flicked a finger, and the [Devouring Origin Curse] roiling within Lu Yao instantly calmed.
“Alright.”
Hu Yanqing’s voice was gentle once more. He stepped forward, reached out, and tenderly wiped the blood and dust from Lu Yao’s forehead. He even patted the dirt from her robes like a caring father.
“Just now, the Sect received news. Traces of Elder Chen, corrupted by [Hatred], have been discovered in a nearby city. The Sect has already dispatched Enforcers to capture her.”
He paused, looking deep into Lu Yao’s terrified eyes. His tone shifted to one of earnest, heavy-hearted admonishment.

“Now that Lu Shu is gone, this Master can only be stricter with you. Although the [Devouring Origin Curse] is painful, it tempers your mind and spirit. You must not resent your Master’s methods. When you achieve the Nascent Soul realm in the future, this curse will naturally dissipate.”
“Your disciple wouldn’t dare...” Lu Yao rasped, her voice ruined. She kept her head bowed, her body trembling, but her heart was filled with nothing but cold, venomous mockery.
“Mn.” Hu Yanqing nodded, seemingly satisfied with her broken demeanor.
At that moment, as if remembering something, Lu Yao struggled to retrieve a weathered, ancient-looking jade slip from her robes.
She held it up respectfully with both hands.

“Master, this is something your disciple obtained by chance in an abandoned cave dwelling before. It seems to be related to... Cultivation Furnace techniques. Your disciple is dull-witted and cannot understand it. I offer it specially to you, Master.”

chapters.title: Chapter 195 This Hairstyle Is Very Popular
paragraphs: A flicker of surprise passed through Hu Yanqing’s eyes as he casually took the jade slip.
He hadn’t held much hope. After all, what true treasures could possibly be found in a long-abandoned cave dwelling?
However, the moment his Divine Sense probed the jade slip, his eyes erupted with a brilliance he couldn’t conceal.
Recorded within was a fragment of a High Grade Cultivation Furnace Technique.

Although the annotations were missing and the text was riddled with omissions, the profound concepts and exquisite methodologies contained within were leagues above the technique he currently practiced.
If he could comprehend even a fraction of it and integrate it into his own cultivation method, the benefits would be immeasurable. He might even glimpse the threshold of the Soul Formation realm.
“Where did you obtain this?” Hu Yanqing’s voice carried a trace of urgency that was difficult to mask.
“It was discovered by chance in a stone crevice while exploring Luoxia Valley half a year ago,” Lu Yao lied smoothly, fabricating a location without blinking.
“Good! Good! Good!”
Hu Yanqing uttered the word three times in succession, a rare, genuine smile breaking across his face. He reached out and, with unusual tenderness, patted the top of Lu Yao’s head.
“Not bad. You are truly worthy of being my good Yao’er! You have shown great filial piety!”
As he spoke, he retrieved two exquisite jade bottles from his sleeve and handed them to her. “These are some healing and foundation-nourishing Spirit Pills. Take them and recuperate well.”
“Thank you, Master!” Lu Yao quickly knelt and prostrated on the floor, her voice trembling with feigned gratitude.
Late at night. Lu Yao’s residence.
Lu Yao collapsed onto her cold bed, her limbs heavy. The hurdle of Master Hu Yanqing had finally been passed, though it had been a walk on a tightrope over a cliff.

Just as the Senior had predicted, the fragmented Cultivation Furnace technique successfully ensnared Hu Yanqing’s attention. Upon obtaining the jade slip, he had hastily announced that he would enter Secluded Cultivation to comprehend it. For the near future, he wouldn’t have the time to find trouble with her.
Her gaze swept over the two jade bottles Hu Yanqing had bestowed.
The corner of her mouth lifted in a bitter, mocking arc.

She casually picked up one of the bottles and popped the stopper. A faint medicinal fragrance wafted out. Inside were a few healing pills and Spirit Pills for consolidating the foundation—quality: average. Under normal circumstances, for a Golden Core cultivator like her, these would be considered a decent reward.
But when she sent her Divine Sense into her own Storage Bag, that mockery instantly transformed into an indescribably complex emotion.
Inside the bag, Spirit Stones were piled up like a mountain, emitting a blindingly rich Spiritual Qi.
Dazzling arrays of rare Spirit Grasses and exotic materials filled the space, many of which were so high-grade she couldn’t even name them.
These were merely the “advance payment” the Senior had given her.

Compared to the wealth within this Storage Bag—fortune enough to make even a Nascent Soul Grandmaster’s eyes turn red with envy—the two bottles of pills Hu Yanqing had bestowed were as worthless as roadside pebbles.
The immense contrast left Lu Yao’s heart in turmoil.
On one side was her Master: stingy, cruel, and viewing her as nothing more than a disposable tool.
On the other was “Lin Xuanwei”: mysterious, powerful, extravagantly generous, yet possessing methods more ruthless than a demon.
After a long silence, she took a deep breath.
She picked up the communication jade talisman that symbolized her status as an Inner Disciple of the Golden Zen Palace. Spiritual light flickered at her fingertip as she inscribed a message:
[The Golden Zen Palace requires several Outer Disciples to assist with miscellaneous tasks. Immediately submit the roster of all Outer Disciples from this session.]
Send.
Lu Yao clutched the jade talisman, her gaze complex as she stared out the window at the pitch-black night sky.
She knew the task assigned by the Senior had begun. She had already stepped onto a path of no return.
Half a month later. Golden Zen Palace, Mountain Gate Plaza.
The Golden Zen Palace threw its gates wide, commencing the grand recruitment of Outer Disciples.
The plaza was a cauldron of noise and excitement. Hundreds of young cultivators gathered here, their faces written with a mix of nervous tension and burning anticipation.
Presiding over this recruitment ceremony were Song Zhang—the Second Disciple under Palace Master Hu Yanqing—and Junior Sister Lu Yao.

Song Zhang wore the standard black-and-white Daoist robes of the Guiyuan Sect. His posture was ramrod straight, and his features were average at best. However, his long hair was deliberately parted down the exact center of his skull, hanging down his temples in an affectation of casual elegance that only succeeded in giving him a greasy, try-hard appearance.
This hairstyle was currently very popular within the Guiyuan Sect.
Its origin, naturally, traced back to the man hailed as invincible in the cultivation world: Grandmaster Taichu.

The massive jade statue of Grandmaster Taichu atop the sect’s highest peak bore this very same visage, complete with the center-parted long hair. This had led countless disciples to emulate the look, hoping to capture even a fraction of his majesty. Both Song Zhang and the deceased Ouyang Chen were devotees of this style.
Lu Yao stood slightly behind Song Zhang.
Today, she had changed into an elegant, understated dress and applied light makeup, though it couldn’t completely conceal the trace of weariness and fragility lingering between her brows.
After several rounds of rigorous screening, dozens of lucky individuals finally stood out, obtaining the qualification to become Registered Disciples of the Golden Zen Palace.
Most were at the early Golden Core stage. Among them were two cultivators possessing mutated High Grade Spiritual Roots—talents that were truly outstanding.

In any lesser sect, such geniuses would be fought over by elders and groomed as Core Inheritors. But within the deep foundations of the Guiyuan Sect, they could only start as Inner Registered Disciples, facing numerous trials before they could hope to become Personal Disciples.
Song Zhang looked at the vibrant group of new Juniors before him and nodded with satisfaction.
However, as his gaze swept over the crowd, his brows involuntarily furrowed.
One figure stood out like a sore thumb.

It was a slightly plump young man wearing a gaudy brocade robe embroidered with gold thread, contrasting starkly with the simple attire of the other cultivators. His face was ordinary, perhaps even a bit simple and honest. His cultivation was merely at the first level of the Golden Core, and his aptitude was an unremarkable Middle Grade Fire Spiritual Root.
Yu Yun.

The name immediately surfaced in Song Zhang’s mind. He remembered it clearly because this person had been specifically named and inserted into the list by Junior Sister Lu Yao—a blatant “backdoor” connection.

Song Zhang came from a humble background. He had climbed to his current position entirely through his own blood, sweat, and a bit of luck. What he despised most were these pampered young masters who relied on family background to reap rewards without labor.
A natural, instinctive hostility surged in his heart.
He opened his mouth, ready to find a pretext to publicly reprimand this Yu Yun, or simply find an excuse to fail him on the spot.
Right at that moment, Lu Yao stepped forward.
Her clear voice rang out, carrying a trace of indisputable firmness.

“Second Senior Brother, this Junior Sister’s cultivation is still shallow, and I fear I am incapable of instructing too many disciples. These three...” She extended a slender, pale finger, accurately pointing toward three people in the crowd—including the chubby Yu Yun. “...shall be taught by me on behalf of the Master.”
The three who were selected, Yu Yun included, barely suppressed their joy.

The other disciples cast looks of envy and jealousy. Being accepted under this beautiful Junior Sister’s tutelage was infinitely preferable to following the stern-faced, greasy-haired Second Senior Brother.
Especially that center-parted hair... gleaming with oil under the sunlight, paired with his pretentiously profound expression... it was truly an assault on the eyes.
The three hurriedly bowed and quickly walked to stand behind Lu Yao, terrified she might change her mind.
Only then did Lu Yao turn to Song Zhang, a perfectly apologetic smile gracing her lips.
“Second Senior Brother, I will only accept these three. The remaining disciples will require you to expend more effort. Is that alright?”
Song Zhang looked at Lu Yao’s lovely face, so close to his own. He saw the weariness in her eyes, the fragility in her posture.
The annoyance in his heart instantly evaporated, replaced by a surge of pity and a masculine desire to protect.
The corner of his mouth lifted into what he believed to be a dashing, elegant smile. His voice turned gentle, almost sickly sweet.
“No problem, no problem at all. Junior Sister, rest assured. Leave the rest to me—this Senior Brother will teach them with the utmost dedication.”
